Take Snapshot: The dialog that opens from the **Snapshot** button. Type a name in the `Snapshot name` field and confirm to pin a named restore point into the history list. The name is saved with a 📌 pin marker so snapshots stand out among ordinary steps.
Restore Version: A confirmation box shown when you click **Restore** on a saved version. It warns `Restore version vN? The current file becomes a new version and the editor reloads.` Confirm with the **Restore** button to load that version; the whole editor reloads afterward.
Version date and size: Under each saved version's `vN` name is a second line showing when it was saved (your local date and time) and its file size in kilobytes. Use it to tell versions apart before restoring.

sections.title: Actions panel dialogs and status text
sections.text:
The naming dialogs behind Stop & Save and Save Look, plus the list markers and helper text.
Saving a recording or a look opens a naming dialog, and the Saved Actions list uses small icons and placeholder text to keep things clear.
Save Action: The naming dialog shown after you press **Stop & Save**. Type a name in the `Name for this action` field and confirm to store the recorded steps as a reusable action. Cancel to discard the whole recording.
Name for this look: The field in the **Save Look** dialog that appears when you save the active layer's filter and adjustments as a reusable look. It is prefilled with the layer's current filter name, or `Look` if there is none. Confirm to save the look; cancel to abort.
Look vs action marker: Each item in the **Saved Actions** list is prefixed with an icon showing its type: a 🎨 palette for a saved look (a filter plus adjustments) and a ▶ triangle for a recorded action (a sequence of steps). It is a read-only hint, not a button.
No actions yet. Record one or save a look.: The placeholder text shown in the **Saved Actions** section when you have not stored any actions or looks yet. It names the two ways to create one.
Recording… apply filters, effects, adjustments, resize/rotate/flip/flatten.: While the recorder is running but nothing has been captured yet, this hint tells you which operations get recorded. As you apply steps they replace the hint and appear as a bullet list. Pressing **Stop & Save** with nothing recorded shows a reminder to apply operations while recording.

sections.title: Right panel width behavior
sections.text:
The panel remembers its width and widens itself when content would otherwise overflow.
Panel auto-width: Beyond the manual drag handle, the right panel remembers its width and can widen itself automatically. If a tab's content (for example a long translated label) would otherwise need a horizontal scrollbar, the panel grows just enough to fit. Your chosen width is saved and restored on your next visit.

sections.title: File menu
sections.text:
The File menu opens and creates documents, saves them in every format the editor supports, and handles projects, import/export and pages.
This menu is where a document begins and ends. Use it to start a **New** design, open or place existing images, and save your work to the WordPress Media Library or as an editable design.
Several items are grouped by destination: the top save block writes finished images, the middle block saves editable designs, and the lower blocks save reusable pieces (templates, assets, patterns) or handle project files and import/export.
Some items are only active in certain situations, and are greyed out otherwise rather than disappearing. For example, `Save to Media Library` is greyed out for a brand new blank document, and `Share Design Link` becomes active once the document has been saved as a design.
New: Starts a fresh blank document. Opens the create dialog where you pick the canvas size before editing.
Open/Place: Opens an existing image or places one into the current document. Use it to bring an image in from the Media Library or your computer.
Open Recent: A submenu listing files you edited recently, each shown as its name and attachment ID. Choosing one reloads the editor with that attachment. If nothing has been opened yet, it shows a disabled `No recent files` entry.
Open Dynamic Template: Opens the template picker so you can start from a saved dynamic template. Dynamic templates carry placeholders that fill in from post or site data.
Save to Media Library: Flattens the design to a single image and saves it back into the WordPress Media Library, overwriting the source attachment. This is the standard save for an image that came from the library. [Availability: Hidden for a brand new document]
Save as New Image: Saves the flattened design as a brand new image in the Media Library instead of overwriting the original. Use it to keep the source untouched.
Export: Opens the export dialog to download the image in a chosen format and quality. Use it to get a file onto your computer rather than into the library.
Share Design Link: Creates or copies a shareable link to the current saved design. Greyed out until the document has been saved as a design and has a design ID. [Availability: Only for saved designs]
Stop Sharing: Revokes the public link of the current design. The link stops working immediately and the shared image is deleted; sharing again creates a new link. Greyed out until the document has been saved as a design. [Availability: Only for saved designs]
Save Editable Design: Saves the full editable design, keeping all layers so you can reopen and change it later. If it is already a saved design, this updates it in place.
Save Editable Design As: Saves the current design as a new, separate editable design. Greyed out until the document already is a saved design (otherwise plain Save already creates one). [Availability: Only for saved designs]
Save as Dynamic Template: Saves the current design as a dynamic template that others can reuse, with placeholders that fill from post or site data. Use it to turn a finished layout into a reusable starting point.
Save as Asset: Saves the active layer into the Asset Library as a reusable asset. Available only when a layer is selected. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Save as Pattern: Saves the current design as a repeating pattern you can fill other layers with. Use it to build your own seamless textures.
Add Page: Adds another page to the document. Use it for multi-page designs such as carousels or documents with several slides.
Project (.wpie): A submenu for working with the editor's own project file format, which stores the whole editable document as a single downloadable file.
Open Project (.wpie): Opens a `.wpie` project file from your computer, restoring the full editable document. Found under the `Project (.wpie)` submenu.
Download Project (.wpie): Downloads the current document as a `.wpie` project file to your computer. Use it to archive or move an editable design between sites.
Import / Export: A submenu for exchanging designs with other formats: SVG, Photoshop PSD, layer comps and carousels.
Import SVG: Imports an SVG vector file into the document. Found under the `Import / Export` submenu.
Export SVG: Exports the current design as an SVG vector file. Found under the `Import / Export` submenu.
Import PSD: Imports a Photoshop PSD file, bringing in its layers. Found under the `Import / Export` submenu.
Export PSD: Exports the current design as a Photoshop PSD file with its layers. Found under the `Import / Export` submenu.
Export Layer Comps: Exports the document's saved layer comps as separate images. Only enabled when the document has at least one layer comp. [Availability: Requires at least one layer comp]
Export Carousel: Opens the carousel export dialog to output a multi-slide design as a set of images. Found under the `Import / Export` submenu.
Close: Closes the editor and returns to where you came from. Use it when you are done editing.

sections.title: Edit menu
sections.text:
The Edit menu holds undo and redo, the layer clipboard (cut, copy, paste, duplicate, delete), style copy and paste, transform and selection basics, and preferences.
Use this menu for everyday editing actions. The top pair steps through your history, and the clipboard block moves whole layers around.
The style block copies just a layer's look (effects and appearance) from one layer to another. The lower block handles free transform, whole-document selection, and a link to the plugin's preferences.
Most clipboard and transform items need an active layer, and paste items need something already on the clipboard, so they grey out when they cannot run.
Undo: Reverses your most recent action. Greyed out when there is nothing to undo.
Redo: Re-applies an action you just undid. Greyed out when there is nothing to redo.
Cut Layer: Removes the selected layer(s) from the document and places them on the clipboard so you can paste them elsewhere. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Copy Layer: Copies the selected layer(s) to the clipboard without removing them. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Paste Layer: Pastes layers from the clipboard into the document. Only enabled when the clipboard holds one or more layers. [Availability: Requires layers on the clipboard]
Duplicate: Makes an exact copy of the active layer in the same document. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Delete: Without an active selection it removes the selected layer or layers from the document. With a selection active it clears the pixels inside that selection on the active pixel layer instead, leaving the layer in place. Requires an active layer either way. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Copy Styles: Copies just the active layer's styles (its appearance and effects) to a style clipboard, without copying the layer itself. Requires an active layer.
Paste Styles: Applies previously copied layer styles to the active layer. Enabled only when a layer is active and styles are on the style clipboard. [Availability: Requires an active layer and copied styles]
Free Transform: Enters free transform on the active layer so you can scale, rotate and skew it by dragging handles. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Select All: Selects the whole canvas as a selection. Use it before an action that should affect everything.
Deselect: Clears the current selection. Only enabled when a selection exists. [Availability: Requires an active selection]
Preferences: Opens the plugin's settings page in a new browser tab. Use it to change editor-wide options.

sections.title: Image menu
sections.text:
The Image menu changes the whole document: its pixel size, canvas size, colors, cropping, trimming, and rotation or flipping.
Everything here affects the entire document rather than a single layer. Use `Image Size` to change the pixel dimensions and `Canvas Size` to change the working area around the content.
The `Colors` submenu gathers background color, palette extraction, palette application and LUT loading. The lower items crop, trim and rotate or flip the whole canvas.
Image Size: Opens the resize dialog to change the document's pixel dimensions, scaling the content to fit. Use it to make the whole image larger or smaller.
Canvas Size: Opens the resize dialog in canvas mode to change the working area without scaling the content. Use it to add or remove space around your design.
Resize Design: Opens the resize tool that re-lays out the design to a new size, moving and re-fitting elements rather than simply scaling. Use it to adapt a layout to a different format.
Colors: A submenu of color utilities: background color, palette extraction and application, brand colors, and LUT loading.
Change Background Color: Sets the document's background color. Found under the `Colors` submenu.
Extract Colors from Image: Reads the dominant colors from the active layer and collects them as a palette. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Apply Palette from Image: Recolors the design using a palette derived from an image. Requires an active layer. Found under the `Colors` submenu. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Apply Brand Colors: Recolors the design using your saved brand colors. Only enabled when a brand palette with colors is available. [Availability: Requires saved brand colors]
Load LUT (.cube): Loads a `.cube` color lookup table and applies its color grade to the active layer. Requires an active layer. Found under the `Colors` submenu. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Crop to Selection: Crops the whole document down to the current selection's bounds. Only enabled when a selection exists. [Availability: Requires an active selection]
Trim: Trims away empty or uniform border areas around the document. Use it to remove excess space at the edges.
Rotate 90° CW: Rotates the entire document 90 degrees clockwise.
Rotate 90° CCW: Rotates the entire document 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
Flip Horizontal: Mirrors the entire document left to right.
Flip Vertical: Mirrors the entire document top to bottom.
Crop to Image: Crops the canvas to the bounds of the selected image layer, so the document exactly matches that picture.

sections.title: Layer menu
sections.text:
The Layer menu creates new layers of every kind, duplicates and deletes them, combines and masks them, and moves them up or down the stack.
Use this menu to build and manage the layer stack. The top block adds new layers: empty layers, groups, fill layers (solid, gradient or pattern) and texture layers.
The middle blocks copy, trim, merge and flatten layers, then convert them to smart objects, add masks and create clipping masks. The bottom pair changes stacking order.
Most items need an active layer and grey out otherwise. `Trim Transparent Pixels` only works on a raster (pixel) layer.
New Layer: Adds a new empty layer above the current one. Use it as a fresh surface to paint or place content on.
New Group: Creates a new layer group (folder) to organise layers together. Use it to keep the stack tidy and move layers as a set.
New Fill Layer: A submenu that adds a fill layer of a chosen kind: solid color, gradient or pattern.
Solid Color: Adds a fill layer filled with a single solid color. Found under `New Fill Layer`.
Gradient: Adds a fill layer filled with a gradient. Found under `New Fill Layer`.
Pattern: Adds a fill layer filled with a repeating pattern. Found under `New Fill Layer`.
New Texture Layer: A submenu that adds a procedurally generated texture layer in one of eight styles. Use these to add tactile surface detail over a design.
Grain: Adds a film-grain style texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Paper: Adds a paper-surface texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Fibers: Adds a fibrous, thread-like texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Canvas Weave: Adds a woven canvas texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Cross-hatch: Adds a cross-hatched line texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Concrete: Adds a rough concrete surface texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Color Noise: Adds a colored noise texture layer. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Scanlines: Adds a scanline texture layer for a screen or retro look. Found under `New Texture Layer`.
Duplicate: Makes an exact copy of the active layer. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Delete: Removes the selected layer(s) from the document. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Layer via Copy: Creates a new layer from a copy of the current selection's contents on the active layer. Requires an active layer. Use it to lift part of a layer onto its own new layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Trim Transparent Pixels: Shrinks the active layer's bounds to remove empty transparent areas around its pixels. Only available on a raster (pixel) layer. [Availability: Raster layers only]
Merge Down: Merges the active layer into the layer directly below it, combining them into one. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Flatten: Combines all layers into a single flat layer. Use it to finalise a design into one image.
Convert to Smart Object: Wraps the active layer in a smart object so it can be transformed and re-edited without losing quality. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Add Layer Mask: Adds a mask to the active layer so you can hide parts of it non-destructively by painting on the mask. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Create Clipping Mask: Clips the active layer to the layer below it so it only shows where the layer beneath has content. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Fit into Frame: Fits the active layer into a frame so its content is contained and cropped to the frame's shape. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Bring Forward: Moves the active layer one step up the stack, in front of the layer above it. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Send Backward: Moves the active layer one step down the stack, behind the layer below it. Requires an active layer. [Availability: Requires an active layer]
Crop to Layer: Crops the canvas to the bounds of the selected layer or selection of layers.

sections.title: File menu (extra states)
sections.text:
Placeholder text the File menu shows when there is nothing to list.
This covers a File menu label that only appears in an empty state, so it is easy to miss when scanning the normal item list.
No recent files: A greyed-out placeholder shown inside `File, then Open Recent` when you have not opened any files yet. It is not clickable and just tells you the recent list is empty. As soon as you open images, this is replaced by their names.

sections.title: Menu keyboard and pointer navigation
sections.text:
Keys and mouse actions for moving around an open menu dropdown.
Every top menu (File, Edit, Image, Layer and the rest) opens the same kind of dropdown, so these controls work identically in all of them.
You can drive a menu entirely from the keyboard, or open submenus by hovering with the mouse. Items that are not currently available appear greyed out and cannot be chosen.
Arrow Down: Moves the highlight to the next selectable item in the open menu. It skips dividers and submenu headers and wraps back to the top after the last item.
Arrow Up: Moves the highlight to the previous selectable item in the open menu. It wraps around to the last item when you go past the first.
Enter: Runs the currently highlighted menu item, the same as clicking it. The menu then closes. [Requires: An item is highlighted]
Escape: Closes the open menu without running anything. Use it to back out of a menu you opened by mistake.
Arrow Right (open submenu): Opens the first submenu in the current menu, for example `File, then Open Recent` or `Layer, then New Fill Layer`. Submenu parents are marked with a small right-pointing arrow.
Arrow Left (close submenu): Closes the currently open submenu and returns focus to the parent menu.
Hover to open submenu: Moving the mouse over a submenu parent (any item with the right-pointing arrow) opens its submenu automatically, and moving away closes it. This is the pointer alternative to the arrow keys.
Disabled (greyed) items: Menu items that do not apply right now are shown greyed out and cannot be clicked. For example `Paste Layer` is disabled until something has been copied, and `Crop to Selection` is disabled until you have an active selection.

sections.title: Select menu
sections.text:
Everything for making, changing, and reusing pixel selections.
The **Select** menu holds the commands that create a selection, refine it, switch to a selection tool, or store one for later. Many items only light up when something is already selected.
A selection limits where edits, fills, and filters apply. `Deselect` returns you to editing the whole layer.
All: Selects the entire canvas so the next edit affects everything.
Deselect: Clears the current selection so edits apply to the whole layer again. Only enabled while a selection exists.
Inverse: Flips the selection so everything that was outside becomes selected and the old selection becomes unselected. Handy after selecting a subject to then work on its background.
Select by Marquee: Switches to the Marquee tool so you can drag a rectangular selection.
Select by Lasso: Switches to the Lasso tool so you can draw a freehand selection outline.
Smart Select [AI]: Automatically finds the main subject in the image and selects it for you, no dragging needed.
Remove Object [AI]: Fills the current selection by rebuilding the pixels behind it so the selected object disappears. Only enabled while a selection exists. With an AI provider configured it asks that provider first, and the whole flattened document is sent for the edit; without one, or if the call fails, it reconstructs the area locally in your browser. Either way the result arrives as a new image layer the size of the document, above the stack.
Feather: Softens the selection edge by a chosen radius so edits fade in gradually instead of stopping at a hard line. Only enabled while a selection exists.
Save Selection: Stores the current selection under a name so you can bring it back later. Only enabled while a selection exists.
Load Selection: Restores a selection you saved earlier. Only enabled once at least one selection has been saved.

sections.title: Filter menu
sections.text:
Preset looks plus grouped image effects for blur, color, duotone, and stylize.
The **Filter** menu is organised into submenus. **Presets** apply a non-destructive whole-layer look. The other groups (**Blur & Sharpen**, **Color**, **Duotone**, **Stylize**) run pixel effects on the active layer.
Effects that have settings open a small dialog first; effects with nothing to adjust (like `Invert` or the `Auto` fixes) apply immediately. Most items are disabled until you select a layer.
Presets: A submenu of one-click, non-destructive filter looks applied to the active layer. Any filter presets added by extensions appear here too.
B&W: Removes all color for a clean grayscale look.
Sepia: Adds a warm brown tint for a vintage feel.
Warm: Pushes colors toward warm tones and lifts saturation slightly.
Cool: Shifts colors toward cooler blue tones.
Vibrant: Boosts saturation and contrast for a punchy image.
Faded: Lowers saturation and contrast and lifts the shadows for a washed-out look.
Vintage: Muted retro tone with a slight sepia shift.
Noir: High-contrast, moody black and white.
Punch: Extra contrast and saturation for a bold pop.
Meadow: Fresh, green-leaning outdoor tone.
Dusk: Soft evening color grade.
Sunbleach: Bright, bleached highlights like strong sun.
Arctic: Cold, desaturated icy look.
Cocoa: Warm brown cinematic tone.
Neon: Vivid, electric saturation.
Mist: Soft, hazy, low-contrast look.
Cinema: Filmic color grade for a movie feel.
Remove Filter: Removes any preset filter from the active layer, returning it to its original look. Only enabled when a filter is applied.
Blur & Sharpen: Submenu of focus effects that soften or crisp the image.
Gaussian Blur: Smoothly blurs the layer by an adjustable radius. Opens a settings dialog.
Box Blur: A fast averaging blur with a boxy character. Opens a settings dialog.
Tilt-Shift: Keeps a horizontal band sharp and blurs above and below it for a miniature look. Opens a settings dialog.
Sharpen: Increases edge contrast to make the image look crisper.
Unsharp Mask: Controlled sharpening with amount, radius, and threshold so you can avoid over-sharpening. Opens a settings dialog.
Denoise: Reduces grain and speckle noise while trying to keep detail.
Color: Submenu of tonal and color adjustments.
Auto Levels: Automatically stretches each channel to use the full tonal range. Applies immediately.
Auto Contrast: Automatically stretches overall contrast without shifting colors. Applies immediately.
Auto Color: Automatically neutralizes a color cast for more natural tones. Applies immediately.
Shadows / Highlights: Recovers detail hidden in the darkest and brightest areas. Opens a settings dialog.
Levels: Manual black point, white point, and midtone (gamma) control plus an output range. Opens a settings dialog.
Curves: Freeform tone curve for precise brightness and contrast shaping. Opens a settings dialog.
Gamma: Brightens or darkens the midtones without clipping black or white. Opens a settings dialog.
Color Splash: Keeps one chosen color and desaturates the rest of the image. Opens a settings dialog.
Invert: Inverts every color to its opposite for a photo-negative effect. Applies immediately.
Posterize: Reduces the image to a small number of tonal steps for a flat, graphic look. Opens a settings dialog.
Threshold: Converts the image to pure black and white at a chosen brightness cutoff. Opens a settings dialog.
Duotone: Submenu that maps the image to two colors (a shadow tone and a highlight tone) using ready-made pairs.
Stylize: Submenu of creative, look-changing effects.
Vignette: Darkens the edges of the frame to draw the eye to the center. Opens a settings dialog.
Glow: Adds a soft bloom around bright areas for a dreamy feel. Opens a settings dialog.
Noise / Grain: Adds film-style grain or noise texture. Opens a settings dialog.
Pixelate: Turns the image into blocky mosaic squares. Opens a settings dialog.
Halftone: Reproduces the image as a pattern of printer-style dots. Opens a settings dialog.
Glitch: Adds digital distortion and color-channel shifts for a broken-signal look. Opens a settings dialog.
Emboss: Turns edges into a raised, gray relief. Opens a settings dialog.
Edge Detect: Traces the outlines in the image and hides the flat areas. Opens a settings dialog.
Duotone (custom): The full Duotone effect where you pick your own shadow and highlight colors, listed inside the Stylize submenu. Opens a settings dialog.
Extensions [Extension]: An extra submenu that appears only when installed extensions register their own effects, listing each one.

sections.title: View menu
sections.text:
Zoom, panels, rulers, guides, snapping, color proofing, and post preview.
The **View** menu controls how the canvas is displayed without changing the image itself: zoom level, which panels are visible, on-screen aids like rulers and guides, and preview modes.
Show/Hide items change their label depending on the current state (for example `Show Rulers` becomes `Hide Rulers`). On Mac the shortcut key is Cmd; on Windows it is Ctrl.
Zoom In: Enlarges the canvas view by 25 percent each time. Does not change the image.
Zoom Out: Shrinks the canvas view by dividing the zoom by 1.25 each time.
Fit: Scales the view so the whole document fits inside the window.
100%: Sets the view to actual size, one screen pixel per image pixel.
Zoom to Selection: Zooms in to frame the current selection with a small margin around it. Only enabled while a selection exists.
Show Navigator / Hide Navigator: Toggles the Navigator panel, a small thumbnail map for panning and jumping around a zoomed-in document.
Show Timeline / Hide Timeline: Toggles the Timeline panel used for animation and frame work.
Show Library / Hide Library: Toggles the side Library panel of assets and templates.
Show Pages / Hide Pages: Toggles the Pages panel for multi-page documents. Only available when the document has pages.
Workspace: Opens the Workspace settings where you can cosmetically show or hide the toolbar, panels, sections, and menus to build a personal layout.
Show Rulers / Hide Rulers: Toggles the horizontal and vertical rulers along the canvas edges.
Show Grid / Hide Grid: Toggles a repeating alignment grid over the canvas.
Show Guides / Hide Guides: Toggles the visibility of your placed guide lines without deleting them.
Snap: Turns snapping on or off so dragged objects and guides jump to align with edges, guides, and the grid. Shows a checkmark when on.
Guides & Grid: Opens the Guides and Grid dialog to add guides at set positions and adjust grid spacing.
Clear Guides: Removes all guide lines from the document in one step. Only enabled when guides exist.
Proof Colors: Submenu that previews how the design looks under color-blindness or grayscale, so you can check it stays readable. Choose None to return to normal.
Check Contrast: Opens the contrast checker that measures text-to-background contrast against accessibility (WCAG) targets.
Preview with Post: Shows your design in the context of a real post or page so you can judge how it will look in place.
Exit Post Preview: Leaves the post preview and returns to the normal canvas. Greyed out unless a post preview is active.

sections.title: Automation menu
sections.text:
Bulk and generative jobs grouped into Content, Images, Design, and Actions.
The **Automation** menu gathers everything that runs across many posts or images or generates work for you, organised into four submenus.
Some items are Pro features, and they carry a **Pro** chip here. In the editor itself they are not greyed out: without the Pro add-on the entry is simply absent from the menu, so if you are looking for one of them and cannot find it, that is why. Items without a chip are part of the free plugin.
Content: Submenu for generating and templating post content.
Generate Content [Pro, AI]: Opens the tool that drafts post or page content for you. Part of WunderPaint Pro.
Content Templates [Pro]: Manages reusable content templates used by the content generator. Part of WunderPaint Pro.
Featured Images [Pro, AI]: Automatically creates featured images across many posts at once. Part of WunderPaint Pro.
Images: Submenu for bulk image processing jobs.
Image Processor [Pro]: Runs resizing, format conversion, and other steps over a batch of images. Part of WunderPaint Pro.
Generate from CSV [Pro]: Produces many images from one design by merging rows of a CSV data file (data merge). Part of WunderPaint Pro.
Batch Watermark: Applies a watermark to many images in one run. Free feature.
Metadata Assistant [AI]: Helps write image metadata such as alt text across images. Free feature.
Design: Submenu of assistants that generate whole designs.
Design Generator [AI]: Generates a complete layout from a brief you describe. Free feature.
Actions: Submenu for recording and replaying editor steps. Lists Manage Actions, then the bundled action categories (Web & Sizes, Photo Fixes, Looks & Styles, Artistic, Privacy & AI, Social Formats) as their own level, and then the actions you saved yourself.
Manage Actions: Opens the manager to record, edit, and organise reusable action macros.

sections.title: Tools menu
sections.text:
Single-purpose creative tools that live inside the editor.
The **Tools** menu holds standalone creative tools that are neither bulk automation nor extensions. Each item opens its own dialog or studio.
Color Schemer: Opens a tool for building and exploring color palettes and harmonies for your design.
Background Studio: Opens a studio for generating and editing backgrounds such as gradients and patterns.
Screenshot Beautifier: Dresses up a plain screenshot with padding, rounded corners, shadows, and a nice backdrop.
Mockup Generator: Places your design onto product and device mockups.
Chart & Table: Creates charts and data tables to drop into your design.
QR Code Generator: Generates a QR code you can style and place in the document.

sections.title: Extensions menu
sections.text:
A launcher that lists the generators of every installed extension.
The **Extensions** menu is a launcher, and its first level is a fixed set of nine categories rather than a list of extensions. Inside a category an extension with a single generator appears as a direct item; one with several becomes a submenu named after the extension. Generators that belong to the editor itself do not appear here.
This menu only appears when at least one extension generator or extension menu item is installed. Managing and installing extensions is done from `Help, then Manage Extensions`, not here.
Installed extension launchers [Extension]: Each installed extension contributes its generator into the category it declares, so you can open it in one click. Extensions with multiple generators show a submenu named after the extension.

sections.title: Help menu
sections.text:
Documentation, shortcuts, tour, Easy Mode, status, and about.
The **Help** menu links to learning resources, the keyboard-shortcut list, a guided tour, and system information. Extension management also lives here for administrators.
Handbook: Opens the full editor handbook with guides and reference.
Keyboard Shortcuts: Opens a reference sheet of every keyboard shortcut in the editor.
Show Tour: Starts the guided walkthrough that points out the main parts of the editor.
Easy Mode: Switches this user to a simplified beginner interface. The full editor stays the default and only the chrome changes for you.
Manage Extensions [Extension]: Opens the extension manager to install, update, and remove extensions. Shown only to users who can manage the site (administrators).
System Status: Opens a diagnostics screen showing environment details, storage use, and health checks for support.
About WunderPaint: Shows version, credits, and other information about the plugin.

sections.title: Filter, then Duotone (color duotones)
sections.text:
Eight ready-made two-tone duotones under Filter, then Duotone that recolor the active layer.
Each preset remaps the image so the darkest areas take one color and the brightest areas take another, giving a poster-like two-tone look. They apply straight to the active layer with a fixed pair of colors. For a fully custom shadow and highlight color pair, use the Duotone effect in the Stylize submenu instead.
Noir: Duotone with near-black shadows and light grey highlights for a classic monochrome look. This is the duotone version, separate from the **Noir** filter preset.
Ocean: Deep navy shadows with light sky-blue highlights, for a cool marine tone.
Sunset: Warm maroon shadows with golden highlights, for a sundown look.
Forest: Dark green shadows with pale green highlights, for an earthy tone.
Berry: Deep purple shadows with soft pink highlights, for a bold pop tone.
Steel: Slate blue-grey shadows with light grey highlights, for a neutral industrial tone.
Gold: Dark brown shadows with gold highlights, for a warm luxury tone.
Mint: Dark teal shadows with mint highlights, for a fresh cool tone.

sections.title: Proof Colors (vision simulations)
sections.text:
The View, then Proof Colors submenu switches the canvas into a display-only color-blindness simulation.
These options tint the canvas so you can preview how your design looks to viewers with color vision deficiency. The change is display only and is applied as a filter on the canvas stage; your saved and exported files are never affected. Only one mode is active at a time, marked with a check.
None: Turns proofing off and shows the design in its true colors. This is the default and carries a check when no proof mode is active.
Protanopia (no red): Simulates red-blind vision (missing red cones) so you can check whether reds and greens still read apart.
Deuteranopia (no green): Simulates green-blind vision (missing green cones), the most common form of color blindness.
Tritanopia (no blue): Simulates blue-blind vision (missing blue cones) so you can check blue and yellow separation.
Grayscale: Removes all color so you can judge whether the design still holds up on tonal contrast alone.

sections.title: Automation, then Actions (saved macros)
sections.text:
Below Manage Actions, the Actions submenu lists your recorded actions for one-click replay.
Any action (macro) you record is listed here under the Manage Actions entry. Selecting one replays its recorded steps on the current document. When you have not recorded anything yet, a disabled placeholder is shown instead.
Saved action: Each recorded action appears as its own item labelled with its name. Click it to replay all of its steps on the current document.
No saved actions: A disabled placeholder shown when you have not recorded any actions yet. Record one in Manage Actions to make it appear here.

sections.title: Character (text properties)
sections.text:
The character controls in the options bar that set the typeface, size and weight of the selected text.
These appear in the top options bar whenever the Text tool is active, or the Move tool is active over a text layer. During an open text edit they restyle the characters you have selected inside the box; with the layer only selected they restyle the whole layer. Changes also apply to every other selected text layer at once.
Font family: Opens the font picker to choose the typeface for the text. During a text edit it restyles the selected characters, otherwise the whole layer. The picker has a search field on top: type to filter all font groups, Enter picks the first match.
Weight: Dropdown that sets the stroke thickness of the letters, from light to black.
Font size: Type a size for the text, or drag the `px` label beside it to scrub the value up and down.
Bold: Toggles the text between normal (weight 400) and bold (weight 700). Highlighted when the text is 700 or heavier.
Italic: Slants the text on or off for emphasis.
Underline: Draws a line under the text on or off.
Color: Sets the text fill color from a swatch. With no text layer active it sets the shared foreground color instead.

sections.title: Paragraph and layout (text)
sections.text:
Alignment, curve and layout controls that act on the whole text layer.
These options sit next to the character controls in the options bar and apply to the entire text layer rather than a character selection. They cover horizontal and vertical alignment inside the text box, curving the line, and the layout and annotation helpers.
Align left: Aligns each line of text to the left edge of the text box. The tooltip reads `left`.
Align center: Centers each line of text horizontally in the text box. The tooltip reads `center`.
Align right: Aligns each line of text to the right edge of the text box. The tooltip reads `right`.
Align top: Positions the text at the top of its box vertically. The default for fixed-width text boxes.
Align middle: Centers the text vertically within its box. The default for auto-width text.
Align bottom: Sits the text at the bottom of its box vertically.
Curve: Bends the whole line of text along an arc. At 0 the text is straight; move toward the ends for a stronger curve up or down.
Layout: Opens a popover with six rendered previews (two classic layouts plus four seeded variations) that restyle the text block into a designed arrangement.
Remove layout: The × button next to Layout clears an applied text layout and returns to plain text. Only shown once a layout is in place.
Annotate: The last group in the text options bar. Its `Presets` button opens a popover of hand-drawn annotation presets (markers, circles, boxes, underlines, strikes and combos), each previewed with your own text. Only appears for an existing text layer.

sections.title: Annotate presets
sections.text:
The hand-drawn annotation presets behind the Annotate button in the text options bar: markers, circles, boxes, underlines, strikes and combos.
Select a text layer and the options bar shows an `Annotate` group with a `Presets` button. It opens a popover of live mini previews grouped into five categories: `Marker`, `Circles & Boxes`, `Underlines`, `Strikes` and `Combos`. Every tile is rendered from your own layer, using the first word of its text (up to six characters, falling back to `Style` when the layer is empty) in its real font, so the tile is the result.
The presets are deliberately hand-drawn only. Material looks such as gold, chrome or neon live in the Effects panel, and shadows and outlines live in Blending Options, so nothing overlaps. Each preset first clears the layer's outline, shadow, per-character styles and text effects, then applies its own combination, which means switching presets never leaves half of the previous look behind.
Clicking a tile applies it and closes the popover, recorded as `Text style preset` in history. The popover also closes on a click outside it or on Escape.
Presets: The button in the `Annotate` group of the text options bar. It opens the preset popover and only appears while a text layer is selected.
Color: The ink swatch at the top of the popover. Picking a color recolors an annotation already on the layer straight away (recorded as `Annotation color`) and tints every preset you apply afterwards, so a whole set of doodles shares one ink. Until you touch it, the swatch shows red.
Preset colors: Resets the ink swatch so presets apply in their own built-in colors again. Only shown once you have picked an ink color. It clears the ink for future clicks and does not change an annotation already on the layer.
Remove annotation: Applies the bare reset preset: clears the layer's text effects, outline, shadow and per-character styles and returns it to plain text.
Marker: A yellow highlighter band swiped behind the text, lightly roughened.
Pink Swipe: A single pink marker swipe, tapered like a pen stroke rather than a full band.
Double Swipe: Two overlapping teal marker swipes, as if you went over the words twice.
Scribble Fill: An orange scribble filled back and forth behind the text instead of a clean band.
Sky Swipe: A light blue marker swipe with extra roughness, for a looser hand.
Weathered Marker: A lilac highlighter band at maximum roughness, so the edges look dried out and worn.
Sun Swipe: A warm yellow marker swipe with clean edges.
Mint Band: A mint green highlighter band behind the text.
Circled: A red hand-drawn oval looped around the text.
Sketchy Circle: A blue oval drawn with a very shaky line, for a rough sketched note.
Double Loop: A red circle looped around the text twice, as if you went round again for emphasis.
Sketchy Box: A near-black hand-drawn rectangle around the text.
Blue Box: A blue hand-drawn rectangle around the text, drawn with a looser line.
Ink Loop: A near-black double loop around the text, like a pen circling a word on paper.
Green Oval: A green hand-drawn oval around the text, roughened for a marked-correct feel.
Red Box: A red hand-drawn rectangle around the text, for a flagged or corrected word.
Scribble Under: A blue hand-drawn wavy line scribbled under the text.
Double Under: Two red hand-drawn strokes under the text, for a stronger emphasis than a single line.
Hand Zigzag: A green hand-drawn zigzag under the text.
Cursive Loops: A purple looping cursive line under the text, like a run of handwritten e's.
Wave Under: A blue sine wave underline drawn as a clean, even ruled line rather than a shaky one.
Rough Under: An orange scribbled wave under the text at high roughness, for a scrappier hand.
Clean Under: A single straight, near-black ruled underline with no hand-drawn wobble.
Dashed Under: A red ruled underline drawn as two parallel straight lines under the text.
Red Strike: A single rough red line struck through the middle of the text, overshooting slightly at both ends.
Double Strike: Two near-black lines struck through the text, one just above and one just below the middle.
Crossed Out: A big red X drawn across the whole text box, corner to corner.
Blue Pencil: A single blue line struck through the text at high roughness, like an editor's pencil mark.
Teacher's Red: Combines a red oval around the text with a red line struck through it, like a marked-up exam paper.
Important!: Combines a yellow highlighter band with a red zigzag underline.
Checked Off: Combines a pale green marker swipe with a green line struck through the text, for a finished to-do item.
Noted: Combines a yellow highlighter band with a red oval around the text.
Proofread: Combines a blue hand-drawn box around the text with a blue double scribble under it.
Sold Out: Combines a yellow highlighter band with a big red X across the text.
Action Item: Combines a near-black hand-drawn box around the text with a red zigzag under it.
Annotated: Combines a purple double loop around the text with purple cursive loops under it.

sections.title: Create New Image dialog
sections.text:
The New Image dialog picks a size preset or custom dimensions, then starts a blank canvas, an AI generation, or a template.
Reached through `File, then New` (and shown as the welcome start screen when the editor opens with no image). A preset list runs down the left side; the main area has three tabs: **Blank Canvas**, **Generate with AI**, and **Templates**.
The footer shows a live memory estimate for the chosen size and warns as the canvas gets very large. Browsers cannot draw canvases beyond about 16000 px per side, so the Create button is blocked past that limit.
Blank Canvas: Starts an empty document at the chosen size, name, resolution, color mode, and background. This is the default tab.
Generate with AI [AI, Cloud AI]: Generates a full image straight onto a new canvas from a text prompt, using a configured AI image provider. The result lands as an `AI Generation` layer sized to the canvas.
Templates: Opens a starter template, an extension template pack, or one of your saved dynamic templates as a new document.
Instagram Square: Size preset for a square Instagram post. Selecting it also suggests its name for the document. This is the preset selected when the dialog opens.
Instagram Story: Size preset for a vertical Instagram or reels story.
OG / Social Share: Size preset for an Open Graph social share image (the thumbnail shown when a link is posted).
Full HD: Size preset for a 1080p full HD landscape canvas.
Header / Banner: Size preset for a wide header or banner strip.
Standard: Size preset for a general purpose 4:3 web image.
Custom Size: Starting point for a free size. Typing your own width or height also switches the selection to Custom.
Name: The document name. Picking a preset fills in the preset label until you type your own name. On the Blank tab the Create button stays disabled until a name is present.
Width: Canvas width in the current unit. If the aspect link is on, height follows to keep the ratio.
Height: Canvas height in the current unit. If the aspect link is on, width follows to keep the ratio.
Link aspect ratio: Chain toggle between the width and height fields. When on, changing one dimension scales the other to preserve the current proportion. Off by default.
Unit: Switches the width and height fields between pixels, inches, and centimetres. Inches and centimetres are converted to pixels using the chosen resolution.
Resolution: Pixels per inch used for print and for converting inch or centimetre dimensions to pixels. Higher values give sharper prints at the same physical size.
Color Mode: The document's color model and bit depth. RGB suits screen work; CMYK is for print pipelines.
Transparent: Starts the canvas with no background fill, shown as a checkerboard. Use this when the image needs to sit on top of something else. This is the default background.
White: Fills the canvas background with solid white.
Black: Fills the canvas background with solid black.
Custom: Picks any background color from a swatch. Selecting Custom reveals a color button next to the choices.
Preview card: A scaled thumbnail of the blank canvas at the chosen aspect and background, with the exact pixel dimensions shown beneath it. Updates live as you change size or background.
Model [AI, Cloud AI]: On the AI tab, chooses which configured image provider generates the picture. Shows one pill per available provider; if none are set up, a link to Settings appears instead.
Prompt [AI]: The text description of the image to generate. Generation is blocked with a toast if this is left empty.
Styles [AI]: One-tap chips that append a style word to the prompt. Each chip adds its lowercased name to whatever text is already there.
Starter templates: On the Templates tab, a grid of built-in ready-made designs. Clicking one opens it as a new document.
Extension template packs [Extension]: Extra template grids contributed by installed extensions, each under its own pack heading. They open the same way as starter templates.
Your templates: Your own saved dynamic templates. Opening one restores its layers and keeps its template link so you can later update it in place.
Delete template: Removes one of your saved templates. Only appears on your own saved templates, not starter or pack templates.
Canvas memory readout: Footer line showing the pixel size and rough memory use of the canvas. It turns to a warning past 8000 px per side and to a blocking error past 16000 px per side.
Cancel: Closes the dialog without creating anything. Hidden on the welcome start screen, where you must pick a size first.
Create & Edit: Creates the document and opens it for editing. On the AI tab the button reads **Generate & Edit** and runs the image generation first. Disabled while busy, past the size limit, on the AI tab with no provider, or on the Blank tab with no name.
Search templates… (Templates tab): The search box above the starter templates in the Templates tab. Same matcher as the Asset Library: it searches the template name, the copy on its text layers, its category and the names of its dominant colors, and every word you type must match.
Category chips (Templates tab): An All chip plus one chip per template category. Picking a category filters both the bundled starters and the installed template packs at once.
Color dots (Templates tab): The twelve color swatches next to the chips. Click one to keep only templates whose dominant palette contains that color, click it again to clear it.

sections.title: Export / Save dialog
sections.text:
One dialog for downloading a file, saving over the media library image, or saving a copy as a new attachment, with format, quality, scale, metadata, and batch options.
This dialog runs in three modes and its title and primary button change to match. **Save to Media Library** overwrites the current attachment (keeping a version). **Save as New Attachment** (called **Apply** when opened from a page builder) writes a copy. **Export** downloads a file without touching the library.
A live flattened preview sits at the top. Below it are the format picker and the quality, scale, and (where needed) flatten controls, followed by batch export, presets, watermark, and metadata sections. When a post preview is active, export renders the resolved dynamic content while the saved project keeps its placeholders.
Dialog modes: The dialog opens as Save (overwrite the library image), Save as / Apply (write a copy or hand it back to a page builder), or Export (download only). Metadata and project options show only outside Export mode.
Preview: A flattened PNG thumbnail of the final composite at up to 220 px, so you see exactly what will be written. Updates live as layers or bindings change.
PNG: Lossless format that keeps transparency. Best for graphics, logos, and anything with sharp edges or alpha. This is the default format.
JPEG: Compressed photo format with no transparency. Smaller files for photos; a Quality slider and a flatten background appear when it is chosen on a transparent document.
WebP: Modern format with good compression and transparency support. A Quality slider appears when it is chosen.
GIF [New]: Animated GIF built from the visible top-level layers, one layer per frame. Only offered in Export mode when there are at least two frame layers. [Availability: Export mode, 2+ frame layers]
APNG: Animated PNG built the same way as the GIF option but with full color and alpha. Export mode only, needs at least two frame layers. [Availability: Export mode, 2+ frame layers]
WebM: Animated WebM video from the frame layers. Only offered in Export mode when the browser supports MediaRecorder and there are at least two frame layers. [Availability: Export mode, MediaRecorder support, 2+ frame layers]
PSD: Layered Photoshop file, download only. Offered in Export mode when there are layers; the media library cannot display PSDs, so re-editing is covered by the project sidecar instead. It has no quality or scale controls. [Availability: Export mode, download only]
PDF: Single-page PDF built from a JPEG render of the canvas. Export mode only; it has a Quality slider and, on a transparent document, a flatten background. [Availability: Export mode]
Extension formats [Extension]: Extra export formats added by installed extensions appear at the end of the format row in Export mode, each with its own label and file extension.
Quality: Compression quality for lossy formats. Higher keeps more detail and makes a bigger file. Shown for JPEG, WebP and PDF only.
Background (flatten): The color that fills transparent areas when a format cannot store transparency (JPEG, PDF). Without it, transparent pixels would turn black in the encoder. Only shown on a transparent document with such a format.
Frame delay: Time each frame is held in an animated GIF, APNG, or WebM. The value is shown in seconds. Only appears for those animated formats.
Frames note: An informational line for animated formats that states how many frames will be produced (each visible top-level layer becomes one frame).
Scale: Multiplier on the output pixel size, so you can render at half size up to double size. The Output line and estimated file size update with it. Hidden for PSD.
Output / Est. size: A read-only line showing the final pixel dimensions (document size times scale) and a rough estimate of the encoded file size in megabytes.
Batch sizes (ZIP): Checkboxes for the built-in size presets. Tick any you want and export renders the design at each one, packed into a single ZIP. Export mode, non-PSD only.
Download ZIP: Builds and downloads the ZIP of the ticked batch sizes. Disabled until at least one size is checked; the button shows how many are selected.
Presets (export): Saved combinations of format, quality, and scale shown as chips. Click a chip to apply it; Alt-click removes it. Export mode only.
Add preset: The plus chip saves the current format, quality, and scale as a named export preset for reuse.
Favicon set (ZIP): Renders the canvas into a favicon bundle: a favicon.ico, a set of PNG sizes from 16 to 512 px, and an HTML snippet, all zipped. Export mode only.
Watermark: Applies a watermark image over the output. The dropdown lists your Brand Kit watermarks plus a legacy Settings watermark; position, size, opacity, and margin follow the last used batch watermark placement. Hidden for PSD.
Filename: The name used for the saved or downloaded file. Prefilled from the document name. Shown outside Export mode as a metadata field, and used as the download name in Export mode.
Alt Text: Alternative text stored on the attachment for accessibility and SEO. Prefilled from the existing attachment when editing one. Save and Save as modes only.
Title: The attachment title saved with the image. Prefilled from the document or existing attachment. Save and Save as modes only.
Caption: The attachment caption saved with the image. Save and Save as modes only.
Description: A longer optional description saved on the attachment. Multi-line text field, Save and Save as modes only.
Generate alt text [AI, Cloud AI]: Uses an AI text provider to look at the rendered image and fill in the Alt Text, Caption, and Description. Disabled with a hint when no text provider key is configured. [Requires: Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini text key]
Version note: An optional note describing what changed, stored with the new version and shown in the Versions panel. Save mode only. [Availability: Save mode]
Overwrites original notice: A caution box shown in Save mode reminding you that saving replaces the original file, while the previous version stays available in the Versions panel.
Keep editable project file: Stores a sidecar project file alongside the image so the layered design can be reopened and edited later. On by default; shown outside Export mode. The sidecar always keeps the raw binding placeholders even when the pixels ship a resolved preview.
Copy to clipboard [Free]: Copies the rendered image as a PNG to the system clipboard instead of saving a file. Export mode only, hidden for PSD and where the browser lacks clipboard image write.
Cancel: Closes the dialog without saving or downloading.
Primary action: Runs the save or export. The label is **Save to Media Library** in Save mode, **Create Attachment** in Save as mode, and **Download** in Export mode. Shows a spinner while working.
Overwriting and image optimizers: Saving over the library image keeps the same URL, and that is what makes this worth knowing. Optimization plugins that deliver WebP or AVIF (Imagify, ShortPixel, EWWW, Smush, Optimole and others work this way) serve a converted copy from that same URL, and that copy was made from the previous version of the picture. Until the optimizer converts the image again, the editor and the media library show your edit while the public page can still show the old one. Two ways around it: re-optimize that single image in whichever optimizer you use, or choose Save as New Attachment, which writes a copy with its own URL that no stale conversion can point at. WunderPaint reports every overwrite to WordPress through wp_update_attachment_metadata(), the signal optimization plugins are meant to listen for; what they do with it is theirs to decide.
EU AI label: Places one of the European Commission's official emblems for AI disclosure into the picture, and can record the matching IPTC entry in the file. Starts on None and does nothing unless you pick a motif. See the next section.

sections.title: EU AI labels
sections.text:
The European Commission's official emblems for disclosing AI involvement, applied when saving or exporting, and only when you ask for one.
Three motifs, each in black, white and half-opacity versions, shipped with the plugin as the Commission publishes them. They are free to use and need no attribution.
Nothing is ever applied on its own. The editor does not inspect your design, does not guess and never suggests a label, because the disclosure rules are about content that could be taken for something real, not about every illustration, and only the person who made it knows which one it is.
EU AI label: Places one of the European Commission's official emblems for AI disclosure into the exported picture. Three motifs: a basic emblem, Fully AI-generated, and Partially AI-modified. The list starts on None and nothing is applied unless you pick a motif yourself. The editor never inspects a design or suggests one, because only you know whether what you made could be taken for a real photograph. [Availability: every still format, including WebP and AVIF; not for GIF, APNG, WebM or PSD]
Emblem color: Black, white, or either of those at half opacity, matching the four variants the Commission publishes. Pick the one that stays readable on your picture.
Emblem position: Which corner the emblem is stamped into, or the center. It is drawn onto the finished export the same way a watermark is.
Emblem size: Size as a percent of the export width. The basic emblem is square and the other two are wide bars, so each motif starts at its own value, chosen so all three end up about the same height.
Also record it in the file metadata: A second box, empty unless you tick it, that writes the matching IPTC digital source type into the file as well. That is the vocabulary picture agencies and image search read, so an image can declare its origin even where the emblem is cropped away. The metadata entry itself can only be written into PNG and JPEG, so the box appears for those two; the emblem on the picture is not limited that way. Nothing is written to the file unless this is on.

sections.title: Image Size / Canvas Size dialog
sections.text:
A Photoshop-style dialog to change pixel dimensions, either resampling the whole image or resizing just the canvas around an anchor.
The same dialog runs in two modes. **Image Size** resamples the whole document, scaling every layer to the new dimensions. **Canvas Size** changes the canvas area only, keeping layers at their pixel size and adding or trimming space around an anchor point.
Width and height can be entered in pixels or as a percentage. Both dimensions are clamped between 1 and 12000 px, and Image Size additionally caps the total at 24 megapixels.
Image Size (mode): Resamples the whole document to new dimensions, scaling all layers uniformly. Use it to make the finished image larger or smaller. Offers the aspect-ratio link.
Canvas Size (mode): Changes the canvas dimensions without scaling layers, adding or cropping space around an anchor. Use it to give a design more room or to trim it. Adds the Relative option and the anchor grid.
Current size: A read-only line showing the document's present width and height in pixels, for reference before you change it.
Width: The target width in the current unit. In Image Size with the link on, height follows to keep the aspect ratio. Press Enter to apply.
Height: The target height in the current unit. In Image Size with the link on, width follows to keep the aspect ratio. Press Enter to apply.
Link aspect ratio: Chain toggle that keeps width and height proportional in Image Size mode. On by default; shown only in Image Size (Canvas Size resizes each side freely). [Availability: Image Size only]
Unit (px / %): Switches the width and height fields between absolute pixels and a percentage of the current size. Switching converts the current values so the target stays the same.
Relative: In Canvas Size, treats the width and height values as an amount to add or remove rather than an absolute size. Positive numbers grow the canvas, negative numbers trim it. Zeroes the fields when toggled. [Availability: Canvas Size only]
Anchor: A 3 by 3 grid choosing where the existing content sits as the canvas grows or shrinks. Centre keeps content centred; a corner or edge pins content there and adds space on the opposite sides. Canvas Size only.
New size: A read-only line showing the resulting width and height. It turns red and blocks Apply if the size is outside 1 to 12000 px.
Cancel: Closes the dialog without changing the document.
Apply: Commits the resize. Disabled while the new size is invalid; Image Size also shows an error and stops if the result would exceed 24 megapixels.

sections.title: Resize Design dialog
sections.text:
Retargets the whole design to a different format, scaling every layer uniformly and recentering so nothing gets distorted.
Unlike Image Size, this dialog is built for changing the shape of a design (for example from a square post to a vertical story). It rescales all layers together and recenters the composition, so proportions are preserved rather than stretched.
Pick one of the social and web presets for a one-click retarget, or type a custom width and height. Undo restores the previous format.
Current size note: A read-only line showing the present dimensions and a reminder that layers scale uniformly with no distortion.
Instagram Post: One-click retarget to a square Instagram post.
Instagram Story: One-click retarget to a vertical Instagram story.
Facebook Post: One-click retarget to a Facebook landscape post.
YouTube Thumbnail: One-click retarget to a YouTube video thumbnail.
X Header: One-click retarget to an X (Twitter) profile header.
Pinterest Pin: One-click retarget to a tall Pinterest pin.
LinkedIn Banner: One-click retarget to a LinkedIn profile banner.
Full HD: One-click retarget to a 1080p landscape canvas.
Width: Custom target width for a size not in the preset list. Combined with Height and the Resize button.
Height: Custom target height for a size not in the preset list. Combined with Width and the Resize button.
Resize: Applies the custom width and height, retargeting the design. Disabled until both values are within 16 to 12000 px. A toast confirms the new size and notes that undo restores the old format.
Cancel / Close: Closes the dialog without changing the design (the corner close button or Escape).

sections.title: Export Carousel dialog
sections.text:
Slices a wide document into a numbered sequence of equal vertical tiles, for a swipeable social carousel, as a ZIP or straight into the media library.
Point this at a wide design and it cuts it into N side-by-side tiles of equal width and full height, numbered in order. A preview shows the design with dashed guide lines where the cuts fall.
Tiles can be downloaded as a single ZIP or written directly as new media library images. The filenames use the document name plus a number.
Preview with slice guides: A scaled preview of the document with dashed vertical lines marking where each tile boundary falls, so you can see the split before exporting.
Tiles: How many equal vertical slices to cut the design into. Each tile is the full height and one Nth of the width.
Format: The image format for the exported tiles. JPEG is smaller for photos; PNG keeps sharp edges and transparency.
Quality: Compression quality for JPEG tiles. Higher keeps more detail at a larger file size. Only shown when Format is JPEG.
Save as: Where the tiles go: a single ZIP download, or added straight to the media library as new images. Defaults to the ZIP download.
Tiles note: A read-only line showing the resulting tile count and each tile's exact pixel size (document width divided by tiles, full document height).
Cancel: Closes the dialog without exporting. Disabled while an export is running.
Export: Renders the master canvas, slices it into the chosen number of tiles, and either downloads the ZIP or creates the new library images. A toast reports how many tiles were exported.

sections.title: QR Code
sections.text:
Build a scannable QR code for links, Wi-Fi, contacts and more, styled to match your brand and inserted as an editable image layer.
The QR Code dialog turns a piece of content (a link, some text, an email, a phone number, an SMS, Wi-Fi login details or a contact card) into a QR code image. A live preview on the right updates as you type and shows warnings if a choice might hurt scannability.
The code lands as an ordinary image layer. All settings are stored on that layer, so you can reopen the dialog later with `Edit QR Code` from the context menu and change anything without starting over. Every content field also accepts dynamic variables like `{{post.url}}` that resolve per post when the design runs as a template.
Content: Chooses what the QR code encodes. Picking a type swaps the input fields below to match (for example a Wi-Fi network shows SSID and password fields).
Link (URL): The web address the code opens when scanned. Shown when Content is set to Link (URL).
Text: Plain text to encode when Content is set to Text. Scanners simply show this text, they do not open a link.
Email address: The recipient address for an Email code. Scanning it opens a new message to this address.
Subject (optional): Pre-fills the subject line of the email that opens when the code is scanned. Leave empty for none.
Message (optional): Pre-fills the body of the email (or the SMS text) that opens when the code is scanned. Optional.
Phone number: The number to call (Phone call code) or text (SMS code) when the code is scanned.
Network name (SSID): The Wi-Fi network name for a Wi-Fi access code. Scanning it lets a phone join the network without typing.
Password: The Wi-Fi password stored in the code. Leave blank if the network is open.
Security: The Wi-Fi encryption type so the phone connects correctly.
Hidden network: Tick this when the network does not broadcast its name, so the phone still finds it from the code.
First name / Last name: The contact's name for a Contact (vCard) code. Scanning it offers to save a new contact.
Company (optional): The organisation stored on the vCard contact. Optional.
Website (optional): A website address saved with the vCard contact. Optional (the vCard also has its own phone and email fields).
Insert variable: The small button next to each content field inserts a dynamic token such as `{{post.title}}`. The token resolves per post when the design runs as a dynamic template; the preview keeps the placeholder text.
Brand Kit: Applies a saved Brand Kit to the code: the darkest kit color becomes the code color, a second dark color becomes the eye accent, and the kit logo (if any) is offered as the center logo. Only shown when Brand Kits exist.
Code color: The color of the code's dark modules (the pattern itself). Keep it clearly darker than the background so cameras can read it.
Background: The color behind the code. Greyed out when Transparent background is on.
Transparent background: Drops the background fill so the code sits directly on whatever is beneath it. Make sure that surface stays light enough to scan.
Module style: The shape of the small squares (modules) that make up the code. Rounded and Dots look softer; Square is the most reliable to scan.
Eye style: The shape of the three large corner markers (the 'eyes') that scanners use to orient the code.
Eye color: An optional separate color for the three corner eyes. Use the Match code color button to clear it and fall back to the code color.
Center logo: Places an image in the middle of the code. Use the kit logo, choose an image file, or remove the current one. Adding a logo locks error correction to H so the code still scans.
Logo size: How much of the code the center logo covers. Larger logos look bolder but risk scannability, so the range is deliberately narrow.
Error correction: How much of the code can be damaged or covered and still read. Higher levels are more robust but make the pattern denser. Locked to H whenever a center logo is used.
Quiet zone: The blank margin around the code. Some scanners need this clear border, so keep at least Standard when placing the code on a busy background.
Preview and warnings: Shows the live code on a checkerboard (so transparency is visible) and lists scannability warnings, for example if the content is too long or colors are too close. Fill in the content to see it.
Insert QR code: Renders the code at high resolution and adds it as an image layer centered in the document (about 30% of the shorter side). When editing an existing code the button reads Update QR code.

sections.title: Chart & Table Studio
sections.text:
A three-zone studio that turns data into one of 35 chart and table types, inserted as a group of fully editable vector and text layers.
The left rail is a type gallery with rendered previews: 24 chart types and 11 table types. The center shows a live preview above a spreadsheet-style data grid, and the right rail holds design, color, series, options and text cards.
Everything the studio builds stays real layers, and the full data and settings are stored on the group: Edit in the context menu reopens the studio with everything intact. Cells and titles accept {{variable}} tokens, and a table imported from WordPress refreshes itself inside dynamic templates on export, batch runs and Preview with Post.
Type gallery: Rendered preview cards for every type, split into Charts and Tables. Switching the type swaps the sample data unless you have entered your own.
Data grid: A spreadsheet-style editor: the first row is the header, cells are edited in place and may hold several lines. Pasting from Excel or Google Sheets works, tabs are understood.
Column widths (drag): Drag the grip between two header cells to give a column more or less room in the finished table; double-click a grip to return it to automatic. The set widths travel with the design.
Add / remove rows and columns: Toolbar buttons extend or trim the grid; rows and columns can also be reordered.
Variables in cells: The { } button inserts a {{variable}} token at the focused cell: post fields, brand-kit values, site and date sources. Tokens resolve when the design is exported, batch-processed or previewed with a post.
Import (CSV file): Reads a .csv, .tsv or .txt file into the grid. With your own data already present the import asks before replacing it.
Import from WordPress: Builds the table from your content: pick a post type, the fields as columns, plus filters (search, category or any taxonomy, author, date range, custom field with compare, offset) and sorting. The field list is reorderable.
Refresh: Re-runs the saved WordPress query and replaces the rows. Inside dynamic templates this happens automatically on export, batch runs and Preview with Post; when a refresh fails the previous rows are kept.
Design cards: Ready-made looks rendered with the current type, plus random variations. A click applies the design; with a locked palette (brand colors on, or a picked kit or swatch set) a design changes geometry and typography only and never your colors.
Shuffle designs: Regenerates the random design tiles for a fresh set of looks.
Use brand colors: Locks the palette to your brand kit: the document's active kit first, then the site kit. While it is on, designs and shuffle never override the colors.
Colors / swatches: The working palette as editable swatches; + and − change the palette size (2 to 8 colors).
Colors from…: Fills the palette from a saved Brand Kit or Swatch set. The picked source is remembered on the chart and locks the palette, so designs and shuffle keep your colors; editing a swatch by hand releases the lock.
Random colors: Rolls a fresh harmonic scheme from the editor's color engine.
Series: One row per data series with its name and an optional fixed color that overrides the palette for that series.
Font: The editor's full font selector (brand, custom, system, editor and Google fonts, each previewed in its own face); the family applies to every text in the chart or table.
Title / Subtitle: Optional heading lines above the chart or table. Both accept {{variable}} tokens via the { } button.
Chart options: Type-dependent styling: card background, corner rounding, bar gap, grid lines, axes, outline, gradient fills, label and value weights, smooth curves, and number formatting (thousands separator, decimals).
Table geometry: Sliders for the table body: text wrapping with a maximum line count per cell, row height, cell padding, outer padding and header size. Long cells wrap instead of clipping.
Tiers (Pricing table): The pricing editor: name, price, period, feature list and call-to-action per tier, with one tier markable as Featured.
Insert / Update: Inserts the chart or table as an editable group; when editing an existing one the group is rebuilt in place with the stored size.

sections.title: Collage & Photo Grid
sections.text:
Arranges a handful of media-library photos into a collage and inserts it as an editable layer group.
Tools, Collage & Photo Grid opens a dialog with a live preview: pick images from your library, choose a layout and tune the look with a few sliders. Five layouts ship: a clean grid, a justified mosaic that keeps each photo close to its own aspect ratio, scattered polaroids with tilt and captions, a filmstrip with sprocket holes, and a contact sheet that labels every photo with its cleaned-up file name.
Inserting builds real layers: every photo is a normal image layer with a cover crop, cards and strips are shape layers, captions are text layers, all collected in one group. You can swap single pictures, nudge frames, restyle captions and apply layer styles afterwards.
Layouts: Grid, Mosaic, Polaroid, Filmstrip and Contact sheet. Mosaic justifies rows to the full width; Polaroid scatters tilted instant-photo cards; Contact sheet adds a file-name caption under every cell.
Spacing: The gap between photos and to the canvas edge, in pixels.
Corner radius: Rounds the photo corners. Polaroid photos stay square, the instant-photo look owns its corners.
Frame and Frame color: A matte card behind each photo, in any color. Polaroid always has its white card; the color swatch recolors it.
Columns: Fixes the column count for grid, contact sheet and polaroid layouts; 0 picks a count that keeps cells roughly square.
Shuffle: Deals a new seeded arrangement: the image order is reshuffled in every layout, and the polaroid scatter also re-rolls its tilt and offsets. The same document and settings always reproduce the same collage.
Captions from file names: For polaroid and contact sheet: labels every photo with its file name, extension stripped and dashes and underscores turned into spaces.
Insert collage: Builds the layers and selects the new group. Nothing is flattened; every part stays editable.

sections.title: 360° Panorama
sections.text:
Walk through any equirectangular image, repair the AI wrap seam, place linked hotspots and copy a fully self-contained HTML embed.
Tools, 360° Panorama opens a WebGL sphere viewer for equirectangular (2:1) images: drag to look around with a little inertia, scroll to change the field of view. The source can be any image layer of the document or a picture straight from the media library; a warning appears when the image is not close to 2:1.
The embed it copies is one self-contained HTML block: inline viewer, inline styles, hotspots included, the image URL as its only outside reference. It works in any Custom HTML block, with or without WunderPaint on the page, and keeps working if the plugin is ever removed.
Create with AI: Panorama creation lives right in the tool: describe a scene and generate a fresh 360° sphere, or click Turn source into 360° to rebuild the current source photo as a full panorama of the same place, light and mood. The result lands as a layer and opens in the viewer.
Source: Every image layer of the document appears in the picker; From library opens the media picker for any other panorama. Layers close to 2:1 are preselected.
Fix seam: AI panoramas typically drift in color across the width, so the left and right edges no longer match at the wrap. Per row the difference is measured and blended so the edges meet, plus a narrow blur band over the residual line. Apply to layer writes the repaired image back (undo restores it).
Add hotspot: Click in the view to place a marker: a text pill or an icon (pin, info, arrow, play) whose label appears on hover. Every hotspot has its own color and size, an optional URL, an optional info text that opens as a small card in the view, and Move re-places it with another click. All of it carries into the embed.
Copy embed HTML: Puts the self-contained viewer snippet on the clipboard, using the current view direction as the start view. The embed opens as a light blurred poster with a 360° badge and boots WebGL only when it scrolls into view or is clicked, so pages with several panoramas stay fast. Start with auto-rotate makes it turn slowly on its own; Embed height sets the block's CSS height.
360° generate format: In the AI panel's Format row, the 360° chip generates a seamless equirectangular sphere (prompt wrapper plus exact 2:1 resample) and inserts it as a layer, ready for this tool.
Viewer controls: Bottom right in both viewers: auto-rotate (slow turntable that pauses while you interact and resumes after a moment), a compass needle that shows the view direction and flies back to the start view when clicked, and fullscreen. Zoom by scroll, pinch or double-tap; camera moves are eased. On phones the embed adds a gyro button - move the device to look around.

sections.title: Color Schemer
sections.text:
Build a five-color scheme with color theory, from an image, or by chance, then save it site-wide and optionally push it into a Brand Kit.
The Color Schemer has five swatch slots driven by classic color-theory harmonies. Pick a base color and a harmony, then nudge spread, saturation and lightness to fine-tune. You can lock individual slots so they survive randomizing and slider changes.
