Colors can also be extracted from the current document or any media-library image. A live design preview shows how the scheme feels as background, card, text and buttons. Saved schemes become Swatch sets that appear in every color picker and in backups.
Swatch slot: One of five color slots that make up the scheme. Each shows its hex value; click a slot to open a color picker and edit it. A manual edit automatically locks that slot.
Lock / Unlock slot: The small padlock on each slot keeps that color fixed while you randomize or move the sliders. Unlock it to let the harmony rebuild that slot again.
Harmony: The color-theory relationship used to derive the scheme from the base color. Each harmony spaces the hues differently around the color wheel.
Base color: The anchor color the whole scheme is built from. Starts from the current foreground color.
Randomize: Generates a fresh, tasteful scheme by randomizing the base color and settings. Locked slots are kept.
From document: Extracts the five most important colors from the current design and fills the unlocked slots. Disabled when the document is empty.
From image…: Opens a media-library picker; choose an image and its main colors fill the unlocked slots. Loads more thumbnails on demand.
Saturation: Shifts the whole scheme more colorful or more muted. Rebuilds the unlocked slots.
Lightness: Shifts the whole scheme lighter or darker. Rebuilds the unlocked slots.
Spread: How far apart the harmony pushes the hues. Low keeps colors close together, high spreads them out.
Design preview: A live mock card showing the scheme in use as background, surface, text, and Primary and Secondary buttons, so you can judge how it works together.
Swatch set name: Names the scheme before saving. Leave blank to get an auto name like Palette 3.
Add / Update swatch set: Saves the five colors as a named Swatch set stored site-wide, so it shows up in every color picker and in backups. Saving with an existing name updates that set in place.
Apply to Brand Kit [Free]: Overwrites the colors of the chosen Brand Kit with this scheme. Asks for confirmation first. Only shown if you can manage kits and at least one kit exists.
Saved swatch sets (Load / Delete): Lists your saved sets with color previews. Load pulls a set back into the slots to keep editing; Delete removes it (with a confirm step).

sections.title: Background Studio
sections.text:
Generate a full-document background from four generative styles with sliders and a seed, all rendered locally with no cloud involved.
Background Studio makes deterministic, seed-based backgrounds in four styles: mesh gradient, organic, geometric and low-poly. Feed the color strip from a Brand Kit, a saved Swatch set, the current document, or chance, and shape the look with per-style sliders plus a grain overlay.
The result is inserted as a full-size raster layer at the bottom of the stack. All settings live on that layer, so `Edit Background` reopens the studio exactly as you left it. Tileable looks can also be saved as a seamless pattern.
Style: The generative background family. Each style shows its own set of sliders below.
Colors: The color strip the background is built from. Click a swatch to change it; use + and − to add or drop colors.
Colors from…: Fills the color strip from the current document's content colors, a Brand Kit, or a saved Swatch set. Only shows sources that exist.
Random colors: Replaces the strip with a fresh harmonious set from the color-scheme engine.
New variation: Rolls a new random seed, giving a different picture with the exact same style and settings.
Color points: How many color blobs the mesh gradient blends together. More points means a busier gradient. Shown for Mesh Gradient.
Softness: How smoothly the mesh colors bleed into each other. Higher is softer and more diffuse. Shown for Mesh Gradient.
Organic variant: Switches the Organic style between rounded Blobs and flowing Waves. This also changes the labels of the two sliders below.
Count / Bands: How many blobs (Blobs) or wave bands (Waves) are drawn. Labeled Count for Blobs and Bands for Waves.
Roundness / Amplitude: Shapes the organic forms: blob roundness in Blobs, or wave height in Waves. Labeled Roundness for Blobs and Amplitude for Waves.
Geometric variant: The repeating geometric motif for the Geometric style.
Size (Geometric): The size of each geometric element (dot, cell, stripe). Shown for the Geometric style.
Spacing (Geometric): The gap between geometric elements. Shown for the Geometric style.
Angle (Geometric): Rotates the geometric pattern. Shown for the Geometric style.
Cell size: The size of the triangular facets in the Low-Poly style. Larger cells mean fewer, bigger triangles. Shown for Low-Poly.
Variance: How irregular the low-poly triangles are. Higher is more jagged and random. Shown for Low-Poly.
Grain: Adds a subtle noise texture over the whole background to reduce banding and give a printed feel. Applies to every style.
Save as pattern: Saves the current look as a seamless, repeatable tile in the Asset Library under Patterns. Only offered for looks that tile cleanly (mesh, organic blobs, and the straight geometric lattices).
Insert background: Renders the background at full document size and adds it as the bottom layer. When editing an existing background the button reads Update background and re-renders in place.

sections.title: Screenshot Beautifier
sections.text:
Wrap a screenshot in a rounded card with shadow, optional browser, window or phone chrome, and a generated backdrop, all as editable layers in a new tab.
The Screenshot Beautifier frames the selected image layer or the whole flattened document in a rounded card with a shadow, adds optional device chrome or a decorative frame, grows the canvas with padding and aspect presets, and drops a backdrop behind it.
Everything opens as a fresh document in its own tab, grouped as editable layers, so your current work stays untouched. The backdrop keeps its Background Studio parameters, so Edit Background still works on it later.
Source: What to frame: the selected image layer, or the whole document flattened into one image. Options only appear when they are available.
Frame: The chrome drawn around the screenshot. Browser adds an address bar, Window a title bar, Phone a device body, Deco draws generative decorative shapes, None just uses the card.
Dark chrome: Switches the browser, window or phone chrome to a dark theme. Shown for those three frames.
Address bar text: The text shown in the browser frame's address bar. Shown only for the Browser frame.
Deco variant: The style of decorative frame when Frame is set to Deco. Offset panes stacks tilted panes behind the card, Ring draws an outline halo, Corners adds corner accents.
Strength (Deco): How pronounced the decorative frame is. Shown for the Deco frame.
Angle (Deco): The tilt of the offset panes. Shown only for the Offset panes deco variant.
Deco colors / Randomize: Two color swatches for the decorative frame, with Colors from… (Brand Kit or Swatch set) and a Randomize button that also reseeds the deco pattern.
Padding: The breathing room between the screenshot card and the canvas edge, as a percentage of the card size.
Corner radius: How rounded the corners of the screenshot card are.
Shadow: The strength of the drop shadow under the card, giving it lift off the backdrop.
Card border: A subtle outline around the card. Zero means no border.
Canvas format: The shape of the output canvas. Original keeps the screenshot's aspect plus padding; the presets crop the canvas to common ratios.
Backdrop: What sits behind the card: a generated Background Studio scene, a single solid color, or transparent.
Backdrop style (Studio): The Background Studio style used for the backdrop, with color swatches, Colors from… and a New variation button. Shown when Backdrop is Background Studio.
Solid color (Backdrop): The single background color when Backdrop is set to Solid color.
Beautify screenshot: Builds the framed composition and opens it as a new document in its own tab, grouped as editable layers. Your current document is left untouched.

sections.title: Mockup Generator
sections.text:
Place your artwork or the whole document onto a studio product mockup (ebook, box, DVD, CD, report or monitor), rendered locally as a transparent-background image layer.
The Mockup Generator wraps the selected layer or the flattened document around a small 3D product shape, lit and shaded in the browser with no cloud involved. Six product types are available and the shape adapts to your artwork's aspect ratio.
The baked result is a normal image layer with a transparent background, so it drops onto any design. Parameters and the artwork are stored on the layer, so `Edit Mockup` reopens this dialog and re-renders in place.
Mockup: The product shape your artwork is placed on. The shape adapts to the aspect ratio of your artwork.
Source: Which image to wrap onto the mockup: the artwork stored on the layer (when editing), the selected image layer, or the whole document flattened. Only available options are shown.
Camera presets: One-click camera angles that set the Angle and Tilt together. Front is nearly straight-on, Classic is a gentle three-quarter view, Steep is a dramatic angle.
Angle: Rotates the product left or right (yaw). Positive values turn the spine or side into view.
Tilt: Tips the product forward or back (pitch). Positive values look slightly down onto the object.
Light: Moves the key light from left to right, changing which side is brightest.
Gloss: The sheen on plastic and glass fronts. Higher values add a stronger highlight.
Shadow: The strength of the ground shadow under the product.
Material: The color of the product's spine, sides or bezel. Pick any color, or click one of the Brand Kit chips shown beside the swatch.
Output: Where the finished mockup goes: added into the current document, or opened as a new document tab. Only shown when inserting a new mockup (not when editing).
Insert mockup: Bakes the mockup at high resolution with a transparent background and adds it (or opens it in a new tab). When editing, the button reads Update mockup and re-renders in place, keeping the box width and following the new aspect ratio.

sections.title: Contrast Check
sections.text:
Rate every visible text layer against the pixels actually behind it and flag any that fall below the WCAG contrast recommendation.
The Contrast Check dialog scans all visible text layers, measures each one's color against whatever lies underneath it in the design, and reports a WCAG contrast ratio. It runs automatically when opened.
A summary tells you how many layers fall short, and each result row can be clicked to jump straight to that text layer so you can fix it.
Checking text layers: The automatic scan that runs when the dialog opens. It composites what is beneath each text layer and computes the real contrast ratio. Shows a spinner while working.
Summary line: A one-line verdict: either how many text layers fall below the WCAG contrast recommendation, or that all layers meet it. Reads 'No visible text layers to check' when there is no text.
Contrast result row: One row per text layer showing its text-color swatch, the layer name, and the measured contrast ratio. Click a row to select that layer and close the dialog so you can adjust it.
Ratio and pass / fail: The measured contrast shown as a ratio (for example 4.7:1). A passing layer shows a check mark; a failing one shows the ratio it still needs to reach, for example '(needs 4.5:1)'.

sections.title: Blur Faces
sections.text:
Find every face on the active layer and pixelate it beyond recognition, in your browser, with no key.
Blur Faces runs on the local Florence-2 model. The model is asked to ground the phrase "human face" in the image, each box it returns is padded a little, and those regions are pixelated straight into the layer. The picture never leaves your site.
The result replaces the content of the active layer as a single undo step, so one Undo takes it back if a false positive lands somewhere you did not want it.
Blur Faces: Runs the detection and pixelates every face it finds on the active layer. A toast reports how many faces were made unrecognizable.
Needs the local caption model: Blur Faces uses the Florence-2 caption model for detection. Until it is installed under Settings, Local AI Models, the action says so instead of running.
No faces found on the active layer: The model grounded nothing for "human face". The layer is left untouched. Check that an image layer is active rather than a text or shape layer.

sections.title: Depth Blur (background)
sections.text:
Estimate a depth map for the active layer and add a graduated depth-of-field blur that keeps the focus sharp while melting the background away.
Depth Blur estimates how far each part of the image is from the camera, then blurs by distance so the subject stays crisp and the background softens like a wide-aperture lens. The depth estimation runs locally with a self-hosted Depth Anything model.
A live preview updates as you move the Focus depth and Strength sliders. Apply bakes the blur into the layer. If the depth model is not installed yet, the dialog links to Settings to download it.
Focus depth: Chooses which depth stays sharp: lower keeps near objects in focus, higher keeps far ones sharp. It starts at an automatically detected focus point.
Strength: How strong the background blur gets. Higher values give a more dramatic, shallow-depth-of-field look.
Preview: A live canvas showing the blurred result as you move the sliders, so you can dial in the effect before committing.
Apply: Bakes the current blur into the active layer, replacing its content. The button reads Applying… while it works.
Model not installed notice: Shown when the local Depth model has not been downloaded yet. It explains where to get it (Settings, then WunderPaint, then Local AI Models) and links straight to Settings.

sections.title: QR code content types and Wi-Fi security
sections.text:
The Content dropdown chooses what the finished QR code holds, and each type reveals its own fields.
Link (URL) and Text are the two simplest types (documented with their fields). The remaining choices below build special payloads so a phone scan does the right thing (start an email, dial, connect to Wi-Fi, save a contact).
Email: Content type that builds a `mailto:` code. Reveals the **Email address**, **Subject (optional)** and **Message (optional)** fields, so a scan opens a pre-filled email.
Phone call: Builds a `tel:` code so a scan offers to dial the number. Reveals the **Phone number** field.
SMS: Builds an SMS code. A scan opens a new text message to the number, optionally pre-filled with the **Message**.
Wi-Fi access: Encodes network join details so a scan connects to Wi-Fi without typing. Reveals Network name (SSID), Password, Security and Hidden network.
Contact (vCard): Encodes a contact card. A scan offers to save the person. Reveals first and last name, Company, Phone, Email and Website fields.
WPA/WPA2/WPA3: Default Wi-Fi security for the code. Use this for almost every modern router.
WEP: Legacy Wi-Fi security. Only pick this for very old networks that still use it.
Open (no password): For networks that have no password. The Password field is ignored when this is chosen.

sections.title: QR code module, eye and logo options
sections.text:
The exact choices inside the Module style and Eye style controls, plus the buttons that manage the center logo.
Square: Module style that draws sharp square pixels. The classic and most compatible QR look.
Rounded: Module style that softens every pixel into a rounded square for a friendlier feel.
Dots: Module style that renders each pixel as a small dot. The most decorative option, so test it with a phone after export.
Square: Eye style that keeps the three finder eyes (the big corner markers) as plain squares.
Rounded: Eye style that rounds the corners of the three finder eyes.
Match code color: Clears a separate Eye color so the finder eyes reuse the main Code color. This button appears only after you have set a custom eye color.
Use kit logo: Drops the current Brand Kit logo into the center of the code. Shown only when the selected kit has a logo.
Choose image…: Uploads any image from your computer to sit in the middle of the code.
Remove logo: Removes the center logo. Shown only when a logo is set.

sections.title: QR error correction and quiet zone options
sections.text:
The individual levels in the Error correction dropdown and the sizes in the Quiet zone dropdown.
L (7%, smallest code): Error correction level L. Least redundancy, so the smallest and densest code. Best for short data and clean printing.
M (15%, default): Error correction level M, the default. A balanced amount of redundancy for everyday use.
Q (25%): Error correction level Q. More redundancy, so the code survives more damage or dirt at the cost of density.
H (30%, most robust): Error correction level H, the most robust. Survives the most damage and is required when a logo covers part of the code.
None: Quiet zone option with no blank margin around the code. Risky, because many scanners need the border to lock on.
Narrow: A thin blank margin around the code.
Standard: The standard blank margin, on by default. The safe choice for reliable scanning.
Wide: A generous blank margin around the code.

sections.title: QR Brand Kit picker, variables and Update
sections.text:
The small controls around the QR dialog: the Brand Kit dropdown items, the variables notice and the edit-mode button label.
No Brand Kit: Top item of the Brand Kit dropdown. Leaves the code colors and logo as they are instead of pulling from a kit.
Edit Brand Kits: Pencil button next to the Brand Kit dropdown. Opens the Brand Kits manager so you can change kit colors and logo without leaving the QR dialog.
Variables resolve per post: Notice that appears when any field contains a `{{token}}`. The live preview keeps the placeholder text. In the free plugin the token resolves against a real post on export and under View, then Preview with Post. Running the design over many posts, or embedding it as a dynamic image block or shortcode, is part of Pro.
Update QR code: Edit-mode label of the primary button. When you reopen a code through **Edit QR Code**, it rebuilds the existing layer in place instead of inserting a new one.

sections.title: Chart types
sections.text:
Every chart choice in the Type dropdown's Charts group.
The Type dropdown is split into two groups, Charts and Tables. These are the nine Charts entries. Data is entered as `Label, value, value` rows (pasting from Excel or Sheets works).
Bars: Vertical bar chart, one bar per row. Extra numeric columns become grouped bars side by side.
Bars (horizontal): Bars drawn sideways. Good when your category names are long.
Stacked bars: Stacks each series on top of the previous one, so a bar shows a total split into parts.
Line: Line chart with one line per series. Good for trends over time.
Area: Line chart with the area under each line filled in.
Pie: Pie chart of a single series, one slice per row.
Donut: Pie with a hollow center. The Thickness slider sets the ring width.
Radar: Spider chart that compares several series across the same set of axes.
Progress rings: One ring per row, each showing a percentage toward a goal. Thickness sets the ring width.

sections.title: Table types
sections.text:
The Tables group of the Type dropdown holds eleven choices. The three below are the ones whose editor changes shape; the rest (Ranking, Schedule, Checklist, Menu / price list, Spec sheet, Scorecard, Timeline and Matrix) are data grids with their own styling.
Data table: A plain data grid. The first row becomes the column headers, and each following row is a record.
Comparison table: A feature comparison grid with yes and no style cells and an optional highlighted column.
Pricing table: Pricing tiers shown as cards. Choosing this switches the editor from a data box to the tier builder.

sections.title: Chart and table option lists
sections.text:
Every choice inside the Value labels, Header, Rows, Frame, Density and Marks dropdowns.
Off: Value labels option that shows no numbers on the chart.
Values: Value labels option that prints the raw number on each bar, point or slice.
Percent: Value labels option that prints each figure as a percentage of the total.
Solid: Header style with a solid color band behind the column titles.
Gradient: Header style with a color gradient band. Choosing it also switches the gradient fill on.
Underline: Header style with just an underline beneath the titles, no fill.
None: Header style with no special header treatment.
Zebra: Row style that alternates a faint background every other row for easier reading.
Lines: Row style that separates rows with thin divider lines.
Plain: Row style with no zebra shading and no dividers.
Cards: Row style that renders each row as a separate card.
None: Frame option with no border or container around the table.
Outline: Frame option with a thin outline around the whole table.
Soft: Frame option with a soft, subtle container.
Dark: Frame option with a dark container behind the table.
Compact: Density option with tight row height, fitting more rows in less space.
Normal: Default row height.
Roomy: Density option with generous row height and more breathing room.
Check: Marks style that shows a check for yes cells in a comparison table.
Badge: Marks style that shows a filled badge for yes cells.
Dot: Marks style that shows a small dot for yes cells.

sections.title: Pricing tier editor fields
sections.text:
The per-tier fields that appear when a tier is expanded in the Pricing table editor.
Each tier is a collapsible row. Click a row to open its fields. The tier list is capped at 5 tiers, and you cannot remove the last one.
Name: The tier's title, for example Starter or Pro. Also shown on the collapsed row.
Price: The headline price text for the tier, for example `€29`. Free text, so any currency works.
Period: The billing period shown under the price, for example per month.
One feature per line: Multi-line box listing the tier's features. Put one feature on each line and it becomes one bullet.
Button (optional): Call-to-action button label for the tier, for example Choose or Contact us. Leave empty for no button.
Remove tier: The minus button on a tier row deletes that tier. Disabled when only one tier is left.

sections.title: Color Schemer harmonies
sections.text:
Every rule in the Harmony dropdown that decides how the swatches relate to the base color.
Analogous: Colors that sit next to each other on the wheel. Calm and cohesive.
Complementary: The base color plus its opposite on the wheel. High contrast and punchy.
Split complementary: The base color plus the two colors either side of its opposite. Contrast with less tension.
Triadic: Three colors spaced evenly around the wheel. Balanced and vivid.
Tetradic: Four colors in two complementary pairs. Rich but harder to balance.
Monochromatic: One hue in several saturations and lightnesses. Very unified.
Shades & tints: The base hue stepped from dark shades to light tints.

sections.title: Color Schemer picker and confirm states
sections.text:
Smaller Color Schemer controls: the media picker, the kit target selector and the two-step confirm buttons.
More…: Loads the next page of media library images inside the From image… picker. Reads Loading… while fetching.
Brand Kit selector: Dropdown next to Apply to Brand Kit choosing which kit receives the scheme. Only visible when you can manage kits and at least one kit exists.
Really overwrite the kit colors?: The confirm state of Apply to Brand Kit. The button turns into this warning first, so you click twice to actually overwrite the kit's colors.
Really delete?: The confirm state of a saved swatch set's Delete button. Click again to remove the set for good.

sections.title: Background Studio styles
sections.text:
The four top-level looks in the Background Studio style switch.
Mesh Gradient: Smooth multi-color gradient blended between color points. The softest, most modern background. Tiles seamlessly.
Organic: Flowing blob or wave shapes. Choose the Blobs or Waves variant below.
Geometric: Repeating dots, grid, stripes or rays. Choose the variant and set size, spacing and angle.
Low-Poly: A faceted, triangulated surface. Set cell size and how much the facets vary.

sections.title: Background Studio variants
sections.text:
The variant choices inside the Organic and Geometric styles.
Blobs: Organic variant of soft rounded blobs. Count sets how many, Roundness sets how smooth. Tiles seamlessly.
Waves: Organic variant of layered wave bands. Bands sets how many, Amplitude sets the height.
Dots: Geometric variant of a dot grid.
Grid: Geometric variant of a line grid.
Stripes: Geometric variant of parallel stripes, angled by the Angle slider.
Rays: Geometric variant of rays fanning from a point.

sections.title: Beautifier source, frame and deco options
sections.text:
The choices inside the Screenshot Beautifier's Source, Frame and Deco switches.
Selected image layer: Source option that wraps the currently selected image layer (or the bottom-most one).
Whole document (flattened): Source option that flattens the entire document to one picture and frames that.
None: Frame option with no browser or window chrome, just the card and shadow.
Browser: Frame option that adds a browser chrome with an address bar. Reveals the Dark chrome toggle and Address bar text.
Window: Frame option that adds a plain app window chrome with a title bar. Reveals the Dark chrome toggle.
Phone: Frame option that wraps the shot in a phone body. Reveals the Dark chrome toggle.
Deco: Frame option that adds a generative decorative frame instead of chrome. Reveals the deco variant, Strength, Angle and deco colors.
Offset panes: Deco variant with offset color panes behind the card. The Angle slider skews them.
Ring: Deco variant that draws a colored ring around the card.
Corners: Deco variant that adds decorative accents to the card corners.

sections.title: Beautifier canvas format and backdrop options
sections.text:
The Canvas format choices and the three Backdrop modes.
Original + padding: Canvas format that keeps the shot's own aspect ratio and just adds the padding you set.
16:9: Canvas format that fits the framed shot into a 16:9 canvas, good for slides and video thumbnails.
4:3: Canvas format that fits the shot into a 4:3 canvas.
1:1: Canvas format that fits the shot into a square canvas, good for social posts.
OG / social card (1.91:1): Canvas format sized 1.91:1, the Open Graph link-preview ratio for social shares.
Background Studio: Backdrop mode that puts a generative Background Studio fill behind the card. Reveals a style dropdown, color swatches and New variation.
Transparent: Backdrop mode with no fill behind the card, so it sits on a transparent canvas.
New variation: Reseeds the Background Studio backdrop for a fresh look while keeping the same style and colors. Only shown for the Background Studio backdrop.

sections.title: Mockup product types
sections.text:
The six product shapes in the Mockup switch.
The shape adapts to the aspect ratio of your artwork, so a tall image and a wide image produce differently proportioned products.
Ebook: Renders the artwork as a standing ebook or book cover.
Software box: Renders the artwork on a boxed software package.
DVD case: Renders the artwork on a DVD case.
CD case: Renders the artwork on a CD jewel case.
Report: Renders the artwork as a printed report or document stack.
Monitor: Renders the artwork on a computer monitor screen.

sections.title: Mockup source, camera and output options
sections.text:
The Source choices, the camera presets, the Material kit swatches and the two Output modes.
Stored artwork: Source option that reuses the exact artwork saved on the mockup layer. Only offered in edit mode.
Selected image layer: Source option that puts the currently selected image layer onto the product.
Whole document (flattened): Source option that flattens the whole document and uses that as the artwork.
Front: Camera preset for a nearly straight-on view.
Classic: Camera preset for the standard three-quarter product angle.
Steep: Camera preset for a dramatic, strongly turned angle.
Material kit swatches: Small color chips from the active Brand Kit shown next to the Material color. Click one to recolor the product body to that kit color.
Into this document: Output option that drops the finished mockup as an image layer into the current document.
New document tab: Output option that opens the mockup as its own new document in a separate tab, leaving your current work untouched.

sections.title: Contrast Check and Depth Blur extras
sections.text:
The remaining states and links in the Contrast Check and Depth Blur dialogs.
No visible text layers to check: Message shown by Contrast Check when there are no visible text layers, so there is nothing to rate.
Contrast swatch: The small color square at the start of each Contrast Check row, showing that layer's text color.
Open Settings: Link in the Depth Blur model-missing notice. Opens Settings so you can download the Depth model, then reopen the dialog.
Applying…: Label the Depth Blur Apply button shows while it bakes the blur into the layer.

sections.title: Shared studio dialog buttons
sections.text:
The common buttons that every studio and generator dialog shares.
These controls behave the same across the QR, Chart, Color Schemer, Background Studio, Beautifier, Mockup, Contrast, Split and Depth Blur dialogs.
Cancel: Closes the dialog and discards its settings without changing your design.
Close: The X button in the top-right corner. Same effect as Cancel or pressing Escape.
Update (vs Insert): When you reopen a studio through **Edit …** in a layer's context menu, the primary button reads Update instead of Insert and rebuilds the existing layer or group in place rather than adding a new one.

sections.title: Asset Library tray
sections.text:
The collapsible dock under the canvas for fast, one-click inserting of assets.
The tray is the fast path to the Asset Library. It sits under the canvas, stays open so you can drop several assets in a row, and remembers whether it was open and which section you last used.
Every tile can be clicked to insert, or dragged straight onto the canvas. Where a section shows your own saved items, hold **Alt** and click a tile to remove it.
Asset Library: The label at the left of the tray head, naming the dock. It does not do anything on its own; the chips next to it choose what the tray shows.
Recent: Lists the assets you inserted most recently, newest first, across every source. Use it to reinsert something you just placed without searching for it again.
My Assets: Your own saved layer snapshots, made with `File`, then `Save as Asset`. Click to insert; Alt-click removes an item.
Dynamic Templates: Your saved dynamic templates. Clicking one opens it as a new document (next to your current work when tabs are on).
Starter Templates: The fully editable starting points that ship with the plugin, plus any templates added by installed extension packs. Clicking one opens it as a new document.
Brand Kits: One tile per Brand Kit that has a logo. Clicking a tile inserts that kit's logo as a layer.
Buttons & Badges: Styled text-and-shape button and badge combinations. Clicking one inserts the group so you can edit each line. This is the tray's default section on first open.
Headlines: Ready-made headline text combinations. Insert one, then edit each line on the canvas.
Lists: Pre-styled list layouts as text groups. Insert, then replace the placeholder lines.
Quotes & Reviews: Quote and review text combinations with attribution lines. Insert and edit in place.
Sales & Prices: Sale, price and offer text groups built around a number or discount. Insert and edit.
Events & News: Event and news text combinations (name, date, venue and similar). Insert and edit.
Stats & Numbers: KPI callouts, comparisons and mini bar-chart text groups. Insert and edit the figures.
Shapes: Vector shape elements (arrows, blobs, badges and more) plus any shapes you saved. Click to insert centered; Alt-click removes a saved one.
Backgrounds: Full-canvas fills: gradient presets, solid colors (including your Brand Kit colors) and any backgrounds you saved. Inserts as the bottom layer.
Icons: The Tabler icon set as line icons. Scroll or filter, then click to insert; the strip loads more as you reach its end.
Emoji: The full emoji set as text glyphs. Filter by name, then click to insert. Loads more as you scroll.
Photos [Free]: Free stock photos from your configured provider. Browse the category cards or type in the tray search; results stream in with infinite scroll and insert as layers.
Illustrations: Free illustrations from Pixabay. Only appears when a Pixabay API key is configured. [Requires: Pixabay API key]
Vectors: Free vector graphics from Pixabay. Only appears when a Pixabay API key is configured. [Requires: Pixabay API key]
Media Library: Images already in your WordPress media library. Click to insert; from three characters the search also ranks by meaning when the image search model is installed.
Filter search field: The search box in the tray head. It filters the current section; in Photos, Illustrations and Vectors it drives the provider search instead, and its placeholder changes to match.
Asset Generators [AI]: Opens the AI Generate dialog seeded to a type that matches the current section: text for a text category, shape for Shapes, otherwise gradient.
Open Asset Library: Opens the full Asset Library dialog on the current section. Photo, illustration, vector and recent sections open on the dialog's Media Library section.
Collapse / Expand: The chevron at the far right opens or closes the tray body. Clicking the active chip again also collapses the tray.
Drag onto canvas: Every tile is draggable. Drag it from the tray and drop it on the canvas to insert at that spot instead of centered.
Alt-click to remove: In the sections that show your own saved items (My Assets, Shapes, Backgrounds, Text), hold Alt and click a tile to delete that saved item.
Category cards (Starter Templates): With the tray search empty, the Starter Templates strip shows one card per template category instead of hundreds of tiles. Each card is previewed with the first template of that category and its tooltip names the category and how many templates it holds. Categories with no templates are skipped, and categories added by installed template packs get a card too.
Drill into a category: Click a category card and the strip switches to the templates of that category, bundled ones and pack ones together. Click a template to open it as a new document.
All categories (back tile): The leading grid tile shown while you are inside a category. Click it to leave the drill-in and return to the category cards.
Tray search in Starter Templates: Typing in the tray search leaves the category cards and lists matching templates directly. It uses the same matcher as the library dialog, so it hits the template name, the copy on its text layers, its category and its dominant color names: "red menu" works. With no category picked, a search word that matches a pack's own name also brings in that pack's templates.
No matches.: The hint shown in the strip when the current search or category leaves no templates. Clear the search or use the All categories tile to get back.
WordArt: Hand-crafted multi-layer word-art lockups; inserting one adds a fully editable group of text layers.

sections.title: Asset Library (full dialog)
sections.text:
The full-screen library modal with a left sidebar of sources and a search across everything you have saved.
The dialog opens from `Assets`, then `Library` (or the tray's Open Asset Library button). The left sidebar lists every source; the header search runs a live hero search across all asset titles at once.
Each sidebar section shows a card grid you can click to insert or, for templates and designs, to open as a new document.
Search all assets [Local AI]: The header search box. Typing runs a live search across designs, media, starters, your assets, text, shapes, backgrounds, icons, emoji and extension packs at once, grouped by source. When the image search model is installed it also ranks your media library by meaning.
Designs: Your layered working files, saved via `File`, then `Save Design`. Open one as a new document; each card also has Duplicate, Move to folder, Rename and Delete buttons, and a Folder dropdown filters the list when designs have folders.
My Assets: Your saved layer snapshots, organised into your own categories. Tabs across the top switch category (All, each category, Unsorted); each category has rename and delete tools, and there is a New category button.
Dynamic Templates: Your saved dynamic templates, grouped per Brand Kit with a "Without Brand Kit" group for the rest. Click to open as a new document; each card has a Delete button.
Starter Templates: The bundled, fully editable starter templates plus installed extension template packs (each pack under its own heading). Click to open as a new document.
Text (styled combinations): The seven text-combination categories are each a sidebar section: Buttons & Badges, Headlines, Lists, Quotes & Reviews, Sales & Prices, Events & News, Stats & Numbers. Insert a group, then edit each line. Your own saved text appears first with Alt-click to remove.
Shapes: Vector shape elements grouped into sets, sized to about 30% of the canvas and filled with the foreground color on insert. Your saved shapes show first with Alt-click to remove.
Backgrounds: Full-canvas fills inserted as the bottom layer. Sub-groups are Gradients, Patterns (dots, stripes, checker, grid, diagonal, crosshatch, zigzag, waves, bricks, plus, triangles, scales), Solid colors (Brand Kit colors plus neutrals) and your saved backgrounds.
Media Library: A paged grid of images from your WordPress media library. Click to insert centered and fitted; Load more pages in as you scroll. The search index hint shows if semantic indexing is available.
Icons: The Tabler icon set. Search by name; the count shows how many match. Icons insert as stroked shape layers in the foreground color. "Show more" (or scrolling) reveals additional pages.
Emoji: The emoji set with a name search and a category dropdown (All categories plus each group). The count shows matches. Emoji insert as a centered text layer.
Patterns: Small seamless tile images that fill shapes and the Pattern Overlay layer style. This section is dialog-only. Upload a pattern (named, downscaled to 256 px max) or delete existing ones; patterns embed into saved documents.
Brand Kits: One logo tile per Brand Kit that has a logo; clicking inserts that logo as a layer. If no kit has a logo, a Manage Brand Kits button opens the kit editor.
Sidebar section list: The left rail listing every source. Clicking a section clears the header search and shows that section's grid. Installed extension packs add their own sections here, matching the tray chips.
Close: Closes the dialog. Pressing Escape does the same.
Search templates…: The search box above the starter templates. It matches the template name, the copy written on its text layers, its category and the names of its dominant colors, so "summer" finds a template whose headline says Summer even when its name does not. Every word you type must match, so adding words narrows the grid.
%d templates (count): The readout next to the template search. It counts what is currently visible: the matching bundled starters plus the matching templates of every installed pack.
Category chips (starter templates): An All chip plus one chip per template category above the grid. Click a chip to show only that category, click it again for All. Built-in categories come first, categories declared by installed template packs follow.
Color dots (starter templates): Twelve round swatches at the right of the chip row, labelled with the raw bucket name. Click one to keep only templates whose dominant palette contains that color, click the active one again to clear it. The buckets match the Media Library Manager's color swatches.
Pack headings follow the filters: Extension template packs are filtered by the same chips, dots and search. A pack heading and its grid only appear while at least one of its templates still matches.

sections.title: Media Library Manager: folders, tags & smart folders
sections.text:
The left rail of the Media Library Manager for organising media into folders, tags and saved smart folders.
The Media Library Manager is a full-screen, free manager for your WordPress media library. Its left rail holds real hierarchical folders, tags, smart folders and the tools menu.
Drag image tiles from the grid onto a folder (or onto All images to remove them from folders) to move them.
All images: The top rail entry showing every image, unfiltered. Dropping selected tiles here removes them from any folder.
Folders: A hierarchical taxonomy of real folders shown as an indented tree, each with its image count. Click a folder to view it; drag tiles onto it to move them in.
New folder: The plus button in the Folders header creates a top-level folder after you name it.
New subfolder: The plus button on a folder row creates a child folder under it.
Rename folder: The pencil button on a folder row renames that folder.
Delete folder: The trash button on a folder row deletes the folder after a confirm. The images stay in your library.
Tags: Flat tag terms with counts. Click a tag to filter to it. A preview of the first six is shown, with a toggle to reveal the rest.
Tag list / cloud view: The grid/list button in the Tags header switches between a chip list (with counts and delete buttons) and a size-weighted tag cloud where bigger tags have more images.
New tag: The plus button in the Tags header creates a new tag term after you name it.
Delete tag: The small x on a tag chip deletes that tag after a confirm. The images stay in your library.
Show all tags: Expands the tag list from the six-item preview to all tags, and back with Show fewer.
Missing alt text: A built-in smart folder listing every image with no alt text. A "Fill with Metadata Assistant" button appears in its toolbar to fix them in bulk.
Unused: A built-in smart folder listing images that are not attached to or used by any content.
Reclaim space: A built-in smart folder that sorts by biggest file first and shows a running total of the space on screen, so you can find and trash the heaviest files.
Saved smart folders: Your own saved filters and saved semantic searches. Each has a delete button; semantic ones re-run their query when opened.
Index status / Index now [Local AI]: A footer readout of how many images are not yet searchable, with an Index now button to build the semantic index. Shows live progress while indexing.
Media Library Tools: The button at the bottom of the rail that opens the tools menu (suggest folders, find duplicates, regenerate thumbnails, rename by pattern, find broken, generate metadata).

sections.title: Media Library Manager: search, filters, sort & grid
sections.text:
The main pane of the Media Library Manager: a semantic search, structured filters, sorting and a multi-select image grid.
The main pane combines a meaning-based search with structured filters (type, file type, orientation, size and color) and sorting. Filters compose with a search, so you can rank by meaning and still narrow by color or shape.
Click tiles to select (Shift-click for a range), hover to read title and alt, and use the pencil on a tile to open the per-image editor.
Search images by what they show [Local AI]: The header search. It ranks your indexed library by meaning (for example "dog on the beach"), so file names do not matter. Debounces while typing and runs on Enter; a clear button resets to All images.
Save as smart folder: Appears in the toolbar during a semantic search. Saves the current query as a reusable smart folder in the left rail.
Sort: Orders the grid. Options are Newest, Oldest, Title A-Z, Largest, Smallest and Biggest file.
Media type: Filters by what kind of media to show: Images, Videos, Audio, Documents or All media.
File type: Restricts to one file format: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, SVG or PDF.
Orientation: Filters by image shape.
Size: Filters by pixel dimensions bucket.
Color swatches: A row of color buttons that filters the grid to images whose dominant color falls in that bucket. Click the active swatch again to clear it. Colors are precomputed in the background.
Reset: Clears all active filters and the sort back to defaults. Only shown when a filter or non-default sort is active.
Upload: Opens a file picker to add images or PDFs. Dropping files onto the main pane starts the same import flow.
Select all: Selects every image currently loaded in the grid.
Clear: Deselects everything.
Image tile: One image in the grid. Click to select, Shift-click to select a range. Shows a checkmark when selected, a "no alt" badge when it lacks alt text, and its title and alt on hover.
Edit metadata (tile): The pencil button on a tile opens the per-image metadata editor for that image.
Load more: Loads the next page of results. The grid also loads more automatically as you scroll near the end (except in ranked search results).
View name and count: The toolbar readout showing the current view's name and how many images or results it holds. In Reclaim space it also totals the file size shown.
Fill with Metadata Assistant: Appears in the Missing alt text smart folder. Opens the Metadata Assistant pre-filtered to images without alt text.

sections.title: Large preview
sections.text:
The full-screen view behind the eye icon on a tile, with arrows to step through the current results.
Opens over the Media Library Manager and shows the file at full size. Images, video and audio play in place, PDFs open in a frame, and any other document offers a link to open it.
Opening it: The eye icon on a tile, or the same action from the tile menu.
Previous and next: Arrows at the left and right edge of the window step through the current result list, in whatever order and filtering the grid is showing. They keep a fixed position regardless of how wide the picture is, so you can click through a folder without moving the pointer. The left and right arrow keys do the same.
Insert into design: Places the image into the open document as a new layer and closes the preview. Shown for images.
Copy file URL: Copies the address of the original file to the clipboard.
Download: Saves the original file to your computer under its own file name. This is the untouched original, not a size generated from it.
Edit metadata: Closes the preview and opens the detail editor for this image, where title, alt text, tags, usage, origin and file data live.
Close: Closes the preview. Clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape does the same.

sections.title: Media Library Manager: selection & bulk actions
sections.text:
The bulk bar that appears when images are selected, for moving, tagging, featuring, inserting, downloading or deleting them.
Selecting one or more tiles reveals the bulk bar at the bottom of the main pane. It acts on the whole selection at once.
N selected: A live readout of how many images are in the current selection.
Move to folder: Moves the selected images into a folder from the dropdown. Includes a No folder option to remove them from folders.
Add tag: Adds the chosen tag to every selected image.
Remove tag: Removes the chosen tag from every selected image.
Auto-tag [AI, Cloud AI]: Uses your cloud provider to generate tags, mood and text for each selected image, creating any missing tags and filling empty alt, caption and description. Shows live progress.
Find similar [Local AI]: With exactly one image selected, ranks the library by visual similarity to it. Needs the image search model. [Requires: Exactly one selected]
Featured image: With exactly one image selected, opens the post picker to set that image as a post's or page's featured image. [Requires: Exactly one selected]
Insert into design: Adds the selected images as layers in the current document, each offset slightly, then closes the manager.
Download: Downloads each selected image to your computer using its title as the file name.
Delete: Moves the selected images to the trash after a confirm. Their files stay on disk for a grace period, and you can bring them back under "Clean up the library".

sections.title: Media Library Tools
sections.text:
The tools menu and its sub-dialogs for tidying the library: suggest folders, find duplicates, regenerate thumbnails, rename by pattern, find broken and generate metadata.
Opened from the Media Library Tools button in the rail. Some tools need the image search model (suggest folders, find duplicates) and are disabled with a hint until it is installed.
Suggest folders [Local AI]: Groups visually similar images into clusters you can turn into folders. Name a group to create it; the panel offers Auto-name (captions the representative image with your cloud provider) and Create all.
Find duplicates [Local AI]: Finds near-identical images and groups them. It pre-marks all but the first of each group for trashing; click any image to flip keep or trash, then trash the marked ones per group.
Regenerate thumbnails: Rebuilds the intermediate image sizes for the selected images. Select images first, then run it. [Requires: A selection]
Rename by pattern: Sets the title of the selected images from a text pattern. Use ### for a zero-padded counter and the { } button to insert variables (brand, site, image dimensions and more); a live preview shows the first few results.
Find broken files: Scans for media whose underlying file is missing or unreadable and lists the results as a ranked view. Reports when none are found.
Generate Metadata: Opens the Metadata Assistant to write titles, alt text, captions, descriptions and tags across your media.
Auto-name (clusters) [Cloud AI]: In the Suggested folders panel, names each unnamed cluster from a quick caption of its representative image using your cloud provider.
Create all (clusters): Creates a folder for every named cluster at once and moves its images in. [Requires: At least one named group]
Create (single cluster): Creates one folder from a single named cluster and moves its images into it. [Requires: A folder name]
Trash group (duplicates): Moves the images marked for trash in one duplicate group to the WordPress trash after a confirm. [Requires: At least one image marked]
Optimize images: Opens the Pro Image Processor in Optimize mode with the current selection preloaded: smallest files with no visible difference, as new attachments or versioned overwrites. Without WunderPaint Pro the entry shows the Pro teaser.
Clean up the library: Opens the cleanup panel: images nothing references, files with no library entry, and originals larger than the site delivers. Deleting moves things to a holding area with a retention period rather than removing them, and re-checks before anything is finally gone. Read the Clean up the library section before using it in bulk.

sections.title: Where an image is used
sections.text:
The Usage tab in an image's detail view: every place on the site that references this file, with a link to each one.
Open an image in the Media Library Manager (the Edit metadata button on a tile) and the left column has three tabs: Details, Usage and Origin. Usage answers the question that stops most people from ever tidying their library: is anything still pointing at this?
The answer is worked out live every time you open it, not read from a stored result, because the honest answer changes the moment somebody edits a page. It is also the same check that runs again at the moment you move an image to the holding area, so a stale list can never cause a deletion.
Post content: Images inserted into any post, page or custom post type. Reads block markup including blocks that carry no wp-image class (cover, media-text, gallery, site logo), gallery shortcodes, plain URLs in src and srcset, and background images in inline CSS. A resized copy in the markup resolves back to its original.
Custom fields and builder data: Featured images, Elementor layouts, ACF fields including repeaters and flexible content, WooCommerce product galleries, and SEO social images. Page builders store their layouts as JSON with escaped slashes; that is read properly rather than skipped.
Site settings and widgets: The site icon, the custom logo, header and background images from your theme settings, and any media widget. Transients are skipped, because a reference that exists only in a cache is not a reason to keep a file.
Categories and user profiles: Category and product-category images from term meta, including WooCommerce category thumbnails, plus local avatars in user meta.
Saved designs and templates: WunderPaint's own data: saved designs, templates, the asset library and brand kits. Without this a design you saved months ago could be broken by deleting an image that looked unused, and you would only find out on opening it.
What it cannot see [Filter]: A plugin that keeps image IDs in a table of its own, or a filename hard-coded into a theme template. The panel says so in plain words when it finds nothing, rather than implying the file is definitely safe. Developers can register additional sources with the wpie_media_usage_sources filter.

sections.title: Clean up the library
sections.text:
Finds images nothing points at, files no library entry claims, and originals larger than your site delivers. Nothing is deleted on the day you ask for it.
Opened from Media Library Tools. Read this before using it in bulk: the panel removes files, and while it is built to be careful, no automatic check can know everything about a site it did not build.
The scan works through your content in slices and can be stopped at any point. Its result is sorted into four groups, and only one of them can be cleaned up. Deleting moves images to the WordPress trash with their files left in place, so addresses on your site keep resolving; a scheduled job re-checks each entry when its retention period is up and restores anything that turned out to be in use.
Take a backup before your first bulk cleanup. Not because the tool expects to be wrong, but because that is the right habit for anything that removes files in bulk.
In use: At least one exact reference was found, by attachment ID or by address. Never offered for cleanup.
Unused: No reference found anywhere, AND the last scan completed cleanly across every source, AND the image is older than the grace period. The only group that can be cleaned up. [Requires: A complete, error-free scan]
Uploaded recently [Filter]: Younger than the grace period of 14 days. Held back deliberately: an image uploaded on Tuesday has probably just not been placed yet. On a site built last month this is most of the library, which is normal and not a fault.
Not checked: Never scanned, uploaded after the last scan, or a source failed to read. If any source errored the run offers nothing for cleanup at all, because a failed query looks exactly like a source with no references in it.
Move to the holding area: Re-checks every selected image live, then moves the ones still unreferenced to the WordPress trash. The file stays on disk, so the site keeps working even if a verdict was wrong. Anything the re-check finds in use is kept and reported back to you.
Waiting to be deleted [Filter]: Everything currently held, with the date it went in and when its period ends. Put anything back with one click. When the period is over a daily job checks each entry once more; still unreferenced means it is finally removed, back in use means it restores itself.
Orphaned files [Filter]: Files sitting in the uploads folder that no library entry points at, usually left behind by imports or removed plugins. The mirror image of Find broken files. Shows a preview and the size of each. WunderPaint's own folders and known plugin cache and backup directories are always skipped.
Oversized originals [Pro for the resize]: Originals stored considerably wider than the largest size your site actually generates, so those extra pixels never reach a visitor. Each row says whether the full size file is linked directly somewhere, which is the one good reason to keep every pixel. Hands the selection to the Image Processor with the target width already set.

sections.title: Replace an image
sections.text:
Swaps the file behind a library entry so every reference keeps working, with a ratio-locked crop when the new file is a different shape.
The Replace image button sits under the preview in an image's detail view. The library entry and its ID survive, which is what lets everything already pointing at the image keep working without being touched.
Keep the current filename: Every address stays valid, so nothing on the site has to change. Caches and CDNs may still serve the old picture for a while. If the new file is a different format it is converted to the original format first, because keeping only part of a filename would change the address and break every reference.
Use the new filename: The file gets its own name and the places the usage check found are rewritten one at a time. Deliberately not a global search and replace, which fixes the database and leaves JSON and CSS files under uploads pointing at a file that no longer exists.
Crop to the original shape: Offered when the new file has a different aspect ratio, with both ratios named. The mask is locked to the original proportions, can be dragged and resized from any corner, and nudged with the arrow keys. A square slot stays square.
Scale to the original size: Renders the result at exactly the dimensions of the image it replaces. Leave it off to keep the higher resolution; WordPress generates the smaller sizes either way.
Transparency warning: Converting into a format without an alpha channel fills transparency with white. The dialog says so and points at the new-filename option as the way to keep it.

sections.title: Origin and licence
sections.text:
Where an image came from, who made it, under what licence and until when, prefilled from the file's own IPTC data.
The Origin tab in an image's detail view. Agencies and shops have to answer this question years after the download folder was cleared, which is usually when the answer is gone.
Source, Creator, Licence: Three free-text fields per image. On upload, creator and copyright are prefilled from the file's IPTC block where stock photos and most cameras already put them, using PHP's own reader so nothing has to be installed.
Licence expires: A date. The detail view warns when a licence has run out, and again while it is within a month of doing so.

sections.title: What is inside the file
sections.text:
The File data tab reads the camera, software and location a file carries, and can take the private parts back out.
The Details tab describes the image; this one describes the FILE. A photo from a phone records the camera and lens, the exposure, the software that has touched it since, and usually the exact spot it was taken at. WordPress shows none of that, and the original file stays reachable under its own address.
Everything is read with PHP's own functions, so no extra software has to be installed on the server. Coordinates are resolved against the place index that ships with the plugin, which means finding out where a photo was taken never contacts an outside service.
What the file carries: A line naming the blocks found in the file: camera data (EXIF), captions and rights (IPTC), XMP, text notes, and location. A file with nothing embedded says so plainly.
Location: Shown as a place name and a rough distance rather than a pair of numbers, worked out on your own server. The exact coordinates and the altitude are printed underneath.
Capture: When the picture was taken, the camera make and model, the lens, and the exposure values the camera recorded.
Device identity: Serial numbers of the camera body and lens, and the owner name some cameras write. Listed on its own because this is the group people are most surprised to find in a published file.
Software and rights: The software that wrote or edited the file, the artist and copyright fields, and the digital source type when one is set, which is how a file declares that AI was involved.
Remove location: Clears the coordinates and leaves everything else in place, so a photo keeps its camera details without saying where you live. The values are overwritten rather than merely unlinked, so they cannot be recovered from the raw file.
Remove all metadata: Clears every embedded block. Useful before publishing images you did not take yourself, or where the file history is nobody else's business.
What happens to the file: Both buttons work on the original and on every size generated from it, and neither re-saves the picture: the blocks are cut out of the file and the image data is left untouched, so quality is exactly as before. The previous files are kept as a version you can restore from the History panel.

sections.title: Media Library Manager: import (smarter upload)
sections.text:
The import panel that reviews files before adding them, with optimize and describe options and duplicate detection.
Triggered by the Upload button or by dropping image files onto the main pane. Files queue up for review; when the image search model is installed each is checked against your library for likely duplicates before import.
Folder (import): Chooses which folder the imported images go into. Defaults to the folder you are currently viewing, or No folder.
Optimize (max 2048px, WebP): Downscales each image to at most 2048 px and converts it to WebP on import to save space.
Describe on import (alt, caption, tags) [AI]: Writes alt text, a caption and tags for each image as it is imported, using a caption model or your provider. Disabled until an engine is available; a note warns when it uses a paid cloud provider.
Duplicate hint [Local AI]: When the image search model is installed, each queued file is checked and flagged if it looks like an existing attachment, so you can skip it.
Skip / Include: Toggles whether a queued file is imported. Skipped rows are dimmed and excluded from the count.
Import: Imports every non-skipped file with the chosen options and shows progress. The button label shows how many will be imported.
Cancel (import): Closes the import panel without importing. Disabled while an import is running.

sections.title: Stock Images dialog
sections.text:
Search free stock photos, illustrations and vectors and insert them as image layers.
Opens from the Stock Images command. Results insert as image layers (as a data URL) and nothing touches your media library until you save. If no provider key is set, it links to Settings.
Providers are whichever of Pexels, Pixabay and Unsplash you have configured. Pixabay adds Photos, Illustrations and Vectors type tabs.
Category cards: Before you search, the dialog shows curated photo categories with live thumbnails; clicking one runs that search immediately.
Provider tabs: Switches between your configured stock providers (Pexels, Pixabay, Unsplash). Changing provider clears the current results.
Type tabs (Pixabay): Only for Pixabay. Chooses Photos, Illustrations or Vectors. Changing type clears the results.
Search field: The query box. Type a term and press Enter or the Search button to run it. Focused when the dialog opens.
Search: Runs the search for the current query. Disabled while busy or when the query is empty; shows "Searching…" during a request.
Result tile: One stock result. Click it to fetch the full image and insert it as a layer, fitted and centered on the canvas. The caption links to the author's page.
Author credit: The link under each result crediting and linking to the photographer or contributor. Opens in a new tab.
Load more: Fetches the next page of results. The grid also auto-loads more as you scroll near the end, and pre-fills tall screens.
Open Settings: Shown when no provider is configured (and you can manage settings). Opens the plugin settings to add a free Pexels or Pixabay API key.

sections.title: Brand Kits dialog
sections.text:
Manage brand kits: colors, fonts, logo, watermark, company profile and custom variables that feed pickers, templates and AI.
Opens from the Brand Kits command. The left column lists your kits; the right column edits the selected kit. Changes are local until you press Save kits, which updates the whole editor.
One kit is free; multiple kits are a Pro feature. The first three colors are treated as primary, secondary and accent.
Kit list: The left column listing every kit with a swatch preview of its first colors. Click a kit to edit it.
+ New kit [Pro]: Adds a new blank kit and selects it. Beyond one kit it requires Pro and shows a PRO badge.
Name: The kit's display name, shown in pickers and template groupings.
Colors: The kit palette as swatches you can recolor or remove, with a + Color button to add more. The first three are the primary, secondary and accent colors used by templates and AI prompts.
Fonts: Up to three house fonts as dropdowns. The first is the primary font; the other two are optional. Empty selections are dropped.
Logo: The kit logo, chosen from your media library. Shows a preview, a Choose from library button (opens an inline picker) and a Remove button when set.
Watermark: An image watermark for this kit, uploaded directly (PNG, WebP, JPEG or SVG). Shows a preview and a Remove button. It appears as a one-click choice in Batch Watermark.
Company profile: Structured company details used by templates and AI: Company, Contact person, Email, Website, Street, ZIP, City, Industry, plus a free-text Description.
Custom variables: Your own key and value pairs. Keys are lowercased and stripped to letters, numbers and underscores; values are free text. They become {key} placeholders in content templates.
+ Variable: Adds an empty custom variable row. Hidden once you reach the maximum.
Delete kit: Deletes the current kit. It asks once ("Really delete?") before removing; the last remaining kit is replaced by a fresh blank one.
Save kits: Saves all kits at once and refreshes the editor so pickers, templates and open dialogs see the changes. Shows "Saving…" while working.
Close: Closes the dialog without saving unsaved edits. Escape does the same.

sections.title: Quick Insert palette
sections.text:
A slash menu to filter and insert or open any insert source by typing.
Opens with the `/` key. Type to filter the list, use the arrow keys to move, and press Enter to run the highlighted command. Escape closes it.
Filter input: The text box at the top. Typing filters commands by label and hint; Arrow keys move the selection and Enter runs it.
Text: Inserts a centered text layer in the foreground color.
Rectangle: Inserts a centered rectangle filled with the foreground color.
Ellipse: Inserts a centered ellipse filled with the foreground color.
Frame: Circle: Inserts a circular photo frame you can drop an image into.
Icon…: Opens the icon library.
Emoji…: Opens the emoji library.
Text combination…: Opens the Asset Library on the styled text-combination groups.
Elements…: Opens the Asset Library on shapes (arrows, blobs, badges).
Background…: Opens the Asset Library on backgrounds (gradients, patterns, colors).
Image…: Opens the Asset Library on your media library images.
Stock photo…: Opens the Stock Images dialog (Pexels / Pixabay).
Chart…: Opens the chart tool (bar, line, pie, donut).
QR code…: Inserts a QR code (link, Wi-Fi, vCard and more).
Generate with AI… [AI]: Opens the AI panel to generate an image from text.
Design Generator… [AI]: Opens the Design Generator to build a whole design from a brief.

sections.title: Command palette
sections.text:
A searchable palette of every editor command: menu actions, dialogs, tools and effects.
Opens with Cmd/Ctrl+K. Type to filter by command label or group; Arrow keys move and Enter runs the highlighted command. Each row shows its group and, for tools, the keyboard shortcut.
Command input: The search box. Filters all commands by label and group as you type; Arrow keys navigate and Enter runs the selection.
Edit commands: Undo and Redo, in the Edit group.
File commands: Export, Library, Design Generator and Stock Images.
Image commands: Image Size, Canvas Size, Resize Design, Trim and Rotate 90 CW.
View commands: Check Contrast and Guides & Grid.
Layer commands: New Layer, Group Layers, Duplicate Layer, Add Layer Mask, Convert to Smart Object and Flatten.
Select commands: Select All and Deselect.
Help commands: Keyboard Shortcuts and Handbook.
Tools: Every editor tool, listed as "Tool: name" with its keyboard shortcut, selecting the tool when run.
Effects: The whole effects registry (non-hidden effects), each opening that effect when run.

sections.title: Asset Generator (AI) dialog
sections.text:
Describe an asset and the AI proposes editable gradients, text lockups, shapes or one full illustration.
A cloud feature that works with any text-capable provider (Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini). It creates a new editable layer from a text prompt; if no key is set it links to Settings.
For gradient, text and shape it returns four options to preview and insert; for illustration it draws one SVG through the real render pipeline.
Brand Kit: Chooses which Brand Kit steers the generation (its palette, fonts and profile). Includes a No Brand Kit option and a pencil to edit kits. Only shown when kits exist.
Asset Type: The type of asset to generate: Gradient, Text, Shape or Illustration. Each has its own prompt hints and suggestion chips.
Prompt: Describes what you want, with a live character count and a type-specific placeholder. The suggestion chips below append their text to it.
Suggestion chips: One-tap prompt starters that change per type (for example Warm sunset, Bold sale banner, Lightning bolt, Cozy home office). Clicking one adds it to the prompt.
Exact text (Text type): Only for the Text type. An optional box for the exact wording, one line per headline, bullet or subline. [Shown for: Text]
Generate / Regenerate: Runs the generation. It asks the AI for four options (or draws one illustration) and shows "Generating…"; after the first run the button becomes Regenerate.
Insert (per option): Adds that single generated option to the canvas as a new editable layer.
Insert all: Adds every generated option to the canvas at once and closes the dialog. Not shown for illustrations.
Cancel: Closes the dialog. Disabled while a generation is running.
Open Settings (no key): Shown in the error message when no provider key is configured; opens the plugin settings.

sections.title: Design Generator dialog
sections.text:
Turn a written brief into a full, editable layout: background, image, shapes and text land as layers.
Describe a design (or start from a style preset) and the assistant plans a layout via the text model and sources an image. It proposes several variant previews; you pick one and it inserts as editable layers.
It can also produce a dynamic template whose chosen fields bind to a post, so the design updates per post while your typed copy stays as the preview.
Canvas readout: Shows the current document's width and height in pixels, the size the design is built for.
Describe the Design: The main brief box. Describe the design you want, for example an Instagram post announcing a summer sale.
Start from a Style: Eight preset style cards that seed the brief with a starting description you can then edit: Bold Promo, Minimal Quote, Energetic Sale, Editorial Hero, Event Invite, Retro Poster, Tech Launch and Soft Pastel.
Image: How the design gets its image: Stock photo (when a provider is set), Placeholder image, Generate with AI (when an image provider is set) or No image.
Image provider: For Generate with AI, chooses the image model (OpenAI or Google Gemini) when more than one is configured.
Image description: For AI or stock images, a box to describe or refine what the photo should show (subject, style, mood, colors). [Shown for: AI or Stock]
Brand & Context: Optional details that steer the copy: Brand or product name, Headline, Subheadline or tagline, Call to action, Website or URL, and Brand colors.
Brand Kit: Applies a Brand Kit's palette, fonts and profile. Includes No Brand Kit and a pencil to edit kits. Only shown when kits with colors or fonts exist.
Use the active image layer as style reference: When an image, raster or smart-object layer is selected, sends a snapshot of it as a style reference for the design. [Shown when: A referenceable layer is active]
Include the kit logo as a layer: Adds the selected Brand Kit's logo as its own layer after the design. Only shown when the kit has a logo.
Make it a dynamic template: Turns the result into a dynamic template. The fields you enable bind to the post; your typed copy stays as the preview placeholder.
Dynamic fields: When dynamic is on, choose which post fields bind: Post title, Post excerpt, Featured image, Category and Publish date.
Create Design: Sends the brief and settings, builds the layout and renders variant previews. The button shows the current status while working.
Pick a variant: The result cards. Click one to insert it as editable layers (plus the logo if enabled). The copy says it proposes three fresh designs.
Regenerate designs: Asks the model again for a fresh set of variants, with new copy and direction, not just a new composition.
Back to the brief: Returns from the variant view to the brief so you can adjust it.
Cancel: Closes the dialog. Disabled while the assistant is working.

sections.title: Use Image dialog
sections.text:
After saving a new image, decide where it should go: as a featured image or in a new draft.
Appears after Save As New. The freshly saved attachment can be set as a featured image on an existing post or dropped into a brand-new draft.
Preview and note: Shows the saved image and a note that it is in the library, ready to use as a featured image or in a new draft.
Search posts: A live title search over your posts to find one to attach the image to.
Set featured: Sets the saved image as the featured image of that post, with a link to edit the post afterward.
Insert into new draft: Creates a new draft post that contains the image, with a link to edit the draft.
Skip: Closes the dialog without attaching the image anywhere. It stays in the library.

sections.title: Post picker dialog
sections.text:
Search and pick a post to preview a dynamic template with, or to receive an action like setting a featured image.
Used by View, then Preview with Post for dynamic templates, and reused by other flows (such as setting a featured image). Picking a post fetches its context so bindings resolve; in preview mode it turns on the non-destructive binding preview on the canvas without changing anything.
Post type: A dropdown to choose which post type to search, shown only when more than one type is available.
Search posts by title: A live title search over published posts, debounced as you type. It is focused on open, and Enter picks the first result.
Result row: One post, showing its thumbnail, title and a meta line (date and first category). Clicking it picks the post.
Heading and subheading: The dialog title and subtitle, which the calling feature can override (for example "Set as featured image"). By default it reads "Preview with Post".

sections.title: Batch Watermark dialog
sections.text:
Stamp a watermark onto many library images at once, with a live preview and saved settings.
One modal with two columns. The left holds the watermark settings (a Brand Kit watermark or a direct upload, a position grid, sliders and a live preview); the right is a large media browser to select the target images.
Watermarked copies are saved as new attachments; originals are never touched. Your last settings are remembered.
Watermark source: Choose the watermark image from your Brand Kits' watermarks (one-click tiles) or upload one directly. A tip suggests storing watermarks in Brand Kits.
Upload image: Uploads a watermark image and selects it. The uploaded mark shows as an active tile labeled Upload.
Live preview: A canvas that shows the watermark placed exactly as the batch run will, over the first selected image (or a neutral area), using the current position, size, opacity and margin.
Preview stage toggle: Switches the preview background between Selected image (the first target) and Neutral area (a plain stage).
Position: A 3x3 anchor grid to place the watermark: Top left, Top right, Center, Bottom left or Bottom right.
Size: How large the watermark is relative to the image.
Opacity: How transparent the watermark is.
Margin: The gap between the watermark and the image edge, in output pixels. Has no effect when the position is Center.
Target image browser: A media browser on the right to pick which images to watermark. Click images to select or deselect; the heading shows how many are selected.
Watermark N image(s): Runs the batch. Each target is redrawn with the watermark and saved as a new JPEG attachment (named with a -watermarked suffix), with progress shown. Disabled until a watermark and at least one image are chosen.
Cancel: Closes the dialog without running the batch.

sections.title: Metadata Assistant (Alt Text) dialog
sections.text:
Generate titles, alt text, captions, descriptions and tags for many media images in one pass, with review before saving.
A two-column tool. The left column sets the engine, output language, which fields to fill, optional prefix/suffix affixes and a cost estimate; the right is a searchable, multi-select media grid.
A run makes one suggestion per selected image (including tags and mood on cloud engines), which you review and edit before writing. The local model only writes descriptive text, not titles or tags.
Engine: The captioning engine: Local model (free, on device) or a cloud provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini). Only installed or configured engines appear. Local writes text only.
Language: The output language for cloud captioning. English is the default plus German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese and Polish. Hidden for the local model.
Fill: Which metadata fields to write: Title (cloud only), Alt text, Caption, Description and Tags (cloud only). Title and Tags are disabled and dimmed under the local model.
Prefix / suffix: An expandable panel to wrap each of Title, Alt text, Caption and Description with a fixed prefix and suffix. The { } button inserts variables like site name, brand or date.
Affix presets: Save the current prefix/suffix set as a named preset, load a saved one, or delete one. Presets are stored in your browser.
Cost estimate: A rough dollar estimate for the current cloud selection, based on the engine and the number of selected images. Shown only for cloud engines with a selection. [Shown for: Cloud engines]
Search by title: Filters the media grid by title text.
Filter (All / Missing alt text): Limits the grid to All images or only those Missing alt text. Opens on Missing alt text when launched from that context.
Select all / Clear: Selects every shown image or clears the selection. A counter shows how many are selected.
Media tile: One image. Click to select, Shift-click for a range; a "no alt" badge marks images without alt text, and the pencil opens the per-image editor.
