Featured (chip): A marker on a post row meaning the post already has a featured image set. When the skip filter is on, these rows are left untouched during a run.
Load more: Loads the next page of posts and appends them to the list. Shown only when more results are available.

sections.title: Featured Images: template, AI background, brand and model
sections.text:
The design controls that decide how each generated featured image looks: the dynamic template, the AI background prompt, the brand kit, the image model and an optional saved Action.
A **dynamic template** is a design whose layers are bound to post data (title, date, price and so on). During a run each post's data fills those bindings, and if the template has an AI background slot, a fresh background is generated from your prompt.
The image model and brand kit are only relevant when a template actually requests an AI background. Templates without an AI background slot still work with no image provider configured.
Dynamic Template: A grid of template tiles; click one to use it for the batch. The chosen template is also saved as the fallback used by auto-generation on publish. Tiles are filtered to the selected brand kit's templates plus unassigned ones.
AI Background (optional): Generates the background through your AI provider. The prompt is user-first: your style directive leads verbatim, brand kit colors join as a color-mood line, and post specifics (title, excerpt, category) are only added when 'Send post context' is enabled. No hidden boilerplate sentences are appended. The bound layer's optional Reference field (set in the editor's properties panel) names a custom image field - every post's background is then re-imagined from its own image; the uploaded reference stays as the ad-hoc alternative.
Style button: A compact helper next to the AI Background box that inserts ready-made background style phrases into the prompt, so you do not have to write the look from scratch.
Variable button: Inserts dynamic variables (for example brand or post tokens like `{{post.title}}`) into the AI Background prompt, so the generated look can reference the current post or brand kit.
Reference: Uploads an example image; every background is then re-imagined from that image's look toward the post's content. Once set, a thumbnail with a small remove (×) button appears in its place.
Send post context: Opt-in: adds the post's title, excerpt and category to the AI background prompt. Off by default so explicit style directives stay in charge; the setting persists and also applies to auto-generation on publish.
Brand Kit: Selects which brand kit steers the run: its colors and fonts guide the AI background, and its variables fill brand bindings in the template. Includes a **No Brand Kit** option. Only shown when at least one non-empty brand kit exists.
Edit Brand Kits (pencil): Opens the in-editor Brand Kits dialog so you can add or change kits without leaving Featured Images. The kit list refreshes automatically after you save. [Shown when: the editor exposes a Brand Kits opener]
Model: Chips that pick which configured image provider renders the AI backgrounds. Only appears when at least one image provider (API key) is set up. The active provider is highlighted. [Shown when: an image provider is configured]
Action (optional): Replays a saved editor Action (effects, filters, adjustments, resize) on every finished image, for example a black-and-white look. Choose **No action** to skip. Only listed when you have saved Actions.

sections.title: Featured Images: processing options
sections.text:
The on/off switches that control what happens to each post during a Featured Images run, plus the per-category template mapping.
These toggles decide the finishing steps and where the result lands. Some appear only when the relevant tool is available, for example the PDF option needs a PDF exporter, and the SEO toggles need an active SEO plugin. The site-wide ones - auto-generate on publish, per-category templates, auto-refresh and the category mapping - are settings for the whole site and need an account that can manage options; everyone else sees the run options only.
Auto-generate on publish: When on, newly published posts that have no featured image are queued automatically and processed while the editor is open. Uses the category mapping if enabled, otherwise the saved default template. Blog posts only.
Auto-refresh dynamic images: The lazy scheduler: a daily schedule marks every embedded dynamic image stale, and the next wp-admin visit re-renders them quietly in the background. Graphics built on live data (for example a Dynamic Showcases products grid) stay current wherever they are embedded, with no server-side rendering required.
Per-category templates: When on, each post chooses its template based on its category, and the template selected above becomes the fallback. Reveals the per-category mapping list. Blog posts only.
Skip posts with a featured image: When on, any selected post that already has a featured image is left untouched and reported as skipped. Defaults on for posts and pages, off for products.
Set as featured image: When on, the finished image becomes the post's featured image. Set server-side, so it works for every post type, not just blog posts.
Also save as PDF: Stores a print-ready PDF of each finished design in the Media Library, next to the image. Only shown when a PDF exporter is available. [Shown when: PDF export is available]
Enhance design with AI: Gives each rendered image one extra AI polish pass. Costs one more generated image per post, and fine text may be redrawn slightly. Only shown when an image provider is configured.
Set social image: Also sets the finished image as the OG/Twitter social image via the active SEO plugin (Yoast SEO and/or Rank Math). The toggle label names the detected plugin(s). Only shown when an SEO plugin is active. [Shown when: Yoast SEO or Rank Math is active]
Generate SEO title & description: Writes an SEO title and meta description for each post, in the post's own language, and stores them in the active SEO plugin's fields. Only shown when an SEO plugin and a text-capable AI provider are both present. [Shown when: SEO plugin + text provider present]
Per-category template mapping: The list revealed by Per-category templates: one dropdown per category, each choosing that category's template or **Default** (the fallback). Changes are saved as you make them.
Webhook after every bake: An optional URL (Zapier, Make, any endpoint) that receives a JSON POST after every finished dynamic-image bake: post, instance, attachment id and the fresh image URL. The bridge for publish-after-bake automations.

sections.title: Featured Images: WooCommerce products
sections.text:
Extra options that appear when the post type is Product: process the whole product gallery and append a generated infographic.
When you switch the post type to **Product**, Featured Images can go beyond the main image and rework the entire WooCommerce gallery, then optionally add an AI infographic built from the product's own data.
Process gallery images: When on, every image in the WooCommerce product gallery is run through the same enhance/action finishing and the gallery template below, then the product gallery is replaced with the results. Products only.
Append product infographic: Generates one AI infographic from the product's name, price, short description and rating, and adds it to the end of the gallery. Products only, and only when an image provider is configured.
Gallery template: Chooses how each gallery image is treated. Options are **No template (finishing only)** to keep it as a photo, **Same template as the main image**, or any specific dynamic template (placed via its Product image binding). Shown only when Process gallery images is on.

sections.title: Featured Images: batch queue and run controls
sections.text:
The right-hand queue panel and the footer buttons that start, stop, resume and monitor a Featured Images batch.
Because progress is stored on the server, a run is resumable. If you reopen the dialog with unfinished jobs, you can pick up where you left off, retry failed ones, and clear finished cards.
Batch Queue: The live list of jobs, newest first. Each card shows the post title, a colored status dot and the current status text, with a link to the finished image or a Retry button as appropriate.
Job status labels: The per-job status shown on each queue card as it advances through the pipeline. Failed jobs also show the error text.
Clear: Removes all finished job cards (done, failed and skipped) from the queue. Only appears when at least one finished job exists. Unfinished jobs are kept.
Clear all: Removes every job you may manage from the queue, including queued and unfinished ones - a running batch stops first. Two-step button: the first click arms it, the second clears.
Resume N unfinished: Restarts processing of the jobs that are still queued or mid-pipeline, for example after a reload. Only appears when unfinished jobs exist and nothing is currently running.
Retry: Re-runs a single failed job from the start, clearing its previous error. Only shown on failed cards while no batch is running.
Open image (link): On a finished job, opens the generated image in a new tab. Shown only when the job is done and has a result URL. [Shown when: job status is Done]
Process N posts: The main action: queues the selected posts (minus any skipped ones) and starts the batch immediately. Disabled until at least one post and a template are chosen. The label shows the selected count.
Stop after current post: Replaces the Process button while a batch runs. It lets the current post finish, then halts the queue so nothing is left half-done. [Shown when: a batch is running]
Cancel: Closes the dialog without starting a new run. Queued and finished jobs remain on the server and can be resumed later.
Selection summary: The footer readout showing how many posts are selected and which template will be used, plus an `N active · N total` count in the queue foot.

sections.title: Image Processor (Batch Process)
sections.text:
Re-encode, resize, convert, optimize and optionally run an Action over many Media Library images in one pass, right in your browser.
The **Batch Process** dialog takes a set of attachment ids, applies an optional saved Action plus export settings, and writes the results either as new attachments or as versioned overwrites. Everything runs client-side through the headless render pipeline, with a live per-image progress list.
Select from Library: Opens the WordPress media modal to pick images to process; picks are added to the current selection. Only shown when the media modal is available.
Paste attachment IDs: A text field to type or paste attachment ids directly, separated by spaces, commas or semicolons. Used when you already know the ids or the media modal is unavailable.
Quick Presets: Eight compact one-tap cards that set format, quality and max size together. The active card is highlighted when the current settings match it.
Action: Chooses a saved editor Action to run on every image before export, or **re-encode only** to just convert and compress without edits.
Format: A five-way switch for the output encoding. **Auto** is the Optimize mode (smallest file with no visible difference); AVIF is encoded by the bundled WASM codec.
Save As: Chooses where results go: **New attachments** creates fresh Media Library entries, or **Overwrite (versioned)** replaces the originals while keeping a version history.
Quality: Slider for the output compression quality. Higher means larger, cleaner files. Ignored for lossless PNG in practice.
Watermark: When ticked, applies your configured watermark to each processed image. Only shown when a watermark is set up in the editor. [Shown when: a watermark is configured]
Process N image(s): Starts the batch and shows a live list where each row reports pending, working, done (with a link) or error. Disabled while running or when nothing is selected; the label reflects the image count.
Cancel: Closes the dialog. Disabled while a batch is running so you do not interrupt it mid-pass.
Optimize (Auto format): The Auto format re-encodes each image at the lowest quality that still looks identical (a perceptual SSIM search), preferring WebP with JPEG fallback. When overwriting, an image is only replaced for a meaningful saving (at least 5% or 10 KB); otherwise it reports **already optimal**, which also protects against quality loss from repeated runs.
Max Size: Downscales every image so its long side stays within the chosen limit before encoding; **Original size** keeps dimensions. Works with every format. A real downscale always saves, even when the byte saving alone would be marginal.
WASM codecs: Bundled WebAssembly encoders (MozJPEG, WebP, AVIF) plus a lossless OxiPNG pass take over encoding when available: better compression than the browser's native encoders, WebP output even on Safari, and AVIF output at all. Loaded lazily on the first run; the native encoders remain as automatic fallback.
Results: A scrollable section that lists every processed image with its title, new file size, format, dimensions, the saving in green, and an **open** link to the saved file. Skipped images show **already optimal**, failures show the error message.
Selection grid: Selected images show as cards with their real Media Library thumbnail and title (plus id), so you can verify the batch before running it. Up to eight cards are shown, the rest is summarized as +N.

sections.title: Series from CSV (Generate from CSV)
sections.text:
Turn the current document into a template and generate one Media Library image per CSV row by filling in {{placeholder}} text.
**Generate from CSV** treats your open document as a template. Any `{{key}}` written into a text layer is a placeholder; upload a CSV whose column headers match those keys, and each row renders the document once and saves it as a new image.
Nothing needs to be pre-configured: the placeholders you type define the columns the CSV should have. The file name for each image comes from a column you choose.
Placeholders in this document: A read-only list of the `{{key}}` tokens detected in the document's text layers. These define the columns your CSV should carry. If none are found, the dialog explains to add one like `{{title}}` first.
Your CSV should look like this: A preview block showing an example CSV matching the current placeholders: a `filename` column plus one column per placeholder. Shown before a CSV is loaded.
Download sample CSV: Downloads a ready-made `wpie-series.csv` with the correct headers and two example rows, so you can fill it in instead of building the file by hand.
Choose CSV file…: Opens a file picker for a `.csv` file. After loading, the file name and row count show, and the CSV's headers appear as chips marked used or unused against your placeholders.
Header chips (used / unused): Each CSV column header is shown as a chip. A **used** chip matches a placeholder in the document; an **unused** chip is a column that will not be applied.
Missing in CSV: A warning listing any document placeholders that have no matching CSV column. Those placeholders stay empty in the output rather than blocking the run.
File name from column: Chooses which CSV column supplies each generated image's file name. Defaults to the first column. Names are cleaned to safe characters, with a fallback like `image-1` if empty.
Format: The output image format for every generated row.
Quality: A number field for compression quality of the generated images. Values are clamped to the valid range.
Generate N graphics: Renders one image per CSV row and saves each as a new Media Library attachment, showing a live progress list with per-row done links or errors. Disabled until a CSV with rows and at least one placeholder are present.
Cancel / Close: While running, a **Cancel** button stops after the current row; otherwise a **Close** button dismisses the dialog. Escape also closes it when idle.

sections.title: Generate Content (AI content generator)
sections.text:
Produce a complete WordPress draft in one pass: article text plus featured image, OG image, body images and an infographic, all in your brand.
**Generate Content** ties the content template, brand kit and a dynamic design template together. You describe the assignment (topic, keyword, context, internal links) and the pipeline writes the article, renders every image in your brand, and files a WordPress draft with SEO meta.
It needs a text-capable AI provider (Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini). Without an image provider it still creates the draft, but without images.
Brand Kit: Selects the brand kit whose profile, colors, fonts and variables steer the article tone and the generated images. A pencil button opens the Brand Kits editor. Defaults to the first kit.
Content template: Chooses which reusable content recipe (model setup, prompts, output rules) writes the article. Managed in the Content Templates dialog.
Dynamic template (featured image): Chooses the design template used to render the featured image. Pick **AI image (no dynamic template)** to generate a plain AI image instead. Templates are grouped by the selected brand kit and a **Without Brand Kit** group.
Action: Replays a saved editor Action on the rendered featured image, for example a black-and-white look. Choose **No action** to skip. Appears only when a dynamic template is selected and you have saved Actions.
Enhance design: Gives the rendered featured image one extra AI polish pass. Costs one more generated image, and fine text may be redrawn slightly. Shown when a dynamic template is chosen and an image provider is configured.
Topic: The free-text subject of the article, for example `How to winterize a garden pond`. Required before you can generate.
Suggest topics: Asks the AI for three topic ideas drawn from your brand profile and category, each with a focus keyword and a short rationale. Clicking an idea fills the topic and keyword fields. Needs a text provider.
Focus keyword: The main SEO keyword for the article. Used to steer the writing and written into the SEO plugin's focus keyword field on the draft.
Category: Assigns the resulting draft to a WordPress category. Choose **No category** to leave it unassigned.
Context (optional): A free-text box for facts, offers or target-audience notes the article should use. Helps ground the writing in your specifics.
Internal links: One link per line as `URL | anchor text`; the article weaves these into the body. Up to 20 links are used.
Load suggestions: Searches your posts and pages for the best internal-link targets matching the focus keyword or topic (service pages are prioritized) and lists them as toggleable rows that add or remove lines in the links box.
Progress (generation steps): A progress bar plus step chips that light up as the pipeline runs. The steps are the full set of outputs produced for the draft. A header shows elapsed time and percent complete.
Open draft in WordPress: After a successful run, links straight to the newly created draft's editor. The panel also reports the draft's post id and any non-fatal image failures. [Shown when: a draft was created]
Generate post: Starts the whole pipeline. Disabled until a text provider, a content template and a topic are all present. The label changes to **Generating…** while it runs.
Cancel / Close: While a run is live, **Cancel** signals the pipeline to stop; otherwise **Close** dismisses the dialog. Escape does not close mid-run.

sections.title: Content Templates
sections.text:
Manage the reusable AI article recipes used by Generate Content: model setup, prompts and output rules.
Each **content template** is a saved recipe of how an article is written and which images accompany it. The left column lists starter templates and your own; the right side is the form. Starters are read-only, so saving an edited starter creates an editable copy.
Prompt placeholders like `{company}`, `{topic}` or `{focus_keyword}` are resolved from the brand kit and the assignment at generation time.
Template list: The left column of saved templates. Each row shows the name, language and description; built-in ones carry a **Starter** chip. Click to load one into the form.
+ New template: Clears the form to a blank template so you can build one from scratch.
Name: The template's display name, shown in the list and in the Generate Content picker. Required to save.
Output language: The language the finished article is written in, regardless of the language of the prompts. The server injects an explicit output-language instruction from this setting.
Description: A short note about what this template is for. Shown under the name in the list and as a hint in Generate Content.
Text provider: Which AI text model writes the article. Choose **Default text provider** to use the editor's global default, or pin a specific one.
Image provider: Which AI image model renders the images. Choose **Default image provider** or pin a specific one.
Thinking budget: How much internal reasoning the text model spends before writing. More thinking generally means a stronger article at higher cost.
Web search: When on, lets the model research current sources while writing the article.
System prompt: The large instruction block that defines the writer's role, tone and rules. This is the core of the recipe and can reference placeholders like `{company}` and `{topic}`.
Image prompt (style template for all images): A shared style description applied to every image the pipeline generates, so body images, featured and OG all look consistent. A Style button inserts ready-made style phrases.
Output directives: Extra rules appended to the generation, for example structural or formatting requirements the article must follow.
Body images: How many in-article body images the pipeline generates. Set 0 for a text-only article.
Body aspect: The aspect ratio for the body images.
Featured aspect: The aspect ratio for the featured image (and typically the OG image).
Min. words: A minimum word count target for the generated article body.
Infographic: When on, adds a summarizing infographic after the quick box in the article.
Save button: Saves the template. The label is **Create template** for a new one, **Save** for an existing user template, and **Save as copy** when editing a starter (which creates an editable copy rather than changing the starter). Disabled until a name is entered.
Delete: Deletes the current user template after a confirmation click (**Really delete?**). Not available for starter templates.

sections.title: Dynamic Template Shortcodes (in-editor dialog)
sections.text:
One dialog that bakes and hands out every shortcode the dynamic-image family offers, for use in the Classic editor, Elementor's shortcode widget and any other builder.
Reached from **View, Dynamic Template Shortcodes**, this dialog explains and produces the three shortcodes so you can use a design outside Gutenberg. The Live Badge is baked from the current design; the Personalized and Dynamic Image shortcodes reference a saved dynamic template by its id.
Personalized and Dynamic Image both require the current design to be saved as a dynamic template first (`File, Save as Dynamic Template`), because their shortcodes point at the template id.
Bake badge from this design: Exports the current document as a vector Live Badge SVG and stores it server-side, returning a `[wpie_live_badge]` shortcode. Updating the design's dynamic template re-bakes the badge automatically; the button (labelled **Re-bake badge** once a badge exists) covers designs you change without saving to a template, and the shortcode stays the same either way. Vector content (text and shapes) works best; pixel layers embed as static images.
Live Badge copy row: Shows the baked badge shortcode in a read-only field with a **Copy** button. Copying confirms with a toast, or tells you to select and copy by hand if the browser blocks clipboard access.
Personalized parameter mapping: For each named text layer, a **parameter** field and a **fallback text** field. The parameter is the URL query key (for example `name`) that will replace the layer; the fallback shows when the parameter is missing. Parameter input strips characters other than letters, digits, underscore and dash.
Personalized copy row: Builds and shows the `[wpie_personalized]` shortcode with the template id and the `map` string assembled from your parameter/fallback entries, with a Copy button. Requires the design to be a saved dynamic template.
Dynamic Image copy row: Shows the `[wpie_dynamic_image template="…"]` shortcode for the current saved template, with a Copy button. Saves mark the baked image stale, and the next open editor session re-bakes it; until the first bake, the template preview shows.

sections.title: Dynamic-image Gutenberg blocks
sections.text:
Three block-editor blocks that place your dynamic templates directly onto pages and posts, each with its own inspector settings.
These blocks live in the **Media** category of the Gutenberg inserter. Dynamic Image bakes a real image on every save; Live Badge is a baked vector whose bound texts the server fills in as the page is served and which re-bakes when its template is updated; Personalized Image renders live in each visitor's browser with URL parameters applied.
Every block shares two inspector controls: a **Dynamic template** picker and a **Width (%)** slider. Blocks render server-side on the front end.
Dynamic Image (WPIE): A real image baked from a dynamic template filled with this post's data, re-rendered on every save so the front end serves a plain, stable ` `. Add it, pick a template, then save (or press Render now) to bake.
Render now: Bakes the Dynamic Image block immediately instead of waiting for the next post save. The button shows **Rendering…** while it works.
Live Badge (WPIE): A vector badge whose bound texts are substituted server-side on every page view, so it stays current with no re-render. Pick a template and press Create badge; vector-only designs (text and shapes) work best.
Create badge / Recreate badge: Exports the chosen template to SVG and stores it as the badge. The label is **Create badge** the first time and **Recreate badge** afterward; **Creating…** shows while it works.
Personalized Image (WPIE): Renders a template live in the visitor's browser, replacing mapped text layers with URL parameters, so every visitor can get their own version. Pick a template, then map layers to parameters. The editor preview uses the fallback values.
URL parameters (Parameter / Fallback text): A second inspector panel listing each text layer of the chosen template with a **Parameter** field (the URL query key, letters/digits/underscore/dash only) and a **Fallback text** field shown when the parameter is absent.
Dynamic template (block picker): The shared dropdown in each block's settings that selects which saved dynamic template the block uses. Its first option is **Select a template**.
Width (%): The shared slider controlling how wide the block renders relative to its container. Present in all three blocks.
Background refresh (lazy scheduler): Dynamic images re-render on every save of their post, and, with **Auto-refresh dynamic images** enabled in the Automate dialog, on a daily schedule: while you work anywhere in wp-admin, an invisible background frame re-renders stale images. The embedded image keeps its stable URL and picks up a fresh version stamp, so it updates everywhere it is shown. Every re-bake overwrites the instance's single attachment (the previous file stays as a restorable version) - the media library never fills with copies.

sections.title: Front-end shortcodes reference
sections.text:
The three shortcodes the dynamic-image family registers, with their attributes, for the Classic editor, Elementor's shortcode widget and any other builder.
Every dynamic block has a matching shortcode so the same designs work outside Gutenberg. All three accept a `width` attribute (a percentage, clamped between 10 and 100). Use the in-editor Dynamic Template Shortcodes dialog to generate them with the right ids filled in.
[wpie_dynamic_image]: Outputs a real, baked image filled with the embedding post's data for the given template. Until the first bake lands, the template preview shows; each post save marks the image stale so the next capable editor session re-bakes it, overwriting the same attachment for a stable URL.
[wpie_live_badge]: Inlines a stored vector badge SVG, substituting its bound text nodes with the current post's field values on every page render. The SVG is sanitized on save (scripts, links and animation stripped) and uses the page's self-hosted fonts. Because the visitor's browser lays out the SVG text, spacing can differ slightly from the editor preview - by design, in exchange for texts that update on every view.
[wpie_personalized]: Renders a template live in the visitor's browser with per-visitor URL-parameter substitutions. Post bindings (title, prices) resolve server-side; only the mapped parameters stay dynamic client-side. Visiting `?name=Anna` replaces the mapped layer with `Anna`.
map attribute format: The `map` attribute of `[wpie_personalized]` is a pipe-separated list; each entry is a layer name, a URL parameter and an optional fallback, separated by colons, as in `map="Name:name:Guest|City:city"`.
Newsletter merge tags (personalized images): The personalized shortcode reads its values from URL parameters, which makes newsletter personalization a one-liner: link your mailing to the page as `?vorname=*|FNAME|*` (Mailchimp) or `?vorname={{contact.FIRSTNAME}}` (Brevo) and map the layer with `[wpie_personalized template="…" map="Name:vorname:Kaffeefreund"]` - the mail tool substitutes its merge tag into the URL, every reader sees the graphic with their own name, and the third mapping part is the fallback for visitors without a parameter.

sections.title: Featured Images: warnings, option values and states
sections.text:
The empty option values, warning banners and state messages in the Featured Images batch dialog that the main control list does not cover.
These items appear inside dropdowns, as inline warning banners above the post list, or as small status texts. They round out the documentation of the Featured Images dialog (`automate-dialog.jsx`).
No Brand Kit: The last option in the **Brand Kit** dropdown. Picks no kit, so the AI background is not steered by brand colors or fonts and any brand variable bindings stay empty.
No action: The default option in the optional **Action** dropdown. Leaves the finished image exactly as rendered, without replaying a saved editor action on it.
No template (finishing only): A **Gallery template** option (products only). Each WooCommerce gallery image only receives the enhance and action finishing, it is not placed into a dynamic template.
Same template as the main image: A **Gallery template** option. Every gallery image runs through the same dynamic template you chose for the featured image, filled through its Product image binding.
Default (per-category row): The first option in each row of the per-category template mapping. Leaves that category on the fallback template selected above instead of assigning it a specific one. [Shown when: Per-category templates is on]
Remove reference image: The small × on the uploaded reference thumbnail. Clears the reference so backgrounds are generated from the text prompt alone.
No image provider is configured (warning): A banner shown when no image API key is set. AI backgrounds are unavailable, but templates that have no AI background slot still work. Add a key in Settings.
This template has no dynamic layers yet (warning): A banner shown when the chosen template has no bound layers, so every post would get the same image. Bind layers via `Properties, Dynamic content`.
This template uses an AI background, but no image provider is configured (warning): A banner shown when the selected template needs an AI-generated background but no image provider is available.
%1$d active · %2$d total: The footer counter under the **Batch Queue**. Shows how many jobs are still unfinished and the total number of jobs stored.
Nothing processed yet. Select posts and press Process.: The empty state of the **Batch Queue** before any run has started.
(no title): Placeholder shown in the post list for a post that has no title yet.
Loading… / No posts found.: The post list states: `Loading…` while a search runs, and `No posts found.` when the search and filter match nothing.
All selected posts already have a featured image.: An error toast raised when every picked post is removed by the skip filter, so there is nothing to process.
%d posts skipped (already have a featured image).: A success note after queueing that reports how many posts the skip filter left untouched.

sections.title: Batch Queue: job status labels
sections.text:
The per-job status text on each card in the Batch Queue as a post moves through the pipeline.
Each queued post shows a colored dot and one of these status texts. They advance in order as the browser processes the job, and closing the editor never loses them (the job store is server-side).
Queued: The job is waiting in line and has not started yet.
Generating background…: The AI image background for this post is being generated.
Rendering…: The dynamic template is being filled with the post data and rendered to an image.
Enhancing design…: The optional extra AI polish pass is running on the rendered image.
Applying action…: A saved editor action (effects, filters, adjustments, resize) is being replayed on the finished image.
Processing gallery…: The product's WooCommerce gallery images are being processed and rebuilt.
Generating infographic…: An AI infographic from the product data is being created and appended to the gallery.
Saving…: The finished image is being written to the Media Library and set as the featured image.
Saving PDF…: A print-ready PDF of the design is being stored next to the image.
Done: The post finished successfully. An Open image link appears on the card.
Failed: The job hit an error (the message is appended). A Retry button appears when nothing is running.
Skipped: The post was skipped, for example because it already had a featured image and the skip filter was on.

sections.title: Batch Process: preset cards, options and states
sections.text:
The quick preset cards, dropdown and segmented options, and progress states inside the Batch Process (Image Processor) dialog.
The Batch Process dialog (`batch-dialog.jsx`, opened as Image Processor) re-encodes, resizes and converts many library images in one browser-side pass. These are the option values and states the main list did not name.
Optimize: The first **Quick Preset** card. Sets the format to Auto: smallest file with no visible difference (perceptual auto quality, WebP preferred).
Web JPEG: A one-tap **Quick Preset** card. Sets the format to JPEG at quality 80, a good default for web photos.
Lossless PNG: A **Quick Preset** card. Sets the format to PNG at quality 100 for a lossless result.
WebP Small: A **Quick Preset** card. Sets the format to WebP at quality 75 for small file sizes.
Max Quality: A **Quick Preset** card. Sets the format to JPEG at quality 100 for the highest-quality JPEG.
re-encode only: The default option of the **Action** dropdown. Applies no saved action, so images are only re-encoded and resized to the chosen format and quality.
Format (Auto / JPEG / PNG / WebP / AVIF): A segmented control for the output file type of the batch. **Auto** runs the Optimize mode; AVIF needs the bundled WASM codec (loaded automatically).
New attachments: The **Save As** option that saves every result as a brand-new Media Library attachment, leaving the originals in place.
Overwrite (versioned): The **Save As** option that overwrites each source image in place, keeping a version so you can roll back.
Source Images / %d selected: The section header for the image list and its live count of how many attachments are queued (from library picks plus pasted IDs).
Remove (source image): The × on a picked image tile. Drops that attachment from the batch (available only for library-picked images, not pasted IDs).
No images yet: add from the library or paste IDs.: The empty state shown before any source image has been added.
Progress rows (…, spinner, done, error): The live per-image progress list. `…` means pending, a spinner means working, `done` is a link to the result, and errors show in red.
Processing…: The label on the primary button while the batch runs, replacing `Process N image(s)` and showing a spinner.
Batch finished: %1$d processed, %2$d failed.: The summary toast after a run, reporting how many images succeeded and how many failed.
Footer summary line: The footer text that previews the batch: image count, format and quality, and whether results become new attachments or overwrite (versioned).
AVIF Small: A **Quick Preset** card. Sets the format to AVIF at quality 60: the most modern codec with the smallest files for photos.
Web 1600: A **Quick Preset** card for content images: JPEG at quality 82, downscaled to at most 1600 px on the long side.
Email 1200: A **Quick Preset** card for images that travel by mail or newsletter: JPEG at quality 70, at most 1200 px on the long side.
already optimal: The per-image state in Optimize mode when overwriting would not save at least 5% or 10 KB. The original file is kept untouched and the summary toast counts these images separately.
open (result link): Each finished row in the **Results** list links to the saved file in a new tab, so you can inspect the output immediately.

sections.title: Generate from CSV: options and states
sections.text:
The export options, empty states and progress messages in the Series from CSV dialog.
The Generate from CSV dialog (`merge-dialog.jsx`) fills `{{key}}` placeholders in the current document from each CSV row and saves one Media Library image per row. These are the smaller controls and states not yet listed.
Format (PNG / JPEG / WebP): The output file type for every generated image. Note the default here is PNG, unlike the Batch Process dialog.
Quality (CSV series): A number field for the export quality of each generated image. Values outside the range are clamped.
None found. (no placeholders): The message shown when the document has no `{{placeholder}}` text yet. Type one like `{{title}}` into a text layer first; the placeholders define your CSV columns.
Progress rows (CSV): The live per-row list. `…` is pending, a spinner is working, `done` links to the saved image, and errors show in red. Rows are labeled by the name column value.
%d rows (CSV summary): After a CSV is chosen, the file name and its row count are shown next to the Choose CSV file button.
%d graphics generated.: The success toast after a run, reporting how many images were saved to the Media Library.

sections.title: Content Templates: option lists, defaults and states
sections.text:
The dropdown option values, section headers, default values and button states in the Content Templates editor.
The Content Templates dialog (`content-templates-dialog.jsx`) manages the reusable AI article recipes. These are the option lists and defaults behind its controls, plus its section headers and save/delete states.
Text provider options: The provider choices for the article text model. `Default text provider` uses the site default; the rest force a specific vendor.
Image provider options: The provider choices for the image model. `Default image provider` uses the site default.
Thinking budget options: How much reasoning the text model spends while writing. `Off` is fastest, `Extended (recommended)` gives the most thorough article.
Output language options: The language the finished article is written in. The prompt texts can stay in any language; the server injects an explicit output-language instruction from this setting.
Body aspect / Featured aspect options: The aspect ratios offered for the body images and the featured image dropdowns.
Output field ranges and defaults: Numeric limits for the output fields: **Body images** accepts 0 to 10 (default 3) and **Min. words** accepts 0 to 20000 (default 1200). A blank template also starts with Web search on, Deep research off, and Infographic on.
Starter (chip): A chip on read-only starter templates in the list. Editing and saving a starter creates your own user copy instead of changing the starter.
Save as copy / Create template / Save: The primary button changes with context: `Save as copy` for a starter, `Create template` for a new one, and `Save` when updating an existing user template.
Really delete?: The Delete button asks for a second click, turning into `Really delete?` before it removes a user template. Starters cannot be deleted.
Settings / Prompts / Output (section headers): The three grouping headers inside the form. `Settings` holds the thinking budget and research toggles, `Prompts` holds the system, image and directive prompts, and `Output` holds the image counts, aspects and word count.
Placeholders like {company}, {topic} or {focus_keyword}: The footer hint. Tokens like `{company}`, `{topic}` and `{focus_keyword}` written into the prompts are resolved from the brand kit and the current assignment.

sections.title: Generate Content: steps, option values and states
sections.text:
The pipeline step labels, dropdown option values, suggestion lists and progress states in the Generate Content dialog.
The Generate Content dialog (`create-post-dialog.jsx`) writes a full draft in one run. These are the individual progress steps, empty option values, suggestion pickers and progress states not covered by the main control list.
Write article: The first pipeline step. The AI writes the full structured article from the topic, keyword and context.
Body images: Pipeline step that generates the in-article images (count and aspect come from the content template).
Featured image: Pipeline step that produces the post's featured image, either from a dynamic template or as a plain AI image.
Social/OG image: Pipeline step that renders the Open Graph and Twitter share image.
Infographic: Pipeline step that builds the summarising infographic (when the content template has it enabled).
Create draft: The final step. Assembles the article and all images into a WordPress draft with SEO meta, tags and category.
AI image (no dynamic template): The default option of the **Dynamic template (featured image)** dropdown. The featured image is generated as a plain AI image instead of being composed from a template.
Without Brand Kit (option group): An option group in the dynamic-template dropdown holding templates that are not tied to any brand kit, shown below the selected kit's own templates.
No Brand Kit: The placeholder option shown in the **Brand Kit** dropdown when no brand kits exist yet.
No category: The default option of the **Category** dropdown. Leaves the draft uncategorised.
No action: The default option of the optional **Action** dropdown (shown when a dynamic template is chosen). Leaves the rendered featured image without a replayed editor action.
Topic idea rows: After **Suggest topics**, up to three clickable idea rows appear, each with a topic, focus keyword and a short rationale. Clicking one fills the Topic and Focus keyword fields.
Internal-link suggestion rows: After **Load suggestions**, matching posts and pages appear as toggle rows; selecting one adds a `URL | anchor` line to the internal links box. Deselecting removes it.
Internal links (one per line: URL | anchor text): The label and format for the internal links box. Put one link per line as the URL, then a pipe, then the anchor text.
No matching posts found.: Shown under the internal links box when Load suggestions returns nothing for the keyword or topic.
Progress header (Starting… / Step X of Y / Finished / Failed): The progress line above the bar. It reads `Starting…`, then `Step X of Y: label…`, ending in `Finished` or `Failed`, with elapsed time and a percentage on the right.
Draft #%d created.: The success panel after a run. Reports the new draft's post id and offers an Open draft in WordPress link.
No text-capable AI provider configured (warning): A banner shown when no text provider is set. Add an Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini key in the settings first; without it Generate is disabled.
No image provider configured (warning): A banner shown when text works but no image provider is set. The draft is created without any images.
Setup (section header): The header for the top row of the dialog holding Brand Kit, Content template and the featured-image dynamic template.
Thinking… / Searching… (loading labels): The Suggest topics button shows `Thinking…` while ideas load, and the Load suggestions button shows `Searching…` while link candidates load.

sections.title: Dynamic Template Shortcodes: sections and states
sections.text:
The three shortcode sections, the copy control, badge states and empty states inside the Dynamic Template Shortcodes dialog.
The Dynamic Template Shortcodes dialog (`shortcodes-dialog.jsx`) hands out shortcodes for the current design so it can be used outside Gutenberg (Classic editor, Elementor's shortcode widget, any builder). These are the section framing, copy control and states not yet listed.
Live Badge (section): The first card. Bakes a vector copy of the current design whose bound texts are substituted server-side as the page is served, ideal for prices and dates. That substitution lands in the page itself, so behind a full-page cache the badge is as fresh as that cached page and no fresher; editing the post refreshes both. Vector content only; pixel layers embed as static images. The badge is not a pixel-perfect copy of the editor preview: the browser lays out its text and complex layer effects are simplified - use a Dynamic Image when the embed must match the design exactly.
Personalized Image (section): The second card. Maps text layers to URL parameters (for example `?name=Anna`) and produces a shortcode that renders live in the visitor's browser. Requires the design to be saved as a dynamic template.
Dynamic Image (section): The third card. Produces a shortcode for a real baked image filled with the embedding post's data. Saves mark it stale and the next open editor session re-bakes it.
Copy: The button next to each read-only shortcode field. Copies the shortcode to the clipboard, showing `Shortcode copied.` on success or `Copy blocked` if the browser refuses (then select and copy by hand).
Baking… / Re-bake badge: The badge button shows `Baking…` while it works, then reads `Re-bake badge` once a badge exists. Re-bake after design changes; the shortcode itself stays the same.
Shortcode (chip): The small chip on each section header marking it as a shortcode-producing tool.
This design has no named text layers to personalize.: Shown in the Personalized Image card when the saved template has no named text layers to map to URL parameters.
Save this design as a dynamic template first (File, then Save as Dynamic Template): Shown in the Personalized Image and Dynamic Image cards when the current document is not yet a saved template. The shortcodes reference the template id, so the design must be saved first.

sections.title: Dynamic-image blocks: inspector options, help text and placeholders
sections.text:
The block-editor option values, busy labels, in-canvas placeholders and help text for the three dynamic-image Gutenberg blocks.
The Gutenberg blocks (`blocks.js`) put dynamic templates onto the site. Their block panels reuse the same Dynamic template picker and Width slider, but each has its own busy states, placeholders and help text documented here.
Select a template: The first option in the **Dynamic template** dropdown of every dynamic-image block. Nothing renders until a real template is chosen.
Rendering…: The busy label on the **Render now** button of the Dynamic Image block while it bakes the image.
Creating… / Create badge / Recreate badge: The Live Badge block button reads `Create badge` first, `Creating…` while it stores the SVG, and `Recreate badge` once a badge exists. Once created, the badge also re-bakes automatically whenever its dynamic template is updated in the editor.
Pick a dynamic template in the block settings.: The in-canvas placeholder shown by all three blocks before a template is selected.
Save the post (or press "Render now") to bake the image.: The Dynamic Image placeholder once a template is chosen but no image has been baked yet.
Press "Create badge" in the block settings.: The Live Badge placeholder once a template is chosen but no badge has been created yet.
Badge stored (%s).: The Live Badge placeholder after a badge is saved. The front end fills it with the post's current data (the template name is shown).
Re-rendered automatically on every save (help): The Dynamic Image panel help text: the image re-renders on every save with the post's current data, and the front end serves a real image file.
A vector badge, filled server-side (help): The Live Badge panel help text: a vector badge whose bound texts the server fills in as the page is served, so it follows its post with no re-render, and behind a page cache it is as current as the page it sits on. Vector-only designs work best; the browser lays out the badge text, so it is close to but not pixel-identical with the editor preview - pick the Dynamic Image block for an exact copy.
Map text layers to URL parameters (help): The Personalized Image panel help text: mapping a layer to a parameter means visiting `?name=Anna` replaces that layer's text live in the visitor's browser.
Block descriptions: The one-line descriptions shown in the block inserter: Dynamic Image is a real image baked on every save; Live Badge is a vector badge substituted server-side; Personalized Image renders per visitor with URL-parameter substitutions.

sections.title: Shortcode attributes and bake behavior
sections.text:
The attributes accepted by the three dynamic-image shortcodes and how they bake on the front end.
The shortcodes (`class-blocks.php`) mirror the blocks for non-Gutenberg builders. These are their attributes and the server-side bake behavior a user should know.
template (attribute): Required on `[wpie_dynamic_image]` and `[wpie_personalized]`. The id of the saved dynamic template to render. Without it the shortcode outputs nothing.
uid (attribute): Required on `[wpie_live_badge]`. The id of the stored badge SVG created when you baked the design.
width (attribute): Optional on all three shortcodes. The display width as a percent of the container. Values are clamped to the valid range.
map (attribute): Optional on `[wpie_personalized]`. Pipe-separated entries, each `layer:param:fallback`, mapping a text layer to a URL parameter with an optional fallback.
Bake-on-save and stale queue: Every save (Classic editor, REST, WooCommerce sync, bulk edit) marks a post's dynamic images stale; the next open editor session re-bakes them. Until the first bake lands, `[wpie_dynamic_image]` shows the template preview. The save scan also walks Elementor (_elementor_data) and Bricks layouts; Divi shortcodes live in the content itself. Fresh entries get a short grace period so the saving editor session bakes them alone, and a registry entry whose baked attachment was deleted heals itself with a fresh file instead of retrying forever.
Live badge SVG limit: A baked live badge SVG is sanitized (scripts, links and animation removed) and must stay under 4 MB, otherwise storing it is rejected.

sections.title: Cinematic Effects (overview & canvas)
sections.text:
A local WebGL engine that builds cinematic 3D backgrounds and effect overlays from stacked motifs, with no AI and no uploads.
A cinematic effect engine for backgrounds and overlays, computed live in your browser with WebGL: no AI, no uploads. Stack up to three motifs from a large curated library spanning energy, particle forms, light, atmosphere, a cosmos family with black holes and comets trailing real dust-and-ion tails, retro sci-fi, fluid and material looks such as liquid chrome and ink bloom, HUD holograms and glitch, neon signs and a music visualizer, raymarched volumetrics and a whole lens-and-film family with true lens flares, light leaks, film burn, dust and scratches.
A formation family can gather your own logo, layer or text out of dust and disperse it again. Finish with bloom, vignette, grain, scanlines, a kaleidoscope, seamless camera moves, refraction distortion, anamorphic lens streaks and shape or text masks. Tint everything with cinematic palettes or your brand kit, and everything loops seamlessly.
Open it from the **Extensions** menu. Insert stills as editable background or overlay layers, export a WebM loop, or copy an interactive HTML snippet that plays the live effect on your website. Presets, favorites and a surprise roll get you somewhere good fast.
Background: Sets the effect to fill the whole document as an opaque background layer, including its own dark backdrop. Use this when the effect is the base of your design.
Overlay: Sets the effect to render on transparent alpha so it sits on top of your existing design. Use this to add glow, particles or light over artwork you already have.
Show document: Renders your current design once and places it behind the transparent overlay preview, so you see the effect over the real artwork instead of the checkerboard. Only appears in Overlay mode when the editor can render the document. [Availability: Overlay mode only]
Drag to orbit: Click and drag on the preview to orbit the camera around the scene. This sets the horizontal and vertical camera angles.
Wheel to zoom: Scroll the mouse wheel over the preview to zoom. Beyond the classic range the camera first flies deep into the scene, then tightens its field of view like a telephoto lens for true macro close-ups - procedural effects stay perfectly sharp at any magnification.
Double-click for colors: Double-click the preview to jump to a random different palette. A quick way to try new color schemes without opening the palette list.
Seamless loop: Every animated value is built from whole-number cycles per loop, so the first and last frame are pixel-identical. This is why exported loops never jump.
Player & timeline: A transport bar under the preview: play or pause the loop and scrub the timeline to any moment. Stills and inserted layers bake exactly the frame you paused on, so you can snapshot the loop at its best.

sections.title: Effect library (left panel)
sections.text:
A browsable library of all 82 motifs with live-rendered preview tiles - click a tile to add or remove an effect.
The left panel lists every motif as a preview tile, grouped into the fifteen families. Thumbnails are rendered live by the effect engine itself, so each tile shows the real motif, not a static image.
Tiles of active effects are highlighted and carry a number badge showing the layer's position in the stack.
Preview tile: One tile per motif with a live-rendered thumbnail. Clicking a tile adds the effect to the stack; clicking it again removes it. When the stack is full with three layers, a click swaps the last layer for the picked motif, and the last remaining effect cannot be removed.
Family folders: Each family is a collapsible group with its motif count in the header. Fold the families you do not need to keep the list short; the panel remembers your folds while the editor stays open.
Search effects: The search field filters tiles by motif name across all families and temporarily opens every family with a match. Clearing the search restores your folds.
Stack badge: Active effects show a numbered badge on their tile. The number is the layer's position in the stack and matches the order of the layer cards in the right panel.

sections.title: Effect stack (per-layer controls)
sections.text:
Stack up to three motif layers, each with its own intensity, size, tempo, opacity, color, blend mode and variation.
The **Effects** card holds your stack of motif layers. Each layer picks one of the 82 motifs and has its own sliders. Layers composite from bottom to top, so a typical look is atmosphere plus energy plus a light accent.
The card header shows the current layer count (for example `Effects · 3`).
Effect: A dropdown that picks which of the 82 motifs this layer plays. It is grouped into the fifteen families (Energy, Particle forms, Light, Atmosphere, Cosmos, Retro sci-fi, Wonders, Fluid & material, Volumetric, Sculpted objects, Lens & film, Sci-fi & tech, Light color & music, Motion & organic, Waves & audio). Changing it rebuilds the layer with that motif's defaults but keeps your opacity.
Shuffle variation: The dice button on a layer rolls a fresh random variation seed for that motif, reshuffling its internal look (positions, rotations, arrangement) without touching your sliders. Use it to get a different take on the same motif.
Position (drag in preview): The crosshair button on a layer arms it for placement: drag in the preview and the effect follows the pointer in the camera plane, so every effect can sit at its own spot in 3D. Orbit first to place it in depth. A double-click in the preview sends the armed effect back to the center.
Remove effect: The small x on a layer deletes that layer from the stack. It is disabled when only one layer remains, since the stack always needs at least one motif.
Intensity: Controls the density, count or strike rate of the motif, for example the number of particles, beams, strikes or bars. Higher means busier and fuller.
Size: Controls the size of the motif's elements, for example beam length, particle spread, ring radius or globe size. Higher makes the elements larger.
Tempo: Controls how fast the motif animates. It maps to a whole-number of cycles per loop (1 to 6), which keeps the loop seamless at any tempo.
Opacity: Sets how strong this layer is in the mix. Lower it to let a layer sit quietly behind the others.
Color: Auto: The `A` swatch spreads the layer across all of the palette's colors automatically. This is the default and gives a varied, multi-color look.
Color: palette swatches: The four color chips lock the layer to a single palette color instead of the auto spread. Pick one to make the motif a single consistent hue.
Custom color: Opens the editor's own color picker to tint the layer with any exact hex color, overriding the palette. Uses the editor's swatch and popover, not a native OS picker.
Blend: Sets how this layer mixes with the layers below it. Add and Screen make it glow and brighten, Normal stacks it flatly, and Multiply darkens.
Source: For the Particle formation motif only, chooses whether the particles form from typed Text or from a captured editor Layer. Switches which input appears below.
Formation text: The text field (shown when Source is Text) types the word the particles gather to spell. Limited to 24 characters.
Use active layer: The button (shown when Source is Layer) captures the currently selected editor layer, trims it and uses its shape as the particle target. A thumbnail preview appears once captured.
Add effect: Adds another motif layer to the stack, up to three total. It picks a motif you are not already using. The button disappears once you have three layers.

sections.title: Look (palette, finish, camera & scene)
sections.text:
The global controls that tint, finish and shape the whole scene: palette, backdrop, bloom, vignette, grain, loop length, camera move, kaleidoscope, mirror, distortion, masks, color cycle, beat, morph and seed.
The **Look** card holds everything that applies to the whole scene rather than a single layer. It sets the color palette and backdrop, the post-processing finish (bloom, vignette, grain), the loop length, and a set of scene-wide transforms and rhythms.
All of these apply on top of your effect stack.
Palette: Picks the color scheme that tints every layer set to Auto or to a palette swatch. Shows eight curated palettes as gradient bars; click one to apply it.
Brand Kit palettes [Extension]: If your site has brand kits with at least two hex colors, they appear at the end of the palette row so you can tint effects with your own brand colors.
Backdrop: In Background mode, chooses the dark backdrop gradient behind the effect: the palette's own backdrop, or a fixed one. Choosing Custom reveals a color picker for your own backdrop tint. [Availability: Background mode only]
Bloom: Controls the glow bloom that spreads light from bright areas. Higher makes the whole effect softer and more luminous.
Vignette: Darkens the edges of the frame toward the corners. Higher focuses the eye on the center and adds a cinematic feel.
Grain: Film grain over the finished frame (0 to 100). Precision-safe noise at full pixel resolution, re-seeded 24 times per loop cycle - alive like real grain, yet the loop stays perfectly seamless. Background mode only.
Scanlines: CRT-style scanlines over the finished frame (0 to 100, default 0): a subtle two-pixel darkening rhythm, multiplicative so transparent pixels stay untouched. Background mode only, sits right below Grain.
Loop: Sets the length of the seamless loop in seconds. Shorter loops feel faster and busier; longer loops feel calmer.
Camera move: Chooses an automatic camera motion over the loop. Static holds still, 360 orbit circles the scene, Pendulum swings back and forth, and Dolly pushes in and out.
Kaleidoscope: Mirrors the frame into a number of radial segments for a symmetric kaleidoscope pattern. Off leaves the scene as-is.
Water mirror: A checkbox that adds a reflected copy of the scene in the lower half, like a still water surface. Good for skyline and cityscape looks.
Distortion: Applies a refraction field that warps the whole image. Heat haze shimmers, Water ripple waves, Glass bends smoothly, Shockwave pushes rings outward, and Gravity lens swirls space around an orbiting singularity.
Lens streaks: An anamorphic post pass that stretches the brightest highlights into horizontal, subtly blue-tinted flares - the cinema-lens signature. 0 turns it off.
Shape mask: Clips the whole effect inside a shape window so it only shows through that shape. Choose a circle, heart, star, or text outline. Text reveals a text field.
Mask text: The text field (shown when Shape mask is Text) sets the word whose letters mask the effect. Limited to 24 characters.
Color cycle: Rotates the hue of the whole scene over the loop, cycling through colors. Off keeps colors fixed; higher numbers make more full hue turns per loop.
Beat pulse: Pulses the overall brightness a set number of times per loop, like a beat. Off holds steady brightness.
Scene morph (A to B): A checkbox that seamlessly crossfades the scene between two variations of itself over the loop, so it slowly shifts from one arrangement to another and back.
Seed: The random seed that fixes the exact arrangement of every motif. The same seed always reproduces the same look. Type a value or press the dice to roll a new one.

sections.title: Color palettes
sections.text:
The eight built-in cinematic palettes that tint the effects.
Each palette is an ordered set of four colors (light to accent) plus a matching glow tint and dark backdrop gradient. Layers set to Auto spread across the four colors; layers set to a swatch pick one of them.
Electric Blue: Cool cyan-to-indigo blues. The default palette, good for tech, storm and hyperspace looks.
Neon Magenta: Hot pinks and magenta running into indigo. Suits laser shows, night city and synthwave.
Fire: Warm yellow, amber and orange into red. Suits embers, flames and solar looks.
Toxic: Acid lime and green into cyan. A punchy cyber and data palette.
Ice: White into pale sky blue. Clean and cold, good for aurora, chrome and polar looks.
Gold: Cream and amber into deep gold. Warm and luxurious, good for dust and noir looks.
Violet Storm: Lavender into deep violet. A dreamy, cosmic palette for nebula and enchanted looks.
Mono: White into slate grey, near-neutral. Lets custom colors, color cycling or holo foil carry the hue.

sections.title: Surprise & favorites
sections.text:
Roll a curated random look, optionally locked to your colors, and save looks you like.
The **Surprise** card composes a plausible cinematic stack from curated ranges (base plus energy plus light accent), never uniform chaos. The **Favorites** card stores looks you want to keep in local storage.
Surprise me!: Rolls a fresh curated look and applies it instantly: a random palette, backdrop, finish and a sensible two or three layer stack, each with its own variation seed. Keeps your current mode (background or overlay).
Colors: A dropdown that locks the color of every surprise roll. Leave it on Random colors, or pick a brand kit or a named palette so every roll lands on your chosen colors. Remembered per user.
Save as favorite: The star button saves the current look (palette plus lead motif name and full settings) to your favorites for later reuse. Favorites are saved with your WordPress account, so they follow you across browsers and devices.
Favorite chip: Each saved favorite appears as a labeled chip. Click it to reload that exact look while keeping your current mode.
Remove favorite: The small x on a favorite chip deletes that favorite from your list.

sections.title: Presets (curated looks)
sections.text:
Twenty-nine curated one-click looks, each a full recipe of palette, backdrop, finish and a two-to-three-effect stack.
Each preset chip loads a complete look: palette, backdrop, bloom/vignette/grain, camera and a curated two or three layer stack. It keeps your current mode. Presets are a fast starting point you can then tweak.
The studio opens on the first preset, Thunderfront, by default.
Thunderfront: An Electric Blue storm: fog banks, lightning strikes and god rays over the palette backdrop.
Hyperspace: An Ice warp tunnel with anamorphic flares on black. A fast forward rush.
Deep Space: A Violet nebula with a particle sphere floating in it.
Cyber Pulse: A Toxic wave grid with pulse waves and a laser fan on charcoal.
Fire Night: A Fire scene of rising embers, fog and warm god rays.
Polar Light: An Ice aurora with a faint nebula on a midnight backdrop.
Gold Dust: Golden embers with god rays and soft fog.
Laser Show: A Magenta laser fan with pulse waves and fog on black.
Neon Net: A Toxic plexus net with an energy orb and anamorphic flares on charcoal.
Noir Smoke: Gold smoke with light pillars and embers on black, heavy vignette.
Outrun: A Magenta synthwave grid with a starfield and anamorphic flares.
Event Horizon: A Gold black hole with a starfield and infalling debris on black.
Star Death: An Ice supernova inside a nebula with a meteor shower.
Stardust Sign: Gold particle formation spelling WOW with a starfield behind it.
Liquid Metal: Ice liquid chrome with caustics, glass distortion on, on black.
Data Stream: A Toxic circuit flow with a HUD hologram and glitch on charcoal.
Solar Storm: A Fire solar surface with a comet and embers, beat pulse 4, on black.
Spectrum: A Mono holo foil with a prism split and music visualizer, color cycle 2x, on black.
Firefly Meadow: Gold fireflies with falling petals and fog on a midnight backdrop.
Sound Wave: Magenta neon silk waves with an audio waveform on black.
Visualizer: A Toxic wave field visualizer with spectrum bars and neon flow lines on black.
Storm Volume: Raymarched storm clouds lit from inside by lightning, finished with anamorphic lens streaks on the electric palette.
Chrome Dream: A polished chrome knot floating in fog with embers and lens streaks - cool studio metal on ice.
Crystal Rift: Crystal shards over a violet nebula, warped by the gravity-lens distortion.
Alien Core: A gyroid lattice around liquid metal blobs in toxic green, with lens streaks.
Sun Flare: A full lens flare with iris ghosts over soft fog, plus star glints on the fire palette - a cinematic sun hit.
Golden Hour: Light leaks, a sunbeam dust shaft and golden bokeh - warm late-afternoon glow for photos.
Premiere Night: Spotlight sweeps crossing over bokeh and star glints - the red-carpet opening shot.
Vintage Reel: Film dust and scratches, film burn and a soft light leak with heavy grain - an old projected print.

sections.title: Motifs: Energy
sections.text:
Seven high-voltage motifs: lightning, laser fan, pulse waves, electric arcs, energy orb, fireworks and electron orbitals.
The Energy family covers bright electric and explosive effects. They read as the active, hard-hitting layer in a stack. Intensity, Size and Tempo on each layer control the count, scale and speed.
Lightning storm: Branching lightning bolts strike down with an ambient sky flash and a fading afterglow between hits.
Laser fan: A fan of straight laser beams spreading from a bright source point, with a haze glow.
Pulse waves: Concentric rings expanding outward from a glowing core, like a radar or sonar ping.
Electric arcs: Jittery horizontal electric arcs crackling between glowing end-orbs.
Energy orb: A glowing core sphere ringed by orbiting sparks and surface crackle arcs.
Fireworks: Shells that launch and burst into showering sparks that fall and fade.
Electron orbitals: Three tilted particle rings spinning around a bright core at different speeds, each shell carrying its own electron highlight.

sections.title: Motifs: Particle forms
sections.text:
Six structured particle motifs: wave grid, sphere, tunnel, plexus, starfield and DNA.
The Particle forms family builds recognizable geometric particle structures. They work well as the base layer of a scene.
Wave grid: A flat grid of points rippling with two crossing travelling waves, like a rolling landscape of dots.
Particle sphere: A breathing sphere of particles that gently pulse in and out.
Warp tunnel: A forward rush through a tunnel of streaming particles with a clear central bore.
Plexus net: A constellation of nodes joined by lines between near neighbours. The net reacts to the pointer, pushing away from the cursor.
Starfield: A drifting field of stars with a few shooting stars streaking across each loop.
DNA helix: A rotating double helix of two particle strands joined by rungs, kept perfectly in sync.

sections.title: Motifs: Light
sections.text:
Five beam and glow motifs: god rays, anamorphic flares, aurora, light pillars and bokeh lights.
The Light family adds atmospheric light and lens effects. They shine as accent layers on top of a busier base.
God rays: Radiating shafts of light from a bright point, with drifting dust motes floating in the beams.
Anamorphic flares: Wide horizontal lens flares (the cinematic streak) with a bright core that pulses.
Aurora: Luminous curtains of northern lights that wave and shimmer.
Light pillars: Vertical beams of light rising like stage spotlights or aurora columns.
Bokeh lights: Out-of-focus lights: big soft discs drifting on tiny loops and breathing in brightness - a photographic backdrop staple.

sections.title: Motifs: Atmosphere
sections.text:
Five ambience motifs: fog banks, nebula, sparks and embers, smoke and neon rain.
The Atmosphere family fills the scene with soft volumetric haze and floating particles. They make excellent quiet base or mid layers.
Fog banks: Slow drifting clouds of soft fog puffs that add depth and haze.
Nebula: Billowing clouds of colored gas with a scattering of stars, like a deep-space cloud.
Sparks & embers: Glowing embers rising and floating upward like sparks from a fire.
Smoke: Billowing rising columns of soft smoke.
Neon rain: Glowing rain streaks falling on a seamless wrap, with a faint ground glow where they land.

sections.title: Motifs: Cosmos
sections.text:
Nine space motifs: black holes, supernovae, planets, debris, meteors, galaxies, solar surfaces, comets and pulsars.
The Cosmos family is the largest, covering deep-space phenomena. Many make strong single-subject centerpieces for a scene.
Black hole: A dark event horizon ringed by a swirling accretion disk, a thin photon ring and matter spiralling inward.
Supernova: A star that gathers, collapses, then flashes and bursts outward with an expanding shockwave.
Neon planet: A neon wireframe globe with surface city lights, a glowing atmosphere and an orbiting satellite.
Debris field: Rim-lit rock shards tumbling through a haze of fine dust.
Meteor shower: Meteors streaking across a background star field.
Galaxy spiral: A rotating spiral galaxy with two or three arms and a bright glowing core.
Solar surface: A churning, turbulent star surface with a glowing corona and edge flares.
Comet: A real comet: white-hot core inside a colored coma, a curved dust tail that widens and fades behind the head, a straighter ion tail at a slight angle and sparkling debris - all trailing the head along its arc across the frame.
Pulsar beacon: A spinning neutron star firing sweeping beams with expanding rings pulsing outward.

sections.title: Motifs: Retro sci-fi
sections.text:
Six retro-futuristic motifs: synthwave grid, time tunnel, fractal morph, glyph rain, portal and tesseract.
The Retro sci-fi family delivers 80s and cyberpunk looks. They pair naturally with the Neon Magenta and Toxic palettes.
Synthwave grid: A retro perspective grid receding to the horizon with a striped retro sun.
Time tunnel: A tunnel of glowing rings rushing past the camera.
Fractal morph: A morphing Julia-set fractal that slowly changes shape over the loop.
Glyph rain: Falling columns of glowing glyphs with bright leading heads, the classic code-rain look.
Portal: A swirling dimensional portal with a shimmer ring racing along the rim and crackle across the mouth.
Tesseract: Nested rotating wireframe cubes suggesting the four-dimensional hypercube, with glowing corner nodes.

sections.title: Motifs: Wonders
sections.text:
Three motifs around the particle formation: your text or layer built from stardust, dissolved to dust, plus lava metaballs.
The Wonders family is now centered on the particle formation pair: build your own text or a captured layer out of particles, or dissolve it to dust and back. Lava metaballs round the family off.
Particle formation: Particles gather to form your typed text or a captured layer's shape, hold it, then scatter and reform. Pick the source with the Source control on the layer.
Lava metaballs: Blobs of molten lava that flow together and split apart like a lava lamp.
Dust dissolve: The formation's sibling: your typed text or captured layer disintegrates into drifting ash as a wave sweeping across it, then reassembles - once per loop.

sections.title: Motifs: Fluid & material
sections.text:
Four material motifs: ferrofluid, liquid chrome, ink bloom and caustics.
The Fluid & material family simulates flowing substances and surfaces. Several use GPU shaders for smooth, organic movement.
Ferrofluid: A spiked magnetic-fluid ball whose radial spikes pulse in and out as the whole shape rotates.
Liquid chrome: A flowing liquid-metal surface with banded, shifting reflections.
Ink bloom: Ink spreading outward into soft blooming clouds.
Caustics: Rippling underwater light patterns like the shifting bright lines on a pool floor.

sections.title: Motifs: Sci-fi & tech
sections.text:
Five interface motifs: HUD hologram, glitch datamosh, circuit flow, radar sweep and hex pulse.
The Sci-fi & tech family adds interface, glitch and hardware looks. Good for data, cyber and dashboard themes.
HUD hologram: A rotating wireframe globe with HUD rings, scale ticks, a vertical scan bar and blinking reticle blips.
Glitch datamosh: Datamosh glitch bands with per-row jitter, RGB-split fringing and scanlines.
Circuit flow: A circuit board of traces with pulse packets running along the lines and nodes blinking at intersections.
Radar sweep: A radar screen with rings, a crosshair and a rotating sweep wedge that lights up blips as it passes.
Hex pulse: A honeycomb lattice of glowing rings with a radial pulse sweeping outward from the center.

sections.title: Motifs: Light, color & music
sections.text:
Five spectral motifs: prism split, holo foil, neon sign, music visualizer and chroma rings.
The Light, color & music family plays with spectrum color and audio-reactive looks. Note that these animate to internal rhythm; there is no live microphone input.
Prism split: A white beam entering a prism and splitting into a rainbow fan on the other side.
Holo foil: A shifting iridescent holographic-foil sheen that sweeps rainbow bands across the frame.
Neon sign: A glowing neon sign (a rounded frame around an inner wave) with a subtle electric flicker.
Music visualizer: A radial ring of bars radiating outward and pulsing like an audio equalizer to an internal beat.
Chroma rings: Concentric chroma rings breathing outward, palette colors cycling ring by ring around a soft core.

sections.title: Motifs: Motion & organic
sections.text:
Seven kinetic motifs: crystal shatter, mobius ribbon, fireflies, falling petals, flames, light trails and firefly swarm.
The Motion & organic family mixes geometric motion with natural, drifting movement. A versatile set of accent and base layers.
Crystal shatter: A crystalline shattered-glass cell pattern with glowing cracks that flicker between the facets.
Mobius ribbon: A rotating figure-eight Mobius ribbon with light pulses running along its path.
Fireflies: Gently wandering, twinkling fireflies that drift organically around the frame.
Falling petals: Petals drifting and swaying from side to side as they fall downward.
Flames: Wavering upright flame tongues that flicker along the bottom of the frame.
Light trails: Streaks of light flowing across the frame at varied depths and speeds, like long-exposure traffic.
Firefly swarm: A whole swarm of glowing motes moving together in gentle flocking loops - denser and busier than the calm fireflies.

sections.title: Motifs: Waves & audio
sections.text:
Seven wave motifs: audio waveform, neon silk waves, wave field visualizer, dot wave, neon flow lines, spectrum bars and water ripples.
The Waves & audio family, added in v2.2, gives sound-visualizer and flowing-wave looks. Like the music motifs, they animate to internal rhythm rather than live audio.
Audio waveform: A travelling audio waveform drawn as a row of vertical bars that rise and fall with the wave.
Neon silk waves: Flowing rainbow silk lines that ripple across the frame like layered ribbons.
Wave field visualizer: A rippling 3D grid of dots with rising spike bars, like a landscape equalizer.
Dot wave: A grid of dots undulating in a wave, with a bouncing marker strip riding over the top.
Neon flow lines: Ribbons of merged neon glows flowing in overlapping waves, with occasional bright sparks.
Spectrum bars: A row of vertical spectrum bars bouncing up and down to an internal beat.
Water ripples: Expanding water rings from scattered drop points, overlapping into a calm interference pattern.

sections.title: Motifs: Volumetric
sections.text:
Three raymarched volume motifs: volumetric storm, gyroid structure and liquid metal blobs.
These motifs march rays through a true 3D volume instead of drawing sprites, so light and depth behave like real matter.
Volumetric storm: A 3D cloud slab lit from inside by loop-safe lightning flashes - a storm front with real volume and depth.
Gyroid structure: An endless gyroid lattice the camera flies through, exactly one period per loop for a seamless infinite flight.
Liquid metal blobs: Molten metal blobs that merge and split in 3D, shaded with color bands and a fresnel rim.

sections.title: Motifs: Sculpted objects
sections.text:
Three sculpted showpieces: chrome knot, crystal shards and cube ocean.
Real 3D geometry with studio-style shading - centerpiece objects rather than particle fields.
