Week planner: A weekly planner with the seven days as columns and writing lines under each, for a printable to-do or agenda page. Built around any date inside the week you want.
Timetable: A school or class timetable: weekday columns against period rows, with period start times generated automatically from a start time and length.
Habit tracker: A monthly habit tracker: one row per habit against a check cell for every day of the chosen month. Type your habits and pick the month.
Opening hours: An opening-hours card listing each weekday with its hours, and closed days shown as such. For a shop or office. No date is needed.

sections.title: Date (moment controls)
sections.text:
The Date panel sets which moment the calendar shows; the exact fields shown depend on the calendar type.
Depending on the type, this panel shows a month picker, a year, a month count, a week date, a birth date and life settings, or a countdown target. Fields that do not apply to the current type are hidden.
The whole Date panel is hidden entirely for Opening hours, Birthday, Advent and Timetable, which do not need a specific moment.
Month: A dropdown of the twelve month names in your site language. Sets which month the Month, Habit tracker and (as start month) Several months views show. [Shown for: Month, Several months, Habit tracker]
Start month: The same month dropdown, relabeled when the type is Several months. It sets the first tile; following months roll forward from here, wrapping into the next year if needed. [Shown for: Several months]
Year: A number field for the calendar year. Used by month, multi-month, year, moon, wheel, habit, wall and pixel calendars.
Months: How many months the Several months view tiles. Two and three sit in one or two rows; four uses two columns; six uses three. [Shown for: Several months]
Week: A date picker for the Week planner. Any day inside the week you want works; the planner shows the seven days of that week, aligned to your week start. [Shown for: Week planner]
Birth date: Your date of birth for the Life calendar. It sets how many cells (weeks or years) are filled in as already lived. [Shown for: Life calendar]
Life expectancy: A slider for the total number of years the Life calendar covers. It sets the overall size of the grid. [Shown for: Life calendar]
Type (In weeks / In years): Chooses whether the Life calendar counts in weeks (a 52-column grid) or in years (a 10-column grid). Weeks give the dense classic look; years are calmer. [Shown for: Life calendar]
Target date: The date the Countdown counts down to. The poster shows the number of days from today until this date. [Shown for: Countdown]
Label (optional): Free text shown under the countdown number. Leave it empty and the calendar fills in a default like `until the target 24 December 2026`. [Shown for: Countdown]

sections.title: Options
sections.text:
Display toggles and layout settings; each option appears only for the calendar types it affects.
The Options panel gathers the small switches and dropdowns that fine-tune a calendar: week start, week numbers, weekend shading, the today marker, moon extras, transparent background, plus the writing lines, holidays and timetable settings.
Only the options relevant to the current type are shown, so this panel looks different for a month grid than for a timetable.
Week starts on: Whether weeks begin on Monday or Sunday. It rotates the weekday column headers and the day grid to match. [Shown for: Month, Several months, Year, Week planner]
Week numbers: Shows ISO week numbers down the left side of the month grid. Useful for planning and for European business calendars. [Shown for: Month]
Tint weekends: Softly shades Saturday and Sunday so weekends stand out from work days. [Shown for: Month, Several months, Year, Week planner, Habit tracker, Wall planner]
Mark today: Highlights the current day in the grid, but only when the shown month and year are the current ones. [Shown for: Month]
Neighbor months: Adds small previous-month and next-month grids in a strip above the main month, wrapping the year at December and January. [Shown for: Month]
Moon phases: Draws small moon-phase icons on the days they occur inside the month grid, computed locally. [Shown for: Month]
Moon ring: Adds a band of moon phases around the Year wheel, showing the lunar cycle across the year. [Shown for: Year wheel]
Season markers: Adds equinox and solstice rays and labels (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter) to the Year wheel, marking the start of each season. [Shown for: Year wheel]
Transparent background: Drops the solid background so the calendar sits on whatever is behind it in your document. Only the grid, text and markers are drawn.
Writing lines: How many writing lines appear under each day column of the Week planner, for notes and tasks. [Shown for: Week planner]
Holidays: Adds public holidays for a country as red dot markers, and (for a single month) into the legend. Choose None to turn it off. [Shown for: Month, Several months, Year, Wall planner]
Days: How many weekday columns the Timetable shows: five (Mon to Fri), six (adds Saturday) or seven (full week). [Shown for: Timetable]
Periods: How many period rows the Timetable has. Each row gets an automatic start time based on the start time and length. [Shown for: Timetable]
Start time: The clock time the first Timetable period begins. Later period times are calculated from here. [Shown for: Timetable]
Minutes each: How many minutes each Timetable period lasts. This spacing sets the start time printed on every following row. [Shown for: Timetable]

sections.title: Markers and highlights
sections.text:
Mark birthdays, events and date ranges either by adding dates in this panel or by clicking days right in the preview.
The Highlights panel manages every marked day. Add a single date, or a start and end date for a range, using the two date fields and the plus button. You can also click days directly in the month, multi-month or year preview to toggle a marker on or off.
Each highlight in the list has a shape button, a color swatch, its date, an optional name, and a remove button. Named highlights can flow into an automatic legend under the grid, and ranges appear as soft pills across the days they cover.
This panel is shown for Month, Several months, Year, Year wheel, Birthday, Wall planner and Year in pixels. For Year in pixels it is used to color days and label each color.
Add date: The first date field in the add row. Sets the day you want to mark. Fill it in, then press the plus button to add it to the list.
Until (optional): The second date field. Set it to turn a single day into a date range, which is drawn as a soft pill spanning those days. Leave it empty for a single-day marker.
Add (+): The plus button that commits the date (or date range) from the fields into the highlights list. Duplicate dates are ignored.
Click days in the preview: On month, multi-month and year previews you can click a day to add a marker and click it again to remove it. The list and preview stay in sync.
Marker shape: The small symbol button on each highlight row. Click it to cycle through the eight marker shapes for that single date. Hidden for date ranges, which are drawn as pills.
Marker color: The color swatch on each highlight row. Sets the accent color for that marker. Left unset, it uses the theme accent color.
Name (optional): A text field on each highlight for a label like a person or event name. Named highlights appear in the automatic legend, and drive the entries and colors of the Birthday and Year-in-pixels calendars.
Remove: The X button on a highlight row deletes that marker from the list and the preview.
Legend below the grid: When on, named highlights (and holidays, for a single month) are listed as a text line under the calendar, wrapped across lines as needed. [Shown for: Month, Several months, Year]
Import ICS / CSV: Reads an `.ics` or `.csv` file and merges its dates into the highlights list, skipping duplicates. A quick way to pull in events from another calendar app.
Date-range pills: A highlight with an Until date is drawn as a soft rounded pill across the covered days instead of a per-day symbol, so multi-day events (holidays, trips) read as one band.
Automatic legend: The named highlights and holidays of the visible scope are gathered into legend text lines automatically, joined with dot separators and wrapped near 58 characters per line.
Color days to build the legend: For the Year in pixels type, the highlights panel note changes: give each single day a color and a name, and every distinct labeled color becomes a legend swatch under the pixel grid.

sections.title: Marker shapes
sections.text:
The eight symbols a single-day marker can take, cycled with the shape button on each highlight row.
Every single-day highlight uses one of eight shapes. Click the shape button on a highlight row to step through them. Date ranges do not use a shape; they draw as pills instead.
Circle: A filled accent circle around or on the day. The default marker, good for a clear positive highlight like a birthday.
Ring: An open ring outline around the day, a lighter touch than the filled circle.
Square: A square marker on the day, a boxy alternative to the circle.
Star: A star marker, for days you want to feel special or celebratory.
Heart: A heart marker, for anniversaries and personal favorites.
Dot: A small dot on the day, the most subtle marker. Public holidays also use a dot.
Underline: A line under the day number, marking it without covering the number.
Strike: A line through the day, useful for crossing off or marking a day as blocked or past.

sections.title: Opening hours
sections.text:
Fills in the weekly hours for the Opening hours card, one text field per weekday.
Shown only for the Opening hours type. Type the hours for each day (for example `9:00 – 18:00`). Leave a day empty and it shows as closed.
Weekday hours field: One free-text field per weekday (Monday through Sunday, in your site language) where you type that day's opening hours. Whatever you type is shown as-is on the card.
Closed: Any weekday field left empty is rendered as Closed on the card. This is the placeholder text shown in the empty field.

sections.title: Habits
sections.text:
Lists the habits tracked, one per line, for the Habit tracker calendar.
Shown only for the Habit tracker type. Each non-empty line becomes one row in the tracker against the days of the chosen month.
Habits list: A multi-line text box, one habit per line. Each line becomes a tracker row with a check cell for every day of the selected month. Blank lines are ignored.

sections.title: Theme
sections.text:
Eight ready-made color themes, chosen from a grid of swatch tiles; picking one resets any manual color overrides.
Each theme sets a background, text, muted and accent color at once. Click a tile to apply it. Choosing a theme clears any custom colors you set in the Colors panel, so you start fresh from the theme.
Midnight: A deep navy dark theme with a bright sky-blue accent. Calm and modern.
Black: A near-black theme with a warm golden accent. High contrast and premium.
Violet: A dark purple theme with a soft violet accent. Playful and rich.
Forest: A dark green theme with a light mint accent. Natural and grounded.
Ocean: A dark teal theme with a muted cyan accent. Cool and quiet.
Golden: A black theme where both text and accent are warm gold, for an elegant monochrome-gold look.
Paper: A light warm-cream theme with near-black text and a terracotta accent. The default; a printable, editorial look.
Blush: A light pink theme with a deep-rose text and a pink accent. Soft and warm.

sections.title: Colors
sections.text:
Override the theme's background, text and accent colors individually, with an Auto reset per color.
The Colors panel lets you fine-tune the three main colors on top of the chosen theme. Each color starts from the theme and can be overridden. Press Auto next to a color to drop your override and go back to the theme's value.
Picking a new theme clears all three overrides.
Background: The color behind the whole calendar. Overrides the theme background. Has no visible effect when Transparent background is on.
Text: The main ink color for day numbers, titles and labels. Overrides the theme text color.
Accent: The highlight color used for markers, the today marker and accents. Overrides the theme accent. It is also the default color for new markers.
Auto: The small reset button beside each color. Removes your custom color for that slot and returns it to the theme's value.

sections.title: Text block
sections.text:
An optional title, subtitle and text-size control that are inserted as real editable text layers above the grid.
Shown only when creating a new calendar (not when editing an existing one). The title and subtitle are pre-filled to match your type and moment until you type your own, and both are inserted as separate text layers so you can restyle them afterward.
When editing an existing calendar the text block is hidden, because the title and subtitle already exist as their own layers you can edit directly.
Title: The large heading above the calendar, rendered in uppercase Montserrat. Pre-filled from the type and date (for example the month and year) until you type your own. [Shown for: New calendars only]
Subtitle: A smaller line under the title, in uppercase Inter. For the Life calendar it is pre-filled with a lived-versus-total stat; otherwise it starts empty. [Shown for: New calendars only]
Text size: A slider that scales the title, subtitle and legend text together, as a percentage of their default size. [Shown for: New calendars only]

sections.title: Studio panels (section headings)
sections.text:
The labeled section headings that split the Calendars side panel into groups.
The right-hand side of the Calendars dialog is divided into labeled sections. Each heading marks one group of controls. Sections show or hide themselves depending on the calendar type you pick, so you only ever see the controls that apply.
Type: Heading over the grid of 15 calendar-type tiles. Click a tile to switch the whole calendar to that type.
Date: Heading over the moment controls (month, year, month count, week date, birth date, life expectancy, target date and label). Only the rows that apply to the current type are shown.
Options: Heading over the toggles and dropdowns that fine-tune the grid, such as week start, week numbers, holidays and timetable layout.
Highlights: Heading over the tools that mark special days: the add-date row, the ICS/CSV import, the legend toggle and the list of marked dates.
Hours: Heading over the seven weekday text fields used by the Opening hours card. Shown only when the type is Opening hours. [Shown for: Opening hours only]
Habits: Heading over the multi-line habit list for the Habit tracker. Shown only when the type is Habit tracker. [Shown for: Habit tracker only]
Theme: Heading over the grid of color-theme swatches. Pick a theme to set the background, text and accent colors at once.
Colors: Heading over the three per-color overrides (Background, Text, Accent) that let you tweak the chosen theme. A brand-kit picker sits here too: choose one of the site's brand kits and the accent comes from its palette.
Typography: Heading over the font controls. It sets the family used for the calendar grid and for the poster texts; leaving it on the default follows the editor.
Text block: Heading over the poster title, subtitle and text-size controls. This section appears only when you are inserting a new calendar, not when editing an existing one. [Shown when: Inserting only, not editing]

sections.title: Week start and holiday options
sections.text:
The individual choices inside the Week starts on and Holidays dropdowns.
These are the option values you can pick from the two main dropdown menus. The week-start choice rotates every grid; the holiday choice adds official public holidays as small dots and legend lines.
Monday: Sets the first column of every week to Monday (ISO style). This is the default.
Sunday: Sets the first column of every week to Sunday, the common layout in the US and some other regions.
None: Adds no public holidays. This is the default; the calendar shows only the days you mark yourself.
Germany: Adds German public holidays automatically, computed locally, shown as dots on the grid and listed in the legend.
Austria: Adds Austrian public holidays automatically, shown as dots and added to the legend.
Switzerland: Adds Swiss public holidays automatically, shown as dots and added to the legend.

sections.title: Year wheel season labels
sections.text:
The four season names printed on the circular Year wheel when Season markers is on.
When the **Season markers** toggle is enabled for the Year wheel type, the ring gets equinox and solstice rays labeled with the four seasons. The words are translated to your site language.
Spring: Label placed at the spring equinox ray on the Year wheel. [Shown for: Year wheel with Season markers]
Summer: Label placed at the summer solstice ray on the Year wheel. [Shown for: Year wheel with Season markers]
Autumn: Label placed at the autumn equinox ray on the Year wheel. [Shown for: Year wheel with Season markers]
Winter: Label placed at the winter solstice ray on the Year wheel. [Shown for: Year wheel with Season markers]

sections.title: Inline hints and notes
sections.text:
The small helper lines printed under controls and next to the dialog title.
Calendars prints short guidance strings in several places: under the dialog title, under the Highlights add-row, and under the Hours and Habits fields. They tell you what a section expects.
Adjust the calendar, the layer updates in place.: Subtitle shown under the dialog title when you reopen an existing calendar with Edit Calendars. It reminds you that saving updates the same layer rather than adding a new one. [Shown when: Editing]
Month grids, year overviews and opening hours, as editable layers.: Subtitle shown under the dialog title when you open Calendars to insert a new calendar. It summarizes what the studio can produce. [Shown when: Inserting]
Birthdays, events - marked with an accent circle.: Note under the Highlights add-row for grid types. It explains that added dates are drawn with an accent-colored marker. [Shown for: Month, Several months, Year, Year wheel, Birthday, Wall planner]
Click days directly in the preview to toggle them.: Second half of the Highlights note. It tells you that you can click a day in the live preview to mark it, and click again to remove it, without typing a date.
Color days in the preview to build the legend.: Note that replaces the normal Highlights hint when the type is Year in pixels. It explains that colored days feed the automatic mood legend. [Shown for: Year in pixels]
Leave a day empty to show it as closed.: Note under the Hours section. Any weekday field left blank is rendered as Closed on the opening-hours card.
One habit per line.: Note under the Habits text area. Each line of text becomes one row in the habit tracker grid.

sections.title: Status and error messages
sections.text:
The transient status and error strings shown while rendering, importing or inserting.
These messages appear in the small status line under the preview, or as a toast, while Calendars works or when something goes wrong.
Rendering the calendar: Status shown after you press Insert Calendar or Update Calendar while the high-resolution image is being baked.
Could not insert the calendar.: Error shown if the insert or update step fails for a reason without its own message.
Could not read the file.: Error shown when an imported ICS or CSV file cannot be parsed or read from disk.
No dates found in the file.: Error shown when an imported file was read but contained no usable dates to add as highlights.
Calendars needs WunderPaint 1.144 or newer.: Error shown if the host editor is too old to provide the document bridge the extension relies on. Update the plugin to use Calendars. [Requires: WunderPaint 1.144+]

sections.title: Defaults and automatic text
sections.text:
Prefilled values, auto-generated titles, and the names of the layers Calendars creates.
Several Calendars fields start with sensible defaults, and the title and subtitle fill themselves in from the current setup until you type your own. When you insert, the result is a named group of editable layers.
Sport, Reading, Drink water: The three habits the Habit tracker starts with. Edit or replace them in the Habits text area, one habit per line.
Automatic title suggestion: The Title field fills itself from the current type and date until you type your own text. For example a Month becomes `July 2026`, a Year becomes `2026`, a Moon calendar becomes `Moon calendar 2026`, a Life calendar becomes `My life`, a Birthday calendar becomes `Birthdays`, and a Week planner becomes `Week 29 · 2026`.
Automatic subtitle (life stat): For the Life calendar, the Subtitle fills itself with your lived total, for example `1,742 / 4,680 Weeks` or a years count, using the words Weeks or Years. It stops updating once you type your own subtitle. [Shown for: Life calendar]
Back to the theme color: Tooltip on the Auto reset button next to each color override. Pressing it drops your custom color and returns that slot to the theme's value.
until the target: The default caption printed under the big countdown number when you leave the Label field empty. It is joined with the formatted target date, for example `until the target 24 December 2026`.
Calendar: The name given to the baked grid image layer, and the prefix of the group that holds the calendar plus its text, for example `Calendar: July 2026`. This is how you find the calendar in the Layers panel.
Legend: The layer name given to each automatic legend line inserted under the grid when Legend below the grid is on.

sections.title: Smart Diagrams dialog
sections.text:
SmartArt-class diagrams: 22 diagram types in five families, inserted as a named group of real shape and text layers.
SmartArt-class diagrams as fully editable layers: process flows, snakes and chevron bands, timelines and quarter roadmaps, funnels, pyramids, cycles, hub-and-spoke, pillars, target rings, org charts and mind maps, SWOT and 2x2 matrices, Venn diagrams, pros and cons, and kanban boards.
Content comes from a guided form, a quick text outline, or an AI assist that extracts the structure from any pasted text. Style presets render live previews with your real content, brand-kit palettes and the full editor font library apply, and every node can carry an icon or emoji. Preview the diagram over your current design, drag any box and the connectors re-route to follow it, click a label to edit it right on the canvas, and restyle a single connector if you like.
Open it from the **Extensions** menu. Every diagram lands as a named group of real shape and text layers, laid out for your document format, and reopens via **Edit Smart Diagrams**.
Title: An optional headline above the diagram; it becomes its own text layer.
Diagram type: A grouped dropdown of all 22 types. Switching the type re-lays the same content out, so trying shapes is free.

sections.title: Content (form, outline, derive)
sections.text:
Three ways in: a guided form, a quick text outline, or an AI assist that extracts the structure from any pasted text.
Items carry a title, an optional description and, for some types, a tag or bucket. The form and the outline stay in sync, so you can switch between them at any time.
Form: One row per item with title and description, reorder arrows and remove. Grouped types (SWOT, Kanban, Venn) add a bucket selector per row.
Icon / emoji per item: The badge button on a form row opens the editor's icon and emoji picker (search plus tabs); # returns to the plain number badge. The chosen icon replaces the number in the diagram.
Outline: A plain-text view: one item per line as `Title | Detail | Tag`, with `# Group` headings sorting lines into buckets for grouped types.
Derive from text: Paste any text and the assist extracts the structure: short parallel titles with one-line descriptions, in the language of your text. With no AI provider configured a local parser splits bullets, lines or sentences instead.

sections.title: Style, colors and connectors
sections.text:
Thirteen style presets with live thumbnails, palette modes, brand kits and per-connector control.
Preset thumbnails render with your real content, so the gallery shows what the diagram will actually look like.
Style presets: Soft cards, Flat, Outline, Gradient, Sticker, Pastel, Bold, Duotone, Mono, Minimal, Glass, Dark and Blueprint; a click restyles every node.
Shuffle designs: Rolls a deterministic random combination of preset, palette, connector style and corner radius.
Palette: Mixed (a hue wheel), Accent (one color), Mono (tints of one hue) or Dark; the base color feeds the wheel and tints.
Brand kit: With more than one kit a dropdown picks which kit's colors drive the palette; Use brand colors switches the palette to it.
Connectors: Global connector look (arrow, line, dashed, none) and route (straight, elbow, curved). Connectors attach to the nodes and re-route live when boxes are dragged.
Per-connector menu: Click a connector in the preview to restyle just that one: route, arrowheads on either end, dashed, hidden, or reset to the global style.
Numbering, corners, density: Number badges on or off, corner radius, and a compact / cozy / airy density that scales spacing.

sections.title: Typography and background
sections.text:
The editor's full font catalog, size and weight control, and a transparent, colored or preset background.
Font: Any family the editor offers (brand, custom, system, editor, Google), previewed in its own face.
Title / body size and weight: Separate size sliders and weights for item titles and descriptions, plus a text alignment override.
Background: Auto follows the preset (dark presets bring their panel), None keeps the diagram transparent for any design, Color adds a picked panel.
Show document: Previews the diagram over your current design instead of a neutral stage, so colors and contrast are judged in context.

sections.title: Preview interactions and insert
sections.text:
Drag boxes, edit labels in place, and insert everything as editable layers.
Drag a box: Every node can be nudged from its automatic position; connectors follow and re-aim live. Reset placement returns to the pure layout.
Click a label: Opens an in-place editor over the preview for that title or description.
Insert / Update diagram: Inserts a named group of real shape and text layers laid out for the document format; when editing, the group updates in place inside its current box.

sections.title: Living Photos (overview and preview)
sections.text:
Turns a still photo into a living picture with a real 3D depth mesh, relighting, looping camera moves and depth aware effects.
Bring a photo to life. Living Photos builds a real 3D depth mesh from any picture, with depth estimated locally in your browser so nothing leaves your site, and turns it into a living image with cinematic camera moves: push-in, drift, sway, vertigo, breathe and orbit, all as perfect loops.
Relight the scene physically with a draggable key light and extra light points, each with its own color and strength, soften the shadows, or start from mood presets from golden hour to neon, moonlight and campfire. Depth-aware atmosphere falls into place behind and in front of your subject: falling snow, drifting fog, glowing embers, floating bokeh.
Open it from the **Extensions** menu. Export a still as an editable layer, or record the animation as a seamless WebM loop straight into your media library.
Living Photos: Opens the studio dialog. Choose it from the Generators menu to create a new effect, or use `Edit` on a layer that was made with it to re-open the same effect with its saved settings.
Source: Picks what the effect is built from. Changing the source reloads the preview and, for the depth modes, recomputes the depth map.
Active layer: Uses only the currently selected image, raster or smart layer as the photo. Best when you want the effect on one subject rather than the full canvas.
Whole document: Flattens the entire document to one photo, then builds depth from that. Use it when the whole composition should come to life.
Effects only (overlay): Skips depth and relighting entirely. Effects (flares, particles, rays, light washes) render on a transparent layer over your document, so you can drop atmosphere onto any artwork.
Depth model requirement: The depth mesh needs the local **Depth Anything** model. If it is missing, the depth sources are blocked with a notice and only the overlay mode stays usable.
Zoom out: Shrinks the preview by one step so you can see the whole frame. Does not change the exported result, only the on-screen size.
Zoom in: Enlarges the preview by one step to inspect fine detail. Preview only, not part of the export.
Fit: Resets the preview zoom to 100 percent so the frame fits the view again.
Drag to move the light: Drag inside the preview to reposition the key light. The light, its shadows and any lens flare follow the pointer.

sections.title: Camera
sections.text:
Sets the looping camera move and how far and how long it travels.
The camera path always loops seamlessly (the last frame matches the first). Pick a move, then dial its strength and length.
Move: Chooses the looping camera motion applied to the 3D scene.
Still: No camera motion. The frame holds steady while depth, light and particles still animate.
Push-in: Eases the camera toward the scene and back out again, a gentle dolly in and out.
Drift: A soft side to side glide with a small vertical bob. This is the default, subtle parallax.
Orbit sway: Swings left and right while turning to keep looking at the subject, like a small handheld arc.
Vertigo: The dolly zoom effect: pushes in while widening the lens so the background seems to warp.
Breathe: A very small in and out pulse. Adds quiet life without any obvious movement.
Orbit: A full elliptical camera path that circles around the subject.
Amount: How strong the camera move is. Higher values travel further and give more parallax.
Duration: The length of one loop in seconds. Longer is slower and calmer, shorter is more energetic.

sections.title: Depth
sections.text:
Shapes the 3D relief built from the depth map: how far it pops, how the subject separates and where focus sits.
These dials shape the depth mesh. Contrast and Smoothing rebuild the mesh shortly after you stop dragging, so a brief pause is normal.
3D depth: How far the photo pushes out into 3D. Higher values give stronger parallax and pop, lower keeps it flat.
Contrast: Separates the subject from the background by stretching the depth range through an S-curve. Raise it when foreground and background feel stuck together.
Smoothing: Softens depth edges so text and gradients do not turn into staircase steps. Higher smooths more but reduces sharp pop-out.
Focus: Sets the focus plane from far (0) to near (100). The camera pivots around it and the depth of field blur focuses on it.

sections.title: Light and relight
sections.text:
Relights the photo with a movable key light: mood presets, color, intensity, a screen-space wash and projected light patterns.
Relight replaces the photo's original lighting with a physical key light you can drag in the preview. Mood presets set color, intensity and position in one click; the sliders fine tune from there.
The light pattern (gobo) casts a shape, like window light or leaf shadows, over the whole frame.
Mood: A one-click lighting preset. Picking one sets the relight amount, key color, intensity and light position (and sometimes a flicker or hue animation).
Original: No relighting. Keeps the photo exactly as shot.
Golden hour: A warm low sun coming from the right, soft and cinematic.
Portrait: A classic two-point portrait setup: a warm key light from the upper right plus a cool shadowless rim light point on the lower left. A ready-made start for the Light points feature.
Neon: A purple key from the upper left for a moody club feel.
Flashlight: A bright neutral beam from the front center, like a torch pointed at the subject.
Moonlight: A cool blue key from high on the left, a calm night look.
Sunset: A warm orange key low in the frame with a violet counter-fill.
Cyberpunk: A magenta key balanced by a cyan fill, high-tech and saturated.
Campfire: A warm orange key from below that flickers over the loop, like firelight.
Studio: A clean bright key from the upper right, an even product-shot light.
Noir: A hard near-white key with a near-black fill for dramatic high-contrast shadows.
Party: A red key that cycles its hue across the loop, a shifting disco light.
Thunderstorm: A cool key from the top with lightning flashes fired once per loop.
Relight: How much the key light takes over from the original photo lighting. At 0 the photo is untouched, at 100 it is fully re-lit.
Color: The color of the key light. Opens the color picker; a mood preset also sets this.
Intensity: The brightness of the key light. Above 100 percent it burns brighter than neutral, below it stays soft.
Blend mode: Adds a screen-space color wash riding on the key light. Chooses how that wash mixes with the frame.
Blend amount: Strength of the light-wash overlay set by the blend mode above.
Light pattern: Projects a shaped light pattern (a gobo) across the frame, as if light passed through it.
Intensity (light pattern): How strong the projected light pattern is against the base lighting.
Pattern size: Scales the light pattern up or down, changing how large the window panes or leaf gaps read.
Soft shadows: Smooths the shadows the key light throws across the 3D relief: higher values widen the shadow edge into a real penumbra, lift the shadow core and suppress terrace artifacts at depth cliffs. 0% keeps the original hard look.
Light points: Up to four extra light points besides the key light, each with its own color and strength (10-200%). Add one, then drag it directly on the preview or use the target button to place it with a click. They follow the master Relight amount and never cast shadows - use them for rim, accent and fill light, portrait-relight style.

sections.title: Lens flare
sections.text:
Adds a lens flare anchored to the key light, with a choice of styles, rotation, size and blend.
The flare sits on the key light and moves with it. Different types give very different looks, from a full sun with ghosts to a single anamorphic streak.
Type: Chooses the lens flare style, or turns it off.
Sun: A bright central core with a soft halo and a trail of lens ghosts.
Anamorphic streak: A single wide horizontal blue streak plus a core, the classic widescreen flare.
Cinematic: A streak, core, halo and ghosts combined for a full movie-lens flare.
Starburst: A many-spiked star burst, like a bright point through a small aperture.
Rainbow ring: A wide circular spectral ring of rainbow color.
Anamorphic (cine): Strong blue horizontal streaks stacked for a heavy anamorphic look.
Ghosts: A chain of polygon lens ghosts marching across the frame, without a big core.
Vintage: Warm amber ghosts for an older, golden lens feel.
Glow: A soft wide bloom around the light with no hard flare elements.
Sparkle: Crossed twinkle bursts, a glinting highlight.
Rotation: Rotates the flare. Only shown for flare types that can rotate (streak, cinematic, starburst, rainbow ring, sparkle).
Size: Scales the whole flare up or down.
Blend mode (flare): How the flare mixes into the frame. Additive glows brightest, Normal is the most contained.

sections.title: Look (color grade and finish)
sections.text:
Cinematic finishing: a color-grade preset plus bloom, depth of field, rack focus, film grain and vignette.
The Look preset sets an overall color grade (split tone, saturation, contrast). The sliders below add finishing effects on top.
Look: A color-grade preset applied as a finishing pass.
None: No color grading, colors stay neutral.
Cinematic: Teal shadows and warm highlights with a little more saturation and contrast, a film-style grade.
Warm: Pushes the whole image warmer toward orange.
Cool: Pushes the whole image cooler toward blue.
Vintage: A faded, desaturated warm look with softer contrast.
Black & white: Removes all color and adds a touch of contrast for a monochrome result.
Dreamy: A soft, slightly magenta grade with lowered contrast.
Glow: Adds a bloom that spreads light out of bright areas for a glowing finish.
Depth of field: Blurs the parts of the scene away from the focus plane, like a shallow lens. Uses the Focus dial to decide what stays sharp.
Rack focus: Rides the focus plane from near to far and back across the loop, a moving focus pull.
Film grain: Adds fine loop-safe grain for an analog texture.
Vignette: Darkens the corners to draw the eye to the center.

sections.title: Glitch and retro
sections.text:
A retro and glitch pass: analog film wear, digital glitch, scanlines, color fringing, heat warp and a light zoom.
Analog film: Adds projector gate weave, scratches, dust and flicker for an old-film feel.
Glitch: Displaces horizontal slices of the image at random, a digital signal glitch that reseeds through the loop.
Scanlines: Overlays fine horizontal scan lines like an old CRT screen.
Color fringe: Splits the red and blue channels toward the edges, chromatic aberration like a cheap lens.
Warp: A heat-haze ripple that wobbles the image with a loop-safe sine field.
Light zoom: Streaks a radial blur outward from the key light, a zoom-burst of light.

sections.title: Effects (atmosphere and particles)
sections.text:
Depth-aware atmosphere: god rays, bokeh, ten particle systems, fog, light rays, light leaks and global particle controls.
Particles are placed in 3D through the depth so they weave in front of and behind the subject. Each slider sets the density of one system; the Size, Speed and Wind dials affect them all.
Sun rays: God rays that pour warm light from bright areas toward the light, blocked by darker shapes.
Bokeh lights: Soft glowing out-of-focus light discs as a post effect. Distinct from the Bokeh particle system below.
Snow: Falling snowflakes drifting through the depth of the scene.
Embers: Glowing orange sparks rising and twinkling, like from a fire.
Bokeh: Large soft golden light orbs floating in front of the scene, an in-scene bokeh particle system.
Dust: Tiny drifting dust motes catching the light.
Rain: Falling rain streaks slanted by the wind.
Leaves: Autumn leaves tumbling and spinning as they fall.
Petals: Soft flower petals drifting down.
Fireflies: Glowing green-yellow fireflies wandering and blinking.
Bubbles: Translucent soap bubbles rising through the frame.
Meteors: Bright meteors streaking across with long tails.
Fog: Soft translucent fog layered through the depth, hazing the background.
Light rays: Drifting volumetric light rays fanning out from the key light in screen space.
Light leaks: Colored light leaks that drift across the frame like film edge fogging.
Size: Global scale for all particles at once. Above 100 makes them bigger, below smaller.
Speed: Global speed for all particle motion.
Wind: Sideways wind pushing all particles. Negative blows left, positive blows right.

sections.title: Weather
sections.text:
Lens-level weather: raindrops on the glass and lightning flashes.
Rain drops: Adds raindrops that sit on the lens and refract the image, growing and sliding once per loop.
Lightning: Fires a bright double lightning flash once per loop, weighted toward the sky.

sections.title: Motion (flow animation)
sections.text:
Paints a flow field so parts of the photo drift like water or smoke, with pinned still areas.
Draw arrows in the preview to say where pixels should flow, and drop anchors where things should stay still. The flow loops seamlessly.
Arrows: Turns on arrow drawing. Drag in the preview to add a flow arrow pointing where that area should move. The button reads **Done** while active; click it again to stop drawing.
Anchors: Turns on anchor placing. Click in the preview to pin an area so it stays still against the surrounding flow. Reads **Done** while active.
Clear: Removes all flow arrows and anchors at once, resetting the flow field.
Speed: How fast the flow animation moves along the arrows.

sections.title: Export and insert
sections.text:
Insert a still layer, record the loop as WebM, or export an interactive HTML snippet, plus the dialog's insert and cancel actions.
The still bakes the neutral pose (no camera offset) so the frame shows the whole document. The loop records the live preview as a seamless WebM. The interactive HTML export uploads the photo and depth map and gives you a self-contained parallax snippet for any HTML widget.
Video size: Output width for the recorded WebM loop.
Record WebM to Media Library: Records one seamless loop and uploads it into the media library. Chrome, Edge and Firefox record WebM; Safari records MP4, and the file is named accordingly. A browser whose recorder can do neither says so instead of starting.
Download WebM: Records one seamless loop and downloads it as a video file instead of uploading it: WebM in Chrome, Edge and Firefox, MP4 in Safari.
Interactive HTML (Elementor): Uploads the photo and its depth map, then builds a self-contained interactive parallax snippet you can paste into any HTML widget. Needs a photo with depth, so it is off in overlay mode.
Copy code: Copies the generated HTML snippet to the clipboard. Appears after the snippet is built.
Download HTML: Saves the generated snippet as a `living-photo.html` file. Appears after the snippet is built.
Insert still / Update FX: The primary button. On a new effect it inserts a still frame as an editable layer named `FX still` (or `FX overlay` in overlay mode); when editing it updates the existing layer in place and re-saves the settings.
Cancel: Closes the studio without inserting or changing any layer. The Escape key and clicking the dark backdrop do the same.

sections.title: Generative Art (overview and playground)
sections.text:
Programmed vector artwork you shape by turning dials, not drawing: 24 motif generators, curated palettes and a live playground preview.
Programmed beauty: you do not draw, you set the dials. Two dozen motif generators, from rings with rhythmic widths, wave lines and color waves to guilloché rosettes, spirals, truchet mosaics, sunbursts and phyllotaxis, create abstract vector artworks from a seed dice, and every roll is reproducible.
Bend the result with a deformer stack of wave, twirl, bulge and shear, and color it from curated palettes or your brand kit.
Open it from the **Extensions** menu. Insert the artwork as an editable overlay layer, record an animated variant as a WebM loop, or export a true vector SVG.
Generative Art: Opens the studio dialog. Choose it from the Generators menu for new artwork, or use `Edit` on a layer it created to re-open the exact artwork with its saved seed and dials.
Show document behind the artwork: A checkbox that toggles a preview of your current document behind the artwork, so you can judge how the piece sits over your design. Preview only, it is not baked into the layer.
Drag to warp: Drag on the preview to pull the artwork toward the pointer, adding a soft warp point. The studio keeps the six most recent pulls.
Shift-drag to orbit / steer: Hold Shift and drag to orbit the 3D motifs or steer the direction and amplitude of flat ones. For 3D motifs the Shift requirement is inverted, so a plain drag orbits them.
Wheel to zoom: Scroll the mouse wheel over the preview to scale the artwork up or down (the Size dial).
Double-click for new colors: Double-click the preview to roll a new palette, hue shift and order on the same artwork, keeping the shapes.
Right-click menu: Right-click the preview for a small playground menu: Add generator, New colors, Clear warp and Reset zoom.

sections.title: Presets, surprises and favorites
sections.text:
A gallery of designed starting points, fresh random rolls, and your saved favorites.
Each preset tile is a real rendered artwork, not a thumbnail. Click one to load it, then let the dials and dice take over. The four surprise tiles are rolled fresh every time you open the dialog.
Preset tiles: Sixteen curated starting-point artworks. Clicking a tile loads its motif, palette, seed and dials so you can tweak from a designed base.
Surprise tiles: Four freshly rolled random artworks (labelled ? 1 to ? 4), regenerated each time the dialog opens. What you see on the tile is exactly what loads when you click it.
Save as favorite: Saves the current artwork (its full settings) as a favorite tile. Favorites are saved with your WordPress account and rendered like presets.
Favorite tiles: Your saved artworks, shown as clickable tiles. Each has an x in its corner to delete it.

sections.title: Motif (generators)
sections.text:
The core generator: choose one of 24 motifs, set the seed, and roll the dice.
The motif decides what kind of shapes are drawn. Each motif exposes its own set of dials (documented in Motif dials). Circle-based motifs stay circular on non-square documents.
The seed drives the deterministic randomness, so the same seed and dials always reproduce the same artwork.
Motif: Chooses which generator draws the artwork. Changing it swaps in that motif's own dials.
Rings: Concentric circles, or broken arcs, with thickness following a rhythmic pattern.
Wave lines: Horizontal sine lines stacked down the frame, strongest in the middle.
Color waves: Filled, overlapping wave bands rising from the bottom edge.
Grid: A mesh of horizontal and vertical lines that bends under the deformers.
Shape pattern: A grid of circles, squares or triangles with smooth size and rotation gradients.
Guilloché: Nested rosette curves, the fine engraved look of banknotes and stamps.
Spiral: Several evenly rotated archimedean spiral arms.
Mosaic: Truchet tiles: quarter-circle arcs whose seeded orientation connects into flowing loops.
Sunburst: Rays radiating from the center, lengths following a rhythmic bar.
Halftone: A dot grid where dot sizes follow a smooth field, like print halftone.
Particle waves: Fields of dots riding sine waves across the frame.
Particle cloud (3D): A rotating cloud of points arranged in 3D space.
Ribbon (3D): A flowing ribbon curve twisting through 3D space.
Lissajous (3D): A 3D Lissajous curve, a looping knot of harmonic motion.
Bloom: A phyllotaxis spiral of dots, the sunflower-seed pattern.
Circle stack: Translucent circles marching along a curved path and shrinking, a tunnel of offset circles.
Shape stack: Like Circle stack but with polygons, and with an added twist dial.
Letters: Your typed text spun into a rotating fan or spelled out around a ring.
Polyhedron (3D): Platonic solid wireframes (cube, octahedron, icosahedron) echoed into depth.
Orbits (3D): Overlapping circles on tilted axes around one center, like an armillary sphere.
Wire sphere (3D): A wireframe globe of meridians and parallels, tilted in space.
Terrain (3D): A wireframe landscape from a harmonic height field, seen from above.
Tunnel (3D): Concentric frames rushing into depth and twisting as they go.
Torus knot (3D): A torus-knot ribbon drawn as parallel strands.
Seed: The number that drives the artwork's randomness. The same seed with the same dials always makes the same art.
New seed: The dice button next to the seed. Rolls a new random seed, keeping every other dial the same, for a fresh variation of the current look.
Randomize everything: Rolls a fully new curated artwork: motif, palette, colors, blends and dials all change at once, but only along combinations that stay beautiful.
Text: The text to draw, shown only for the Letters motif. Up to 24 characters.

sections.title: Motif dials
sections.text:
The per-motif parameter sliders. Which ones appear depends on the selected motif.
Every motif shows its own small set of these dials. The ranges below are the values the sliders use; a few labels share an underlying parameter but are named for what they do in that motif.
Count: How many elements the motif draws (rings, lines, dots, arms, and so on). More elements means denser artwork.
Gap: The spacing between rings, the empty space between each band.
Offset: Shifts ring centers along a direction (Rings) or the frame offset of a tunnel, for an off-center feel.
Arcs: Breaks rings into arcs with gaps. At 0 the rings stay whole; higher opens bigger gaps.
Amplitude: How tall the waves are. Bigger amplitude gives deeper crests and troughs.
Phase: Shifts each successive line's wave along, spreading or aligning the crests.
Weight: The stroke thickness of the lines or curves.
Size: The size of each element (shapes, dots or stacked forms).
Rotation: Rotates each shape by an amount that grows across the size gradient, in the Shape pattern motif.
Wobble: How much the rosette curves wobble in and out, the liveliness of the engraved lines.
Turns: How many times each spiral arm winds around the center.
Inner radius: How far the sunburst rays start from the center, leaving a clear middle.
Spread: How widely the orbit rings fan out across their axes.
View angle: Turns the 3D camera around the motif, changing the viewing angle.
Tilt: Tilts the wireframe globe forward or back.
Height: How tall the terrain peaks and valleys rise.
Twist: How much the tunnel frames rotate as they recede, or the twist added to a Shape stack.
Thickness: The band width of the torus knot ribbon.
Reach: How far the stacked shapes travel out along their path from the center.
Direction: The direction the stack or letter fan marches away from the center.
Shrink: How quickly each successive stacked shape (or letter copy) gets smaller.
Spin: How much the letters (or polyhedron echoes) rotate as they repeat.

sections.title: Colors
sections.text:
Palette, custom brand color, how colors walk the shapes, opacity, hue, order and the background fill.
Colors always stay inside a curated palette, so every roll stays harmonic. You can also feed a custom brand color, which is expanded into a five-stop palette, or pick a saved brand kit.
Palette: The color set for the artwork. Twelve curated palettes, plus a custom brand color option and any saved brand kits.
Northern Lights: Deep blues rising to pale teal and cream, an aurora feel.
Sunset: Purple through magenta and coral to warm yellow.
Bauhaus: Primary red, gold, teal and navy on cream, a classic Bauhaus set.
Ocean: Navy through blues to pale aqua.
Terracotta: Earthy browns, clay orange and warm sand.
Pastel: Soft blue, pink, yellow, green and lilac.
Neon Noir: Near-black with electric purple, pink, coral and mint.
Sage: Muted greens fading to soft off-white.
Ink: A grayscale ramp from near-black to pale gray.
Royal: Deep indigo and violet up to pink and gold.
Citrus: Dark green through lime and yellow-green to pale cream.
Rosé: Deep wine through rose pinks to blush.
Custom (brand color): Builds a five-stop harmonic palette from a single brand color you choose, so the artwork matches your brand.
Base color: The brand color the custom palette is built from. Shown only when Palette is set to Custom.
Brand kit palettes [Pro]: Any saved brand kits (Pro) appear in the palette list with a star. Choosing one copies its colors into the artwork so it stays reproducible even if the kit later changes.
Color chips: A read-only row of swatches showing the current palette's colors after any hue shift and order changes.
Mode: How colors are assigned across the elements as the motif steps through them.
Cycle: Steps through the palette colors one by one and repeats, so neighbors differ.
Gradient: Blends smoothly through the palette from first color to last across all elements.
Contrast: Alternates between the palette's darkest and lightest color for a high-contrast look.
Duo: Alternates between just two mid-palette colors, a clean two-tone.
Opacity: The overall transparency of the shapes. Lower values let overlaps blend and show through.
Hue shift: Rotates every palette color around the color wheel, recoloring the whole set at once.
Order: Whether the palette runs dark to light or light to dark, flipping which end leads.
Background: The fill behind the artwork. Transparent leaves it clear; the others use the palette's dark or light color, flat or as a gradient.

sections.title: Deform
sections.text:
A stack of up to three deformers that bend the artwork, each with a strength and frequency.
The three deformer slots apply in order, each bending the points before the next. Every deformer is off at strength 0 and uses whole-number frequencies so the bends stay rhythmic, never noisy.
Deformer slot (1, 2, 3): Each of the three numbered rows picks one deformer to apply. Leave a slot on None to skip it.
None: No deformation for this slot, the artwork passes through unchanged.
Wave: A horizontal sine wave that pushes points up and down.
Wave (vertical): A vertical sine wave that pushes points left and right.
Twirl: Rotates points around the center, more near the middle, for a spiral swirl.
Pinch / bulge: Pushes points toward or away from the center, pinching the middle or bulging it out.
Shear: Slants the artwork, sliding the top and bottom in opposite directions.
Ripple: Concentric ripples radiating from the center, like a drop in water.
Squeeze: Narrows the artwork horizontally in a band based on vertical position, a soft waist.
Strength: How strongly this deformer bends the artwork. At 0 it does nothing.
Frequency: How many waves or repeats the deformer uses. Whole numbers keep the bend rhythmic.

sections.title: Effects
sections.text:
Blend mode, glow, star dust sparkle and line style for the whole artwork.
Blend mode: How overlapping shapes mix. Screen and Additive fuse overlaps into brighter new colors, Multiply darkens them.
Normal: Standard drawing, later shapes cover earlier ones by their opacity.
Screen: Lightens where shapes overlap, glowing new colors on a dark ground.
Additive: Adds colors together, the brightest fusing of overlaps.
Multiply: Darkens overlaps, works best on a light background.
Glow: Adds a soft glow around the shapes, strongest with a dark background and additive blends.
Star dust: Scatters tiny sparkle particles across the artwork.
Line style: How open (stroked) lines are drawn.

sections.title: Combine
sections.text:
Fuse up to three extra generators into the artwork, each with its own motif, blend and size.
Beyond the main motif you can stack up to three more generators. Each fuses in with its own blend mode, and screen or additive blends make the overlaps create new colors.
Extra generator row: Each numbered row adds one more motif on top of the artwork. Its x button removes that generator.
Second motif: Picks which motif the extra generator draws. Any of the 24 motifs can be layered in.
Blend mode (combine): How this extra generator mixes with the layers below it.
Size (combine): Scales this extra generator relative to the main artwork.
Add generator: Adds another extra generator with a random complementary motif and blend. Also available from the preview's right-click menu.

sections.title: Layout
sections.text:
Kaleidoscope mirroring, overall size and rotation of the whole artwork.
Kaleidoscope: Mirrors the artwork into symmetric wedges for a kaleidoscope pattern. Off leaves it as one piece.
Size: Scales the whole artwork within the frame. The mouse wheel over the preview changes this too.
Rotation: Rotates the entire artwork around its center.

sections.title: Animation
sections.text:
Play a seamless loop of the artwork and record it as a WebM video.
The animation loops seamlessly, the last frame matching the first. Play previews it live; the record buttons capture it as a WebM at the document's aspect ratio.
Play loop: Starts and stops a live animated preview of the artwork looping. The button toggles between play and pause.
Duration: The length of one animation loop in seconds.
Record WebM to Media Library: Records one seamless loop and uploads it into the media library. Chrome, Edge and Firefox record WebM; Safari records MP4, and the file is named accordingly. A browser whose recorder can do neither says so instead of starting.
Download WebM: Records one seamless loop and downloads it as a video file instead of uploading it: WebM in Chrome, Edge and Firefox, MP4 in Safari.

sections.title: Export and insert
sections.text:
Export true vector SVG, and the dialog's insert and cancel actions.
The artwork is real vector geometry, so the SVG export is identical to the inserted layer. Inserting adds it as a full-size editable layer that re-opens with its exact seed.
Download SVG: Saves the artwork as a true vector SVG file, with paths identical to the inserted layer.
Save SVG to Media Library: Uploads the vector SVG into the WordPress media library. If the server blocks SVG uploads, it suggests using the download instead.
Insert artwork / Update artwork: The primary button. On new artwork it inserts a full-size editable layer named `Artwork` with the seed; when editing it updates the existing layer in place and re-saves the seed and dials.
Cancel: Closes the studio without inserting or changing any layer. Escape and clicking the dark backdrop do the same.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
A short brief becomes a whole set of on-brand ad banners, copy first, images second, all in one dialog.
Turn a short brief into a whole set of on-brand ad banners. Pick a brand kit with logo, colors, fonts and industry, or define your own reference image and colors, then describe the audience, the goal, the offer and the key message. You can also build ads straight from a post, page or WooCommerce product: its image becomes the reference and its text feeds the copy.
The editor's text AI writes a copy concept per banner that you can edit before anything is rendered, then the image AI generates several banners at once in the formats you choose, from square and portrait to story and widescreen. A scannable QR code can be composited into every banner.
Open it from the **Extensions** menu. Send each result to the media library, download it, drop it onto the canvas, or regenerate it, all inside one dialog. It uses your configured AI provider, exactly like the AI Studio panel.

sections.title: Ad Banners dialog
sections.text:
The main modal that turns a short brief plus your brand into a whole set of AI ad banners.
Ad Banners opens from the editor's **Extensions** menu and fills one modal split into two panes: the brief on the left, a live **Batch queue** (copy first, then the finished banners) on the right.
It works in three moves: fill in the brief, write the copy with the text AI, then generate the banner images with the image AI. The brand logo (or a picked post image) rides along as a visual reference so the ads stay on brand.
Ad Banners…: Opens Ad Banners. It is added to the editor's **Extensions** menu and sits at the top of that menu.
Design a whole set of on-brand ad banners with AI.: The subtitle shown under the dialog title. It is a description, not a control.
Batch queue: Heading of the right pane. It holds the live queue: your editable copy concepts first, then the banner images as they finish rendering.
Close: The X in the top-right corner closes the dialog. It is blocked while copy or banners are still generating so a job is not lost.
Backdrop click: Clicking the dimmed area outside the dialog closes it, the same as Close. It is ignored while a job is running.

sections.title: Quick start (campaign presets)
sections.text:
One-click starting points that prefill the brief, formats, image style and copy tone.
The **Quick start** card sits at the top of the left pane. Each preset drops a ready-made campaign into the brief: it fills the goal, offer and key message, sets the banner formats, picks a visual style and a copy tone.
Presets are a starting point, not a lock: everything they set stays editable afterwards. They do not touch the audience field or the brand you picked.
Sale / Discount: A high-energy discount campaign. Prefills a discount offer and an urgent call to action.
Product launch: Announces a brand-new product with a clean hero look and confident wording.
Event / Webinar: Drives signups for an event or webinar with a friendly, date-and-time-friendly poster layout.
Black Friday: A premium Black Friday sale set with a dark, gold-accented look and urgent copy.
New arrival: Showcases a new item in the range with a fresh, editorial product shot and very few words.
Newsletter: Grows newsletter signups with a warm, inviting look and a welcome-offer angle.
Holiday / Season: A seasonal campaign with a warm festive scene and emotional wording.
App download: Pushes app downloads with a sleek device mockup and a bold call to action.

sections.title: Basis (what the ad is based on)
sections.text:
Choose whether the banners come from your brief alone or from picked posts, pages or products.
The **Basis** card decides the source of each ad. `Free topic` builds only from the brief you type. `From content` pulls one or more posts, pages or products: each item's featured or product image becomes the visual reference and its text feeds the copy.
Picking several items runs a batch: one banner set per item. A live counter warns you if the total (items times formats) grows too large.
Free topic: Builds the banners from your typed brief only, with no post or product attached. This is the default.
From content: Bases each banner on a chosen post, page or WooCommerce product. The item's image becomes the reference and its text feeds the copy.
Choose posts, pages or products…: Opens the content picker so you can select the items to build banners from. Shown when no items are picked yet.
Add / change items: Reopens the content picker to add more items or swap the current selection. Shown once at least one item is picked.
Picked item row: Each selected post, page or product shows as a row with its thumbnail, title and type. If the item has no image, the row is tagged `no image` and the banner falls back to the brand logo as reference.
Remove (picked item): The small X on a picked item row removes just that item from the batch.

sections.title: Content picker
sections.text:
A pop-over dialog to search and multi-select the posts, pages or products a batch is built from.
Opened from **Basis** when you choose `From content`. Pick a content type, search, then tap tiles to select several items at once. Your selection is kept as you switch type or search.
On confirm it loads each item's full context (title, text, image, link, and WooCommerce price for products) and returns to the brief. The first item's text can prefill the offer field, and its link can prefill the QR target.
Choose content: The picker dialog title. Its subtitle explains that the item's image becomes the reference and its text feeds the copy.
Type dropdown: Selects which content type to browse. It lists the post types the site exposes; if none are reported it falls back to Posts and Pages.
Search…: A search box that filters the current type by title. It waits about 300 ms after you stop typing before reloading the grid.
Result tile: Each result shows as a tile with a thumbnail (or a placeholder icon) and title. Tap to select or deselect; selected tiles show a check mark and stay selected across type and search changes.
Use selection: Confirms the picked items and returns to the brief. The button shows the count in brackets and is disabled until at least one item is selected.
Cancel: Closes the picker without changing the current selection.

sections.title: Brand
sections.text:
Pick a saved brand kit or define your own colors and reference logo for the ads.
The **Brand** column (left half of the Brand & AI card) sets the look the banners follow. If you have saved brand kits, a dropdown lets you pick one or choose `Custom`. A kit shows its logo and color swatches.
With `Custom` (or when you have no kits) you supply your own reference image and up to six colors. The brand colors and logo are handed to both the copy writer and the image generator.
Brand kit dropdown: Selects which saved brand kit the banners follow. Shown only when at least one kit exists. Picking a kit resets the logo toggle to on if that kit has a logo. [Shown when: Brand kits exist]
Custom: The last option in the brand dropdown. It drops the saved kits and lets you define colors and a reference image by hand.
Use the logo as a visual reference: When a picked kit has a logo, this checkbox decides whether that logo is attached to the image AI as a reference so it appears in the banner. On by default when the kit has a logo.
Reference image / logo: In Custom mode, the image handed to the AI as the brand reference. It shows a thumbnail once set, or a placeholder icon when empty.
Upload: Opens a file picker to upload an image from your device as the reference logo. Accepts any image file.
From media library: Picks the reference image from the WordPress media library. Shown only where the media library is available.
Remove: Clears the current custom reference image so no logo is attached.
Colors: The list of custom brand colors the banners are built around. Each color is a swatch you can recolor or delete.
Color (swatch): A single brand color. Click it to open the editor's color picker and change the value; the swatch updates to the picked color.
Add color: Adds another color swatch to the custom brand palette, up to six. New swatches start at the editor blue.
Remove color: The X on a color chip deletes that color from the palette.

sections.title: Image AI and visual style
sections.text:
Choose the image provider and an optional visual style for the generated banners.
The AI column (right half of the Brand & AI card) sets which image provider renders the banners and, optionally, the visual style prompt.
If no provider is configured, a warning appears with a link to open settings, and the Create copy button stays disabled.
Image AI: Provider pills that pick which configured image AI renders the banners. The active pill is highlighted; the editor's default provider is preselected when available.
No AI provider configured.: A warning shown when no image provider is set up. Banners cannot be generated until one is configured.
Open settings: A link next to the no-provider warning that opens the editor settings in a new tab so you can add a provider.
Visual style: An optional style prompt for the look of the banners (for example a preset chosen from the editor's style button). It is added to the image prompt for every banner.
Click here to select a style: The placeholder text inside the style box when no style is chosen. Clicking the box opens the editor's style menu.
Clear style: The X on the style tag removes the chosen visual style so banners generate without a style prompt.

sections.title: Campaign brief and copy style
sections.text:
The four brief fields and the copy tone that steer the AI-written ad copy.
The **Campaign** card holds the brief. Two fields per row: audience and goal, then offer and key message. These feed the copy writer and (offer, key message) the image prompt.
Below them, the **Copy style** chips pick a tone of voice for the wording. Only one tone can be active; tap it again to clear it.
Target audience: Who the campaign is aimed at. Guides the copy so it speaks to the right reader.
Campaign goal: What the campaign should achieve. Points the copy at the right outcome (signups, sales, downloads).
Offer / product details: The concrete offer or product facts (discount, deadline, what is included). A multi-line field; it feeds both the copy and the banner image prompt.
Key message: The single idea the ad should leave behind. A multi-line field that anchors the headline and the image.
Copy style: A row of tone chips that set the voice of the AI-written copy. Choose one; tapping the active chip again turns the tone off.
Playful: Copy tone: playful and light, with a wink.
Serious: Copy tone: serious, factual and trustworthy.
Urgent: Copy tone: urgent and scarcity-driven, with a strong call to action.
Luxury: Copy tone: elegant, premium and exclusive.
Minimal: Copy tone: minimal and clear, very few words.
Storytelling: Copy tone: narrative and vivid, emotionally engaging.
Bold: Copy tone: bold, confident and punchy.
Friendly: Copy tone: warm, friendly and personal.
Witty: Copy tone: witty and humorous, with a clever twist.
Benefit-led: Copy tone: benefit-led, concrete customer value.
Emotional: Copy tone: emotional and inspiring.
Premium-short: Copy tone: a few premium words, understated.

sections.title: Banner set (formats and QR)
sections.text:
Choose up to five banner formats and, optionally, add a scannable QR code.
The **Banner set** card lists the formats you want, one tile per banner, up to five. Each tile shows a shape preview and a format dropdown. The card heading shows the current count.
A counter note reports how many banners the set will produce (items times formats) and warns when that exceeds the batch cap. At the bottom, an optional QR code can be composited into every banner after it renders.
Banner slot tile: One banner in the set. Shows a preview of the chosen aspect and a dropdown to change its format. Add up to five.
Format dropdown: Per-tile menu that sets the aspect ratio of that banner. Options are the seven ad formats below.
Add banner: Adds another banner slot to the set. Hidden once five slots exist.
Remove banner: The X on a tile removes that banner from the set. Disabled when only one slot is left.
1:1 (Square): Square banner for a feed or post.
4:3 (Landscape): Landscape banner for display or web placements.
3:4 (Portrait): Portrait banner for a flyer or pin.
3:2 (Photo wide): Wide photo-ratio banner for display.
2:3 (Photo tall): Tall photo-ratio banner for a pin or print.
16:9 (Wide): Wide banner for a leaderboard or cover.
9:16 (Story): Tall banner for a story or reel.
Count note: A line under the tiles showing how many banners the set produces. In a batch it reads `items times formats = total`; it turns to a warning when the total passes the cap.
Add a scannable QR code: A checkbox that composites a working QR code into the bottom-right corner of every banner after it is generated.
QR target URL: The web address the QR code points to. Shown once the QR checkbox is on. Prefills from the picked item's link or the brand website when available.

sections.title: Copy concepts (batch queue)
sections.text:
The editable copy the text AI writes, one concept per banner, before you render images.
After **Create copy**, the right pane fills with one editable concept per banner: a title, a headline and body copy. In a multi-item batch the concepts are grouped under each item's name.
Edit the wording freely, or reroll a single concept to get a fresh take. When happy, generate the banner set; each image uses the current copy, including your edits.
Concept title: The name of a copy concept, taken from the AI response or numbered as a fallback. It labels each editable block.
Format badge: A small tag on the concept header showing which banner format this copy is tied to (for example 16:9).
Reroll this copy: Rewrites just this one concept with the text AI, keeping its format and group. Disabled while another job runs.
Headline: The main line of the ad, rendered prominently on the banner. Editable; the strongest line from the AI lockup is used by default.
Copy: The supporting body text (subline and optional call to action). Each line is rendered on the banner. Editable, three rows.
Group heading: In a multi-item batch, a heading that separates the concepts belonging to each picked post, page or product. [Shown when: More than one item]

sections.title: Banner results and per-banner actions
sections.text:
The finished banner images with save, download, canvas and regenerate actions on each.
Once you generate the set, each banner renders in the queue below the copy, grouped per item in a batch. Banners generate a few at a time so the provider is not overloaded.
Each finished banner has its own action row. While rendering it shows a spinner; on failure it shows an error with a Retry button.
Generating…: The loading state on a banner tile while the image AI renders it. A spinner with this label.
Generation failed: The error state shown when a banner could not be produced. It prints the provider error and offers Retry.
Retry: Re-runs generation for a single failed banner using its current copy. [Shown when: Banner errored]
To media library: Saves this banner as a new image in the WordPress media library. After saving it switches to `In library` and is disabled.
Download: Downloads this banner to your device as a PNG. The filename is built from the brand, concept and format.
Add as layer: Drops this banner onto the current editor canvas as a new image layer, centred and scaled to fit.
Regenerate: Renders this single banner again from scratch, picking up any copy edits you made.

sections.title: Footer and batch actions
sections.text:
The footer buttons that drive each step, plus the bulk actions once banners are ready.
The footer changes with the step. Before copy exists it offers Cancel and Create copy. With copy but no images it offers Reroll all copy and Generate banner set. Once images exist it offers Regenerate all and Done.
A batch bar appears above the queue as soon as at least one banner is finished, letting you act on all of them at once.
Create copy: Writes the copy concepts from your brief with the text AI. Disabled until an AI provider is configured. Shows `Writing copy…` while it runs. [Requires: AI provider]
Cancel: Closes the dialog. Shown in the footer before any copy has been written.
Reroll all copy: Rewrites every copy concept with a fresh pass of the text AI. Shown once copy exists but before banners are generated.
Generate banner set: Renders every banner in the set from the current copy. Moves the flow to the image step.
Regenerate all: Re-renders the whole set again. Disabled while any banner is still generating.
Done: Closes Ad Banners. Shown once the banners are generated.
All to media library: Saves every finished banner that is not already saved to the media library in one go, then reports the count.
All as ZIP: Downloads every finished banner as PNGs bundled in a single ZIP file, named after the brand.
All as layers: Drops every finished banner onto the editor canvas as image layers, each nudged so they do not stack exactly. Shown only with the editor bridge.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
One design, every platform size, without the crop: the layout re-arranges instead of being cut.
One design, every platform size, without the crop. Reformat re-lays-out your document for Instagram post, portrait and story, Pinterest, YouTube thumbnails, Facebook and OG, X and LinkedIn: backgrounds fill each frame while text, logos and content keep their position anchors, scale cleanly and respect each platform's safe zones, so stories keep clear of the username and caption UI.
A live preview grid shows every size at once, with an adjustable content scale for the layouts that need a nudge.
Open it from the **Extensions** menu. Download everything as one ZIP, or save every size straight to the media library.

sections.title: Reformat dialog
sections.text:
Re-lays out the current design into every platform size without cropping, previewed as a live grid.
Reformat (registered as an Extensions generator) takes the open document and rebuilds it at each target platform size. Backgrounds cover-fill the new frame, while text and logos keep their composition anchors, scale uniformly, and stay inside each platform's safe zone.
The dialog shows a live preview grid on the left and the controls on the right (Formats, Options, Export). It needs a document with at least one layer to open.
Reformat: Launches the Reformat tool. It is registered as a generator and appears in the editor's Extensions menu.
One design, re-laid-out for every platform.: The dialog subtitle. It describes the tool, it is not a control.
Preview grid: The left pane renders a live thumbnail of the design in every format. Previews redraw when you change the content scale or safe-zone option.
Close: The X in the header closes the dialog. Esc and clicking the backdrop also close it.
Cancel: The footer button that closes Reformat without exporting.

sections.title: Formats (target platforms)
sections.text:
The platform sizes to produce, each a toggle card, with All and None shortcuts.
The **Formats** card lists ten platform presets. Each is a card you tap to include or exclude; active cards are highlighted and every card shows its pixel dimensions.
Seven formats are on by default; the last three (LinkedIn Post, X Header, Facebook Cover) start off. Use All or None to flip the whole set at once. Each format carries a safe zone so content stays clear of platform UI.
All: Selects every platform format at once.
None: Clears the selection so no format is chosen. Export buttons disable until you pick at least one.
Instagram Post: Square Instagram feed post.
Instagram Portrait: Tall Instagram feed post.
Story / Reel: Full-screen vertical story or reel. Its safe zone keeps content clear of the username row on top and the caption/CTA block at the bottom.
Pinterest Pin: Standard Pinterest pin.
YouTube Thumbnail: Video thumbnail. The safe zone avoids the timestamp and progress bar along the bottom.
Facebook / OG Image: Facebook share and Open Graph link preview image.
X Post: In-timeline image for X (Twitter).
LinkedIn Post: LinkedIn feed image. Off by default; toggle it on if you need it.
X Header: X (Twitter) profile header banner. Off by default.
Facebook Cover: Facebook profile cover. Off by default. Its safe zone allows for the profile picture overlapping the lower left on desktop.

sections.title: Options
sections.text:
Content scale, safe-zone respect, output file type and the base file name.
The **Options** card tunes how the re-layout looks and how files come out. The content scale shrinks or grows the design's content inside each frame, the safe-zone toggle keeps content clear of platform UI, and the file type and name control the export.
Changing the scale or safe-zone option redraws the preview grid live.
Content scale: Uniformly scales the design's content (text, logos, foreground) within each target frame. Backgrounds still cover-fill; this only affects the anchored content. Lower to add breathing room, raise to fill more.
Respect platform safe zones: When on, content is clamped inside each platform's safe zone so it does not collide with story caption bars, the YouTube timestamp, a Facebook profile picture, and similar UI. Turn off to use the full frame edge to edge.
File type: The image format the reformatted files are saved as. JPEG flattens onto a white background at 90% quality; PNG keeps transparency.
File name: The base name for every exported file. It is slugified (lowercased, non-letters turned to dashes); each file appends its format id. Falls back to `design` if left blank.

sections.title: Export
sections.text:
Save every selected format to the media library or download them all as a ZIP.
The **Export** card and footer render each selected format at full size and hand them off. A status line reports progress (for example `Rendering formats… (2/6)`).
Both export buttons disable when no format is selected, and again while an export is in flight.
Save to Media Library: Renders every selected format at full size and uploads each to the WordPress media library. Each upload is titled with the base name plus the format label. Reports how many saved and how many failed.
